Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale
documents.raw_text: News Highlights:AMD Helion lets customers tailor CPU core density, performance and power to agentic workloads, with CPU-only configurations for hyperscale deployments and integrated CPU/GPU configurations for enterprises.AMD Helion combines open hardware and software with an integrated token router that directs agents’ model calls across frontier and open-source models.SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 – AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today introduced the AMD Helion agentic AI rack, an open blueprint for agentic AI infrastructure based on an Open Compute Project spec-design and powered by AMD compute.Building on the open-platform approach of the AMD Helios™ rackscale solution, AMD Helion is designed to provide partners and customers with the flexibility they need for agentic AI infrastructure. With AMD Helion, customers can match CPU performance, core density and power with GPU acceleration for the work their AI agents perform.“Agentic AI is not a single workload. It spans personal agents, enterprise applications, code execution and complex workflows, each with different compute requirements,” said Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD. “To do that takes optimized compute and infrastructure that can adapt to different workloads. With AMD Helion, we are bringing AMD EPYC™ performance, open software and flexible rack designs together so our partners can build systems around customer needs and make efficient use of available power.”AMD Helion’s OCP spec-based rack blueprint supports open software and can come in flexible configurations, including liquid- and air-cooled versions, allowing customers to create virtually any configuration needed for their needs. Some examples of this include:A CPU-only rack powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors that can support up to 32,768 CPU cores. This rack is designed for hyperscale customers, providing dedicated capacity for agent execution and connections to separate model inference infrastructure.An all-in-one rack that combines AMD EPYC CPU nodes, AMD Instinct™ MI350P GPU nodes and general-purpose compute on one platform. This rack is designed to provide partners and customers an all-in-one concept for enterprise agentic AI.AMD Helion enables customers to deploy agentic AI in the IT infrastructure they already have, turning existing investments into a foundation for new AI capabilities. Partners can tailor CPU and GPU configurations to customer workloads, matching agent execution, model inference and supporting compute to each deployment’s performance, power and cost requirements.AMD plans to contribute the AMD Helion specification to OCP, making it available to the community for further development and adoption. AMD Helion agentic rack configurations are currently under development with ecosystem partners and are planned to be available in November 2026.Ecosystem SupportAMD is helping shape the next phase of AI infrastructure through open, flexible platforms, a broad portfolio of workload-optimized compute and collaboration across the ecosystem. AMD Helion brings that approach to agentic AI, helping partners match software and compute to the work agents perform and giving customers flexibility to scale as their requirements evolve.Cisco Compute:“Agentic AI is changing what customers need from their infrastructure. It's not just about compute performance, but how the entire system is connected, managed and secured. Architectures like AMD Helion, combined with Cisco's full-stack infrastructure capabilities, can give customers greater flexibility to deploy, operate and scale agentic workloads into their environments as their needs evolve.— Jeremy Foster, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Cisco Compute”Dell Technologies:“Dell PowerRack gives customers choice without compromise, and our support for AMD Helion Agentic Rack Reference Design extends that promise to the next generation of agentic AI. By combining AMD's rack-scale architecture with Dell's proven engineering expertise, along with the flexibility to extend deployments with Dell PowerRack for Networking and Storage, we're giving customers a complete, validated path to deploy agentic compute at scale with the manageability and reliability they expect from Dell.— Arun Narayanan, Senior Vice President, Compute and Networking, Dell Technologies”Hon Hai Technology Group:“Hon Hai Technology Group continues to deepen its collaboration with AMD on AI infrastructure, supporting the new AMD Helion Agentic AI Rack reference design. Built on an open architecture, the platform combines 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors with flexible CPU and GPU configurations to address hyperscale data center and enterprise Agentic AI workloads. The Group will continue to leverage its strengths in rack-level system integration and global manufacturing, working with ecosystem partners to advance rack-scale Agentic AI solutions and accelerate next-generation AI infrastructure deployment.— Hon Hai Technology Group”HPE:“Next-generation AI workloads require scale, efficiency, and flexibility that open, rack-scale architectures deliver, as demonstrated by our recent customer agreement to deploy AMD Helios. For decades, HPE and AMD have jointly championed open standards, and we are continuing to advance those efforts with AMD Helion. Together, we are ushering in the next era of AI with open large-scale systems, enhanced with air-cooled and direct liquid-cooled networking, supported by decades of HPE expertise and innovation.— Trish Damkroger, Senior Vice President and General Manager, HPC & AI Infrastructure Solutions, HPE”Lenovo:“As agentic AI moves into production, customers need flexibility in how and where they deploy it. That’s at the core of the Lenovo Hybrid AI Advantage, and AMD Helion will give added versatility to meet customers where they are and support the workloads they want to run.— Scott Patti, VP, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Lenovo”QCT:“Agentic AI will require a range of system designs to serve different customer needs. AMD Helion provides an open blueprint that gives QCT the flexibility to tailor compute configurations and bring system design and customization expertise to those requirements.— Mike Yang, President, QCT”Supermicro:“Supermicro is accelerating the deployment of next-generation agentic AI infrastructure by bringing AMD’s Helion - the open, ORv3 compliant rack-scale architecture to market through our Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS). With our proven expertise in OCP accepted™ rack-scale design, integration, liquid cooling, software, and deployment services, we transform advanced Agentic AI architectures into production-ready solutions. Together with AMD, we enable customers to deploy faster, scale efficiently, and accelerate time to online for agentic AI.— Vik Malyala, Chief Business Officer, Supermicro”Wiwynn:“AMD Helion provides an open, flexible foundation for agentic AI infrastructure. Wiwynn is excited to collaborate with AMD, bringing our expertise in rack-level integration and advanced cooling to help hyperscaler customers tailor systems that meet the demanding workloads, power requirements, and data center environments of the agentic AI era.— William Lin, President and CEO, Wiwynn”Supporting Resources Learn more about AMD HelionLearn more about AMD Instinct GPUsLearn more about AMD EPYC CPUsFollow AMD on LinkedIn          Follow AMD on X

documents.title: OCP 2026: AMD CEO Highlights Open Infrastructure for AI
documents.raw_text: During the opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit, Dr. Lisa Su, chair and CEO at AMD, showed how the company’s portfolio of open, full-stack infrastructure delivers the computing power to support agentic AI at every scale.As it works with ecosystem partners and peers to champion open standards, AMD delivers powerful and flexible agentic AI with a broad portfolio of systems enabled by leadership compute – from enterprise systems to gigawatt-scale deployments.​ Throughout the four-day event in San Jose, Calif., AMD – along with its partners and customers – will showcase platforms, demos and use cases.The keynote presentation followed the earlier AMD announcement of the AMD Helion agentic AI rack based on an Open Compute Project spec-design and powered by AMD compute.Keep reading for highlights from the OCP keynote.

    Intel GPU D-series, code-named Crescent Island, is designed for AI inference workloads and is built on Intel's Xe3P architecture. The GPU combines up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory, 1.5TB/s of memory bandwidth and 1.3 petaflops of FP8 compute to help improve the economics of sustained, memory-intensive AI inference. (Credit: Intel Corporation)
    What Is New: At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit today, Intel shared new technical details on the Intel GPU D-series, formerly code-named Crescent Island, introduced new Intel Xeon-based rack designs and highlighted open software and ecosystem innovations.
As open models reshape the economics of agentic AI, demand is growing for more flexible, cost- and power-efficient infrastructure. Together, these advancements reinforce Intel’s approach to open, heterogeneous AI infrastructure, combining general-purpose compute, purpose-built acceleration, open software and standards-based systems to optimize performance and efficiency across AI workloads.
Why It Matters: Agentic AI is transforming inference into a multi-step workflow spanning retrieval, reasoning, orchestration, tool use and execution, with x86 CPUs playing a central role. While open models give enterprises greater choice, power constraints, memory bottlenecks and cost pressures make scaling AI increasingly a systems challenge.
Meeting these demands requires turnkey, heterogeneous infrastructure that is easy to deploy and manage. Building on the established x86 software ecosystem, Intel brings CPUs, GPUs and specialized accelerators together through open, interoperable software to match the right compute resources to each task, improving utilization, performance and efficiency across the entire workflow.
    “Open models are expanding the options enterprises have for deploying AI. To realize their full potential, organizations need infrastructure that can match different workloads with the right intelligence, right compute resources and right economics. That's what we mean by 'put every prompt in its place.”
            - Nicolas Dubé, corporate vice president, Data Center Systems and Solutions Group, Intel.
    Intel Xeon: The Compute Foundation for Agentic AI
At OCP, Intel showcased new Xeon-based rack designs developed with ecosystem partners to meet the growing compute demands of agentic AI. Many leverage the Open Compute Project's Open Rack v3 (ORv3) standard to simplify deployment and integration within open data center infrastructure.
    Intel and its ecosystem partners showcased Xeon-based rack solutions designed to support agentic AI workloads. Many of the systems are built on the Open Compute Project's Open Rack v3 (ORv3) standard, providing customers with deployment-ready infrastructure based on open, modular designs. (Credit: Intel Corporation)
    As agentic workflows grow more complex, they place greater demands on general-purpose compute to orchestrate workloads, process data, manage I/O and execute tasks that keep accelerators productive. To address these needs, select Xeon 6+ configurations scale beyond 46,000 cores per rack at 133.45 kW total rack power, delivering greater CPU compute density to support agentic AI at scale.
Building on two decades of rack-scale innovation and the broad x86 software ecosystem, Xeon provides the high-density, general-purpose compute foundation needed to scale agentic AI. Working alongside GPUs and specialized accelerators, Xeon orchestrates workloads, executes tasks and manages data movement to keep the entire system productive. As AI infrastructure evolves, performance is increasingly measured by the number of concurrent agents a rack can sustain at target latency – and Xeon helps maximize that delivered work by keeping data flowing, tools executing and accelerators fed.
Intel GPU D-Series: Purpose-Built for Efficient Inference at Scale
Intel GPU D-series, code-named Crescent Island, is designed to improve the economics of sustained, memory-intensive AI inference. Built on Intel's latest Xe3P architecture, the GPU combines up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory, 1.5 TB/s of memory bandwidth and 1.3 petaflops of FP8 compute within a 350-watt power envelope. This balance of memory capacity, compute performance and power efficiency reflects Intel's approach to optimizing infrastructure for real-world inference workloads.
Designed for large language models, long-context workloads and concurrent inference services, Intel GPU D-series supports models with up to 300 billion parameters on a single card and more than one trillion parameters in an eight-GPU system. Target applications range from multi-tenant AI services to robotics and other latency-sensitive workloads.
With a standard PCIe form factor, air-cooled design and common Xe software foundation, Intel GPU D-series is designed to simplify deployment within existing data center environments while supporting application portability across Intel GPU platforms. This allows customers to scale inference without specialized rack or cooling infrastructure.
“Inference is becoming the defining AI workload, and enterprises need infrastructure that delivers the right performance at the right cost,” said Anil Nanduri, vice president, AI Products & GTM, Intel Data Center Group. “With Intel GPU D-series, we're focused on making high-capacity inference practical to deploy and economical to scale.”
To help bring these capabilities into production, Intel is collaborating with a broad ecosystem of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, independent software vendors, appliance providers and AI-native companies. Together, these efforts focus on validated platforms, software integration and deployment-ready solutions that reduce complexity and help customers move more quickly from model evaluation to production.
    Intel highlighted a growing ecosystem of customers and partners supporting Intel GPU D-series, including OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, software providers and AI-native companies. Many of the organizations represented are Open Compute Project (OCP) members working to deliver validated, interoperable AI infrastructure and deployment-ready solutions. (Credit: Intel Corporation)
    With customer sampling underway, Intel continues to expand its hardware, software and open-source ecosystem, giving enterprises greater flexibility to deploy and scale inference across existing and new data center infrastructure.
Open Software for Heterogeneous AI
Making heterogeneous AI infrastructure work at scale requires open software that connects compute resources, simplifies deployment and gives developers the flexibility to run workloads on the right architecture. Intel's open software strategy emphasizes native upstream integration with industry-standard AI frameworks, inference runtimes and deployment environments across CPUs and GPUs. By building on the tools developers already use, Intel is helping simplify development, optimize performance and accelerate deployment through several key capabilities:
Simplified deployment across Intel GPUs: Built on a common Xe software foundation, Intel GPU D-series supports software portability across Intel GPU platforms, helping developers reuse existing applications and reduce the effort required to deploy workloads on new hardware.Open frameworks and performance software: Intel supports the AI frameworks, serving engines and development tools already used across the industry, complemented by performance libraries and programmable software layers to optimize inference throughput. These same frameworks support inference and agentic applications running on Intel Xeon processors, enabling developers to work across CPU and GPU architectures.Day 0 support for emerging open models: Through upstream framework integration and model enablement, Intel is working to support new open models as they become available across Intel GPU D-series and Xeon processors. Recent efforts include Day 0 support for Meta's Muse Glimmer, helping developers more quickly evaluate and deploy emerging agentic AI workloads.Built for real-world AI applications and agents: Intel's software stack supports diverse workloads, from high-throughput token generation to coding agents and complex enterprise workflows. The Intel AI for Enterprise Agent Toolkit is optimized and deployable on Xeon processors today, providing orchestration capabilities for production agentic applications. Its provider-based architecture is designed to extend to Intel GPUs, giving enterprises a flexible foundation for multimodal workflows and a path to scale across heterogeneous compute resources.
Open Infrastructure for Heterogeneous AI
Intel continues to advance open infrastructure through its work with the Open Compute Project, where it has made 116 contributions since 2011.
This year, Intel is showcasing its contribution to the Open Adapter Card workgroup, developed with industry partners to define a standardized sub-rack accelerator card form factor. The effort is designed to improve mechanical, electrical and management interoperability across system designs, giving system builders and cloud providers a more consistent path for integrating accelerators into open infrastructure.
For customers, the value of this approach is the freedom to evolve their AI systems without starting over. By building on existing investments and incorporating new compute technologies as workloads change, enterprises can scale inference more efficiently, manage costs and maintain choice over how their infrastructure evolves.
Underlining this, Kevork Kechichian, executive vice president and general manager, Data Center Group, Intel said: “Agentic AI is changing what customers need from their data centers. Success will depend not on any single component, but on open, heterogeneous infrastructure that brings together Xeon, purpose-built acceleration and interoperable software. Intel is helping customers build on their existing investments while creating a flexible foundation to scale emerging AI workloads efficiently.”
Attendees can visit Intel at booth B32 and hear from Intel leaders, including Nic Dubé's keynote, ‘Put Every Prompt in Its Place’, on October 13 at 10:30 a.m. PT. Intel will also participate in more than 30 technical sessions and speaking engagements. For more information, see Intel's OCP 2026 media alert.

documents.raw_text:
News
                    Announcing Intel® Inference Microservices: Tuned LLM Inference on Intel® Processors
                    Intel® Inference Microservices make it easy to get tuned LLM performance on existing Intel® processors, eliminating days of complex, manual hardware optimization.
      Print
      Email
      Copy Link
  Copied
        Artificial Intelligence (AI)
    Getting a large language model to respond is easy. Getting it to respond well, repeatedly, on the hardware you already own is the part that can take a week. Precision, how work is distributed across cores, how memory is laid out across NUMA nodes, and which instruction sets the engine uses all depend on both the model and the processor beneath it. Change the model and the good settings change. Move to a different generation of silicon and they change again.
Intel® is announcing Intel® Inference Microservices. Each microservice is a container that serves one model behind an OpenAI compatible API and configures itself for the Intel® processor it detects at startup, using settings Intel® tuned and validated for that model on that silicon. You pick the model. The container picks the settings.
This first release runs on Intel® Xeon® processors, and it is the first step toward a single inference interface across Intel® hardware. A microservice serves one model on one host. When you need a fleet of them, shared across teams with security and routing already handled, the Intel® AI for Enterprise Inference toolkit provides that layer.
    Try It Now
The example below serves Qwen3-4B. You need a 4th, 5th, or 6th Gen Intel® Xeon® processor and Docker:
                    Python
                    docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 \
  --cap-add SYS_NICE
  --shm-size=2g \
​​​​​​​  intel/inference-xeon-qwen-qwen3-4b:0.1.0
            View all
    That is the only command. On startup the container inspects the processor it landed on, selects the best available configuration profile for that model on that hardware, and applies it for you. There is nothing for you to tune and nothing to work out first.
The first start takes a few minutes while the weights download. Wait for /health, then send it a request straight from the terminal:
                    Python
                    curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-4B",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
  }'
            View all
    That is the whole integration. No custom protocol, no Intel® SDK, no Python environment to build, and no engine to install.
Most AI frameworks already speak the OpenAI API, so pointing one at that base URL is all it takes: the OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, and Haystack all work unchanged, streaming included.
What It Changes for the Business
Faster time to production, at the tuned configuration. Tuning, benchmarking, and adjusting for each model on each platform is replaced by a pull and a run, and what you pull is the configuration that performed best in Intel® Hardware.No new hardware to procure. Inference becomes a scheduling decision against Intel® Xeon® capacity you already own, not a capital purchase, so a project can start this quarter rather than after a procurement cycle.A wider pool of developers can ship AI. Application developers change a base URL. Deploying a model no longer needs an inference optimization specialist, which is the bottleneck most enterprise AI programs actually hit.One pattern to standardize on. A validated profile plus a pinned tag means the same model behaves the same way on every matching host, under Docker and under Kubernetes alike.What you build now carries forward. The interface is the contract, not the silicon. This release runs on Intel® Xeon®, and as Intel® Inference Microservices extend across the rest of the Intel® hardware portfolio the API in front of them stays the same, so moving a workload onto different Intel® hardware later is a deployment change rather than an application rewrite.Your data stays put. Models run in your environment, on your hardware.
What You Get
                Category
                What You Get
            What you run
            One container per model
            What it exposes
            An OpenAI compatible API on a port of your choosing, 8000 by default: chat completions, completions, models, health, and Prometheus metrics
            Engine
            vLLM, with additional engines planned
            What Intel® Inference Microservices sets for you
            Precision, core and work distribution, and memory layout, for your model on this processor
            Hardware
            4th, 5th, or 6th Gen Intel® Xeon® processors, 32 GB RAM suggested. Intel® GPU support planned
            Clientes that work unchanged
            OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM, Haystack. Change the base URL only
                Tooltip content
    Performance is the reason the profile exists. Precision, how work is spread across cores, and how memory is laid out are what decide how much a host delivers, and finding the right combination is normally a week of benchmarking for every model on every platform. Each container ships with the best configuration Intel® measured for that model on that processor, so the tuned path is the one that runs by default.
Automatic Profile Selection
    Figure 1. Your application talks to an OpenAI compatible API. The microservice container sits between that API and the Intel® processor underneath it.
    At startup the container inspects the host it landed on processor generation, how many cores it was given, how many NUMA nodes the machine has, and which built in accelerators the processor offers. That last one is where the real acceleration comes from. Recent Intel® Xeon® cores carry dedicated engines for exactly the math inference spends its time on, Intel® Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel® AMX) for the matrix multiplication at the heart of a model and the vector extensions (AVX-512, AVX2, and VNNI) for the work around it. They are already in the silicon you own, and they only pay off if the serving engine knows they are there and is configured to use them.
Those findings select a validated profile, the runtime resolves the tuned engine parameters, weights are cached, and the optimized inference engine starts behind the API on the port you mapped, 8000 by default. In this release that engine is vLLM. Two hosts with similar product names can legitimately get different settings if their capabilities differ, which is the point. Constrain the container and it configures for the constraint, not for the host.
What happens when nothing matches depends on which container you run. The model specific images ship with the general profile fallback disabled, so an unrecognized host surfaces as an error at startup rather than as a quietly untuned deployment you discover later in a benchmark. That is the conservative default on purpose: the only configurations those images will run are ones Intel® measured for that model. The base image, the one you point at any model on Hugging Face, defaults the other way with profile fallback `enabled`. When no model specific profile matches, selection uses a compatible general profile instead, one that is model agnostic and tuned to the hardware rather than to the model.
You can see what it found without serving anything, and dry-run will print the resolved profile and the exact vLLM command it would execute:
                    Python
                    docker run --rm intel/inference-xeon-base:0.1.0 detect-hardware
docker run --rm intel/inference-xeon-qwen-qwen3-4b:0.1.0 dry-run --format json
            View all
    “The optimizations behind this release are the same ones Intel® contributes in the open, upstream in the frameworks enterprises already build on, including vLLM. Intel® Inference Microservices package that work behind a standard API, so customers get a tuned stack without doing the tuning themselves. We are committed to continue contributing optimizations upstream as we extend the same interface across our hardware portfolio."
            -Bill Pearson, Intel vice president, Data Center Software, Data Center Group
    A First Step Toward Unified Inference on Intel®
This first release targets Intel® Xeon® processors with vLLM at BF16 across 4th, 5th, and 6th Gen, on Docker or Kubernetes 1.24+. Tool calling and structured output are reachable today as vLLM pass throughs rather than validated capabilities. A Helm chart, a Kubernetes Operator, additional inference engines, and additional precisions are planned for later releases.
Each model carries its own license, shown on the model's listing in the Intel® Software Catalog. Users are responsible for complying with the license terms of the model they deploy.
Intel® Xeon® is where this starts, not where it stops. The contract a microservice presents is deliberately independent of the silicon behind it: one container per model, an OpenAI compatible API on a known port, and a runtime that detects the platform it lands on and applies the profile Intel® validated for that combination. Nothing in that contract is specific to a CPU. As the portfolio broadens to Intel® GPUs, including the data center inference GPU codenamed Crescent Island , the same microservice model extends to them. The profile that gets selected changes. The interface your application talks to does not.
That is the point of unifying on one interface. Build against Intel® Xeon® today, on processors already in the fleet and available at ubiquitous scale, then move the same workload to an Intel® GPU when model size or economics call for it, without rewriting the application, tuning it again for the new platform, or standing up a second serving stack beside the first. The choice of silicon becomes a deployment decision rather than an engineering project, and it stays a reversible one. A single API spanning general-purpose CPUs and dedicated inference GPUs provides a consistent portability path across Intel® platforms.
That the interface can stay this stable is not a packaging trick. It holds because the work underneath it goes upstream: native integration with the standard frameworks and open inference engines teams already run, with Intel®'s optimizations contributed to those projects rather than locked inside a vendor-specific toolkit. A tuned container stays a standard OpenAI compatible endpoint instead of becoming an SDK you have to adopt. Intel® Inference Microservices are where that blueprint becomes something you pull and run, and the full picture is laid out in Software Connects the System to the Open Model: An Open Blueprint for Production AI.
Get Started
Intel® Inference Microservices ships as software you run on your own infrastructure. There is no hosted endpoint and no API key to create. Pull an image and run it.
Browse the models to find an image name, and token requirement.Read the documentation for the QuickStart, the Kubernetes guide, and the supported platform list.Learn more about Intel® Inference Microservices.Explore the Intel® Software Catalog for the rest of the developer software.

Samsung Presents ‘Design Is an Act of Love’ at Seoul Design Week 2026 - Samsung Global Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
Samsung Electronics today announced that it is presenting its “Design is an Act of Love” exhibition at Seoul Design Week 2026, taking place in Seoul, Korea.
The exhibition features 14 artworks inspired by Samsung products, displayed on the 2026 OLED TVs (model: S95H) fitted with frames customized for each work.
Building on the theme of the exhibition Samsung held with Korean artists at Design Miami Seoul 2026 in September, this iteration of “Design is an Act of Love” is being held with POLI.design in collaboration with emerging Italian artists. Through creative expression shaped by different cultures and experiences, the exhibition celebrates human diversity and individuality while sharing Samsung’s design vision rooted in understanding and caring for people.
“Through the eyes of different creative minds, familiar products become new expressions of personality, perspective, and ways of life,” said Mauro Porcini, President and Chief Design Officer of the Device eXperience (DX) Division at Samsung Electronics. “By bringing these interpretations together, we want to show how design can make technology a more personal part of everyday life. Ultimately, our ambition is to move beyond designing technology for people to designing technology that truly reflects them.”
14 Italian Artists Reinterpret Samsung Products Through Creativity and Imagination
The artworks draw inspiration from a range of Samsung products spanning mobile devices, home appliances, and TVs — including Music Studio 5, Bespoke AI Family Hub, and Galaxy Z Fold8.
The artists drew on their experience and imagination to reinterpret the forms and characteristics of Samsung products. They used AI as a tool to develop ideas and explore new forms of expression, with each work grounded in the artist’s own perspective and creativity.
Tommy Tokyo, a multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans virtual reality, animation, and digital media, created an artwork inspired by the Infinite AI air purifier. The work translates the product’s core concept of clean air into an expressive visual narrative. Caffè Design drew inspiration from The Serif TV’s iconic I-shaped silhouette, exploring how its distinctive design interacts with the surrounding space.
OLED TVs Showcase Expressive Design With Frames Customized for Each Artwork
The exhibition features 14 Samsung OLED TVs (model S95H), each fitted with a custom frame designed to complement its corresponding artwork’s colors and mood. Created specifically for the exhibition, the frames work together with the on-screen imagery to enhance the presentation of each work.
The Float Layer Design of the OLED TV (model: S95H) makes the screen appear to float above a metal plate. Together, the TV’s distinctive design and custom frames create a visual presentation that highlights the character of each artwork.
Visitors can experience Expressive Design — an approach that embraces human diversity and imagination — through the varied combinations of artworks and frames on the same TV model.
The exhibition will take place from Oct. 15-25 at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) in Seoul.

documents.title: From Smart City to Race Circuit: Samsung’s The Wall in Control Rooms - Samsung Global Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
On the front lines of crisis management, where timely decisions are critical, control rooms are evolving to meet the demands of today’s highly connected society. Moving beyond traditional monitoring, they have become centralized hubs that manage growing volumes of video and data while overseeing communications networks.
From industrial operations to sports and critical infrastructure, organizations around the world are turning to Samsung’s The Wall. Among them are the Iskandar Puteri Command and Control Centre (IPCCC), the integrated operations center for Iskandar Puteri City Council, Johor, Malaysia; and NASCAR, one of the world’s leading motorsports organizations.
▲ The Wall at the Iskandar Puteri Command and Control Centre’s control room
Engineered for Mission-Critical Control Rooms
While the information displayed on screen varies across industries, every control room requires robust security and unwavering reliability.
The Wall uses the industry-standard Advanced Encryption Standard 128-bit (AES-128) encryption algorithm and Samsung’s proprietary Knox Security platform to securely encrypt data transmitted from S-Box to Cabinet.
AES-128, a symmetric-key encryption algorithm adopted by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), protects sensitive control room information while enabling fast data transmission and reception.
Designed for uninterrupted 24/7 operation, The Wall incorporates redundant power and signal systems. If an unexpected power failure or signal error occurs, the backup system activates immediately to ensure continuous monitoring and control.
The Wall’s modular chip-on-board (COB) architecture allows individual modules to be replaced quickly while the display remains on, minimizing downtime. With an LED lifespan1 of up to 150,000 hours — among the longest in the industry – it also helps reduce long-term total cost of ownership (TCO).
Optimized for control room environments, The Wall offers a modular, scalable design that can be customized to virtually any space. Advanced display technology ensures large volumes of information are presented with clarity and precision.
IPCCC: Cross-Agency Coordination for Faster Emergency Response
Urban crises often unfold as a chain of interconnected events. For example, if a water main bursts, traffic may need to be redirected immediately. If a major traffic accident occurs, firefighters conducting rescue operations and police managing the scene must coordinate in real time.
In Johor, Malaysia, IPCCC uses Samsung’s The Wall to support integrated city monitoring and coordination among relevant agencies. IPCCC selected The Wall for its image quality, color richness, and brightness, as well as Samsung’s reputation as a reliable long-term technology partner.
▲ The Wall supports IPCCC’s city operations monitoring with an immersive visual experience.
IPCCC brings together traffic, public safety, and environmental monitoring data onto a single, unified display. Anchoring the operations center is Malaysia’s longest The Wall installation, spanning 19.35 meters and capturing the city’s vast network of information on one screen.
Today, the massive display serves as the command hub for citywide operations — from security monitoring to coordinated incident response. By consolidating this information, The Wall supports stronger inter-agency coordination across departments.
▲ The Wall helps IPCCC city operations teams monitor traffic, public safety, and city services.
“Installing a curved large-scale display allows us to maximize the space while maintaining an efficient operational layout for our workstation and war room,” said Farah Izzati Binti Muhamad Fuad, Director of the Smart City Unit at IPCCC. “The ultra-wide screen enables us to monitor multiple smart safety systems, improving coordination and allowing our team to respond more quickly to incidents.”
NASCAR: Race Control for Split-Second Decisions
Beyond public services, control systems also play a critical role in sports — where capturing every moment of the action is essential. In motorsports, where speeds exceed 290 kilometers per hour and up to 40 cars race in close formation, officials must assess incidents and make decisions in fractions of a second.
▲ The Wall provides NASCAR’s Remote Race Control center with a large, clear view of live race data, video feeds, and on-track conditions.
NASCAR, the most popular motorsport in the U.S., built its Remote Race Control center around The Wall to support race control staff at the track with additional monitoring, analysis, and replay capabilities. Measuring 9.75 meters wide and 2.74 meters high, the massive display provides up to 24 officials a shared, high-resolution view, giving them the visual clarity to review and manage split-second race incidents together.
Equipped with a Micro AI Processor, The Wall analyzes complex live footage in real time to reduce noise. This enables dynamic camera feeds from around the track to be displayed in ultra-high definition with minimal noise and motion blur, helping officials make fast, accurate decisions.
At the launch in 2025, Steve Stum, NASCAR Vice President of Operations and Technical Production, highlighted the visibility that Remote Race Control would provide through more than 200 camera angles and multiple data points from every car, along with its potential to enable faster, more accurate competition calls and improve the racing product. Now in its second season of operation, the remote race control room gives officials greater visibility across races and supports more efficient and accurate officiating.
By consolidating multiple video feeds and data streams on The Wall, the remote race control room enables officials to view more information simultaneously and share feeds for collaborative review.
Describing the experience, Scott Miller, competition strategist at NASCAR, said, “It’s like having 20 monitors in front of you, as opposed to probably two or three sitting at a single work station.”
▲ Samsung technology supports NASCAR’s Remote Race Control center at its production facility in Concord, North Carolina.
Control rooms across industries are evolving to meet increasingly complex demands — whether ensuring the stable operation of infrastructure, enabling integrated citywide monitoring, or supporting live sports where decisions made in fractions of a second can make all the difference. Regardless of the application, every control room depends on a display that helps operators process vast amounts of information and make fast, accurate decisions. As a safe and reliable visual hub for mission-critical operations, Samsung’s The Wall will continue to provide the clarity needed to support decision-making across major industries worldwide.
LED lifetime refers to the rated operating time (L50) until an LED’s brightness decreases to 50% of its initial output. ↩︎

documents.title: Samsung Hosts Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 - Samsung Global Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
Samsung Electronics today announced that it is bringing together global telecommunications industry partners at the Samsung Research America campus in Mountain View, California for the Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 on Oct. 15 (local time), following Partner Day held at the same venue the prior day.
Telecommunications experts from major global operators, manufacturers, government agencies, and academia are participating in the events, with more than 100 attendees gathering to exchange insights and explore the future of next-generation networks.
▲ A view of Partner Day in Mountain View, California, on Oct 14
Samsung is discussing the evolution of software-driven networks for the AI and 6G eras, as well as ecosystem-wide collaboration that creates new value across the telecommunications industry. The company is also showcasing its leadership in 6G communication technology, sharing achievements in AI-native technologies applied to its communication systems, and providing other updates.
Collaboration To Create New Network Value in the AI Era
Partner Day fostered engaging conversations grounded in the expertise and experience of leaders from across the industry. Participants examined software-driven network strategies and ecosystem-wide collaboration as the convergence of AI and networks accelerates the evolution of network infrastructure.
Samsung opened the event with a keynote highlighting the way AI is transforming the architectural foundation that has defined telecommunications networks for more than a century. The company emphasized that, moving beyond the limitations of existing technologies, the convergence of connectivity and AI will be a key driver of new ways of communication that humanity has long imagined. Drawing on the industry’s collective intelligence, Samsung then delved into the strategic direction of network evolution in the AI era.
▲ Woojune Kim, President and Head of Networks Business at Samsung Electronics, is giving his keynote speech at Partner Day, on Oct 14.
The panel sessions centered on experiences and key lessons learned from the commercialization of virtualized networks, exploring how the ecosystem can continue to evolve. Participants also discussed ways to move beyond connectivity by developing new services and translating them into tangible business opportunities.
“Networks in the AI era are evolving into intelligent infrastructure that can understand the diverse requirements of a growing range of new services, flexibly adapt through virtualization, and deliver optimal solutions for each need,” said Angelo Jeongho Park, Executive Vice President and Head of Global Strategic Sales, Networks Business at Samsung Electronics. “Together with our industry-leading partners, Samsung has successfully commercialized virtualized networks at scale. By adding advanced AI technologies to that foundation, we will transform communications infrastructure into a new engine for growth and lead the way toward the industry’s next leap forward.”
AI-Driven Innovation in Wireless Communications
The Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit is opening with keynote presentations from telecommunications industry experts, followed by three panel sessions — “AI-Native 6G Networks,” “Taking 6G to Space With NTN,” and “Connecting the Physical and Digital Worlds” — along with technology demonstrations. Each session includes a lecture on the topic, as well as panel discussions that facilitate dynamic exchanges between participants.
The “AI-Native 6G Networks” session positions AI as the core technology driving innovation in network performance and operational efficiency, with discussion centered on the technical challenges and global collaboration needed to evolve 6G into a truly intelligent network infrastructure.
The “Taking 6G to Space With NTN” session reviews the current status and outlook of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, discusses the technical barriers of space-based communication and satellite connectivity as a potential solution, and addresses satellite communication standards and roadmaps currently under discussion within the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP).
Concluding the day is the “Connecting the Physical and Digital Worlds” session, where participants are discussing new ways to deliver next-generation user experiences by sensing physical spaces and seamlessly linking them to digital services, such as Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) and physical AI.
The technology demonstration session showcases cutting-edge 6G core technologies jointly developed and validated by Samsung and partner companies, including AI RAN implementations, eXtreme Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (X-MIMO) systems, Distributed MIMO (D-MIMO) technologies, and ISAC. Samsung is demonstrating field validation results for the performance of AI-enabled RAN across all layers, transmission performance in the 6G candidate frequency band (7 GHz band), the user experience at cell boundaries, and sensing performance that utilizes base station infrastructure.
▲ An overview of the 6G core technology exhibition booth operated by Samsung Research at the event venue in Mountain View, Silicon Valley, on Oct. 14-15
“Together, 6G and AI-native technologies represent the next step in telecommunications, bringing people closer together than ever before,” said Jinguk Jeong, Executive Vice President and Head of the Advanced Communications Research Center at Samsung Research. “The Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 demonstrates our commitment to closely collaborating with industry partners to advance telecommunications.”
Strengthening the Global 6G Ecosystem
Silicon Valley Future Wireless Summit 2026 and Partner Day come amid Samsung’s efforts to expand its collaboration on 6G and AI-native communication technology with global partners, including telecommunications operators, research institutes, and business groups.
This year, Samsung has initiated collaboration with LG U+ and conducted field validation with Verizon at a major international soccer fan event in Dallas, Texas, for ISAC technology development. The company is also strengthening research partnerships with major telecommunications operators globally, including NTT DOCOMO, KDDI Research, KT, SK Telecom, and SoftBank. These collaborations are part of ongoing efforts to make 6G technology a reality.
Samsung will continue to deepen collaboration with global partners and advance research at the convergence of AI and communications. By connecting its research strengths with business expertise, the company aims to translate innovation into greater value for the industry and reinforce its leadership in AI-native, 6G networks.

documents.title: Samsung Expands Language Support Across AI Experiences on Galaxy - Samsung Global Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
Samsung is expanding language support for Galaxy AI and Bixby, bringing these experiences to more users in their own language.
Galaxy AI is expanding language support across more of its features, starting with those that translate, transcribe, and summarize. Call Assist, Note Assist, Interpreter, and Transcript Assist now include Hungarian and Malay, bringing features such as Live Translate to 24 languages.1
▲ Live Translate of a phone call in Malay-English (Image simulated for illustrative purposes. Actual UX/UI may differ.)
Elsewhere in Galaxy AI, Now Nudge, which suggests a relevant next step based on what is on screen, adds eight languages2 to reach 24 as well.
Bixby is a device agent that offers intuitive device control through natural conversation. Users can ask for what they need in their own words, without having to know the exact name of a setting or where to find it in a menu. With the addition of Polish, Thai, and Vietnamese, Bixby now supports 12 languages,3 allowing more Galaxy users to control their devices more effortlessly.
Bixby’s new languages will begin rolling out on October 14,4 with the new Galaxy AI languages to follow in the coming weeks.5
Galaxy AI supports 24 languages: Arabic, Chinese (China mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan), Dutch, English (Australia, India, UK, U.S.), Filipino, French (Canada, France), German, Gujarati, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil, Europe), Romanian, Russian, Spanish (Mexico, Spain, U.S.), Swedish, Thai, Turkish, and Vietnamese. 				September 8, 2026
                    ASML begins construction of new Eindhoven campus, strengthening its presence in the Brainport region   Groundbreaking ceremony was held Tuesday September 8, 2026 at Brainport Industries Campus North New campus will add manufacturing capacity in support of ASML’s planned growth needs    VELDHOVEN, the Netherlands, September 8, 2026 – ASML Holding N.V. (ASML) today marked the start of construction of its second major industrial campus in the Brainport region, the Netherlands. Together with partners, the company celebrated the milestone with a groundbreaking ceremony at Brainport Industries Campus (BIC) North, launching a multi-phase development project that will eventually span approximately 350,000 square meters and provide potential capacity for up to 20,000 workplaces.  The new location ensures that key activities remain closely connected within the region and are an integral part of the company’s global network. The milestone was celebrated during a ceremony attended by the Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten and representatives from government, customers, suppliers, knowledge institutions and regional partners.   "The growing global demand from the semiconductor industry requires continuous investments," said Christophe Fouquet, President and CEO of ASML. "As part of our global expansion plans, BIC North provides the space and flexibility we need to continue innovating and supporting our customers around the world. It will complement our existing office space and manufacturing capacity in the Brainport region and further strengthen our footprint in the Netherlands. This milestone would not have been possible without close collaboration with local, regional and national authorities and we are particularly grateful for the support we have received from the City of Eindhoven."  A new location, introducing an innovative way of workingThe first phase of BIC North, expected to be completed in 2029, will house at least 3,000 employees, bringing together production, logistics and supporting office activities in one integrated industrial campus. These workplaces are primarily intended for teams relocating from existing ASML locations.    A key element of the campus will be ASML’s new flow factory, ASML’s next-generation innovative manufacturing operating model for the TWINSCAN factory. This model is designed to enable faster, more efficient and higher-scale module production and installation. It streamlines the flow of materials and work through the factory, helping improve productivity while maintaining high-quality standards. The approach follows proven models used in other industries such as automotive and aerospace.  Future footprint in the Brainport regionIn the long term, the BIC campus could accommodate up to 20,000 workplaces, depending on future requirements, providing the flexibility needed to support industry growth.  ASML’s future footprint in the Brainport region will comprise three complementary campuses: a dedicated headquarters campus (De Run 1000) and an industrial campus (De Run 6000/7000) in Veldhoven, alongside the company’s second industrial campus at BIC North in Eindhoven. Together, these locations will support ASML’s innovation, manufacturing and corporate activities in the region.   The development of BIC North reflects the close collaboration between ASML, governments, knowledge institutions and many other stakeholders. Through public-private partnerships, ASML and its partners continue to invest in long-term priorities such as talent development, affordable housing and equal opportunity, helping to support sustainable growth for both the company and the Brainport region.    Media Relations contactsInvestor Relations contactsMonique Mols +31 6 5284 4418Jim Kavanagh +31 40 268 3938 Sarah de Crescenzo +1 925 899 8985Pete Convertito +1 203 919 1714 Karen Lo +886 9 397 88635Peter Cheang +886 3 659 6771 About ASMLASML is a leading supplier to the semiconductor industry.                     Monterey, CA and Veldhoven, the NetherlandsWith more than one million wafers processed to date, Intel Foundry and ASML are helping customers put High NA EUV to work today while preparing for future scale.This week at the SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography conference, Intel Foundry and ASML highlighted continued progress in bringing High Numerical Aperture (High NA) Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography into production and advancing the technologies that will shape its future adoption.Specifically, Intel Foundry and ASML shared the following updates:High NA continues to be used in high-volume manufacturing production at Intel Foundry today, with more than one million wafers processed to date across early tool certification and testing, research and development efforts, and volume production on select layers for a subset of Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 3 processors, code-named Panther Lake. Overlay, throughput and availability are meeting Intel Foundry's expectations.Products manufactured on Intel 18A using High NA for select layers continue to deliver performance that meets or exceeds comparable layers patterned using the NXE platform (EUV with numerical aperture of 0.33).Customers can realize the benefits of High NA using the industry's current mask format, either by floor-planning within the 6-inch mask or by utilizing Intel Foundry’s stitching capabilities and process design kit (PDK) solutions.For more than three years, Intel Foundry has championed the large mask format initiative to align the mask ecosystem, working closely with ASML, mask makers, automation suppliers, EDA partners, materials providers, and semiconductor manufacturers to advance the standards, infrastructure, and technology needed to support future High NA scaling.“Intel Foundry has been one of the key leaders of the industry's adoption of High NA, from installing the first commercial EXE system in 2024, to qualifying the latest generation of tools, to shipping the first high-volume logic product manufactured with High NA,” said Christophe Fouquet, president and CEO, ASML. “ASML recognizes Intel Foundry's pioneering role in High NA and its innovations to deliver value today with 6-inch masks, as well as its long-time support of the 6x12-inch mask evolution.”“The companies building the increasingly complex AI products of the future need manufacturing innovations that are production-ready and easy to use,” said Naga Chandrasekaran, Intel Executive Vice President and Co-General Manager of Intel Foundry. “Within our lithographycapabilities, Intel Foundry is focused on near term enablement of High NA on 6-inch masks with or without stitching, and making the transition to 6x12-inch masks. We will continue to work closely with ASML and the entire industry to enable this transition.”Intel Foundry and ASML are building on years of collaboration to bring together the lithography ecosystem around larger-format masks, helping drive standards, infrastructure, and technology advances needed to support future High NA EUV scaling. Working alongside mask makers, automation suppliers, EDA partners, materials providers, and semiconductor manufacturers, the companies have helped establish the industry's path to larger-format masks while enabling customers to realize the benefits of High NA EUV today.Presentations at SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet LithographyThis week at the SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography conference, Intel Foundry and ASML will share updates on reticle stitching, a technique that enables designers to use High NA EUV with today's standard 6-inch masks.             Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold, the 11th Hyundai Commission, presents a major new multisensory installation by artist and composer Tarek AtouiCombining sculpture, performance, music, technology and social research, Atoui’s Hyundai Commission creates environments where sound is experienced through the whole body and situates Tate Modern’s Turbine Hall as a site for encounter and exchangeHyundai Motor's long-term partnership with Tate continues to support artistic innovation and expand public access to contemporary art, fostering meaningful dialogue and collaboration
                            #Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold
                            #Tate
                            #Artlab
                    SEOUL/LONDON, October 12, 2026 – Hyundai Motor Company and Tate Modern announce the opening of Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold, a major new multisensory installation by artist and composer Tarek Atoui. Combining sculpture, performance, music, technology and social research, Atoui creates environments where sound is experienced not only through the ears, but through the whole body. For his Hyundai Commission, he has transformed Tate Modern’s Turbine Hall into an immersive sonic landscape comprising custom-built wind instruments, percussion, electronics and sculptural objects, woven together to make an orchestra which connects the earth and sky. Through participation and performance, this living environment will constantly evolve throughout the run of the commission.Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold marks the 11th annual Hyundai Commission and inaugurates the next decade of the Hyundai Motor and Tate partnership extending through 2036. Established in 2014, the partnership represents the longest initial commitment from a corporate partner in Tate's history, encompassing the Hyundai Commission and, since 2019, the Hyundai Tate Research Centre: Transnational.Atoui's Hyundai Commission is the culmination of over two decades of experimentation, including collaborations with musicians, instrument-makers, engineers and researchers across Asia and Europe. Drawing on these projects, he reimagines shengs, Korean drums, Uzbek horns and custom-built electronic systems.Hanging above the Turbine Hall ramp, a metal karnai (a ceremonial brass trumpet from Uzbekistan) is joined by two 3D-printed horns that echo and amplify the instrument’s elongated form. At the far end of the hall, drum skins, gongs, horns, stones and 20m long textiles are suspended among a network of bamboo and shengs (mouth organs from China and Southeast Asia), through which wind is channeled by a computer-controlled motor. In making the work, Atoui has responded to the extraordinary height, airflows and acoustic character of the Turbine Hall. Lithophone-like stones and warm lights invite visitors to sit, lie, gaze up, and attune themselves to the relationship between sound, materials, architecture and bodies. Drawing on the artist’s memories of gathering places, from vine-covered canopies to sheltered courtyards, Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold situates the Turbine Hall as a site for encounter and exchange.Microphones embedded within the installation sample the sounds produced by the instruments and the bustling backdrop of the Turbine Hall, with custom software reworking and playing them back as layers of the composition. Foregrounding the importance of improvisation in Atoui's practice, these elements contribute to an ever-changing soundscape.Throughout the six-month duration of the Hyundai Commission, the Turbine Hall will regularly become a site for live sound-based performances, where a network of musicians will 'plug into' Atoui's installation as a sound system. The program will platform both local and international musicians – from instrumentalists to electronic artists, collectives and labels – highlighting the work of Atoui's longstanding collaborators and fostering new connections.
                    Hyundai Commission: Tarek Atoui: Hold creates new forms of connection through sound, bringing together diverse cultures and communities. Through his multisensory and collaborative practice, Atoui invites meaningful exchange and collective reflection on our contemporary world.
	                    DooEun Choi
	                         Art Director, Hyundai Motor Company
                    The annual Hyundai Commission has attracted over 21.6 million visitors and established a platform for some of the most bold and memorable artworks of the past decade – from Kara Walker's spectacular fountain to Anicka Yi's floating artificial lifeforms. By extending the partnership until 2036, Hyundai Motor and Tate reaffirm their shared, long-term commitment to artistic innovation and public access to contemporary art.

However, the company may upload new or updated information if required and assumes that it is not liable for the accuracy of any information interpreted and used by the reader.About Tarek AtouiTarek Atoui (b.1980, Beirut, Lebanon) is a sound artist based in Paris, France. He received a BA in sound art and electro-acoustic music from the French National Conservatory of Reims, France in 1998. He has exhibited and presented performances at major institutions globally, including at TBA21 Thyssen-Bornemisza Art Contemporary, Madrid, Spain (2025); HangarBicocca, Milan, Italy (2025); S.M.A.K., Ghent, Belgium (2024); Museum of Contemporary Art, Sydney, Australia (2023); the Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art, Porto, Portugal (2022 and 2018); Bourse du Commerce - Pinault Collection, Paris, France (2021); Sharjah Art Foundation, Sharjah, UAE (2020); the 58th Venice Biennale, Italy (2019); Tate Modern, London (2016); Serpentine Gallery, London, UK (2012); and dOCUMENTA 13, Kassel, Germany (2012). His work is held in prestigious international collections, including the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, USA; Saradar Collection, Beirut, Lebanon; Tate, London, UK; and the Pinault Collection, Paris, France. He was awarded the Suzanne Deal Booth / FLAG Art Foundation Prize in 2022.About Hyundai Motor’s Art ProjectsFor over a decade, Hyundai Motor Company has deepened its partnerships with museums and cultural organizations worldwide, including Tate, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Korean Pavilion at the Venice Biennale. Hyundai Translocal Series is a new partnership initiative that roots itself in fostering dialogues and collaborations among art institutions in Korea and across the globe. Hyundai Motor’s own art-initiatives include open call programs such as the VH AWARD, the Hyundai Blue Prize+, and Artlab Editorial, a digital platform dedicated to art writing by transnational voices. These ongoing collaborations embrace the complexities of the cultural landscape by exploring new ideas and perspectives within and beyond the art ecosystem. For further information, visit artlab.hyundai.com or follow @hyundai.artlab

            The all-new TUCSON embodies the “Boldest SUV” vision through its “Art of Steel” design, enhanced hybrid performance and intelligent efficiency, and advanced Pleos Connect infotainment systemA refined, spacious cabin enhances everyday comfort with intuitive controls, flexible storage and available relaxation featuresNext-generation Hybrid System delivers intelligent efficiency, targeting up to 42 mpg while harmonizing fuel economy with driving performancePleos Connect drives everyday progress with an ever-evolving digital experience, enabled by Gleo AI, an expanding app marketplace, and intuitive UI/UXTUCSON XRT PRO expands adventure capability with Smart Terrain Assist and advanced off-road technologiesHyundai premieres the all-new TUCSON globally against the Manhattan skyline, showcasing the vehicle's innovative spirit and reinforcing its position as a global SUV icon.

                    NEW YORK, October 1, 2026 – Hyundai Motor Company today unveiled the all-new TUCSON, introducing its boldest SUV ever, which combines the “Art of Steel” design philosophy, hybrid performance enhanced by intelligent efficiency, and the advanced Pleos Connect next-generation infotainment system.The all-new TUCSON made its world premiere against the iconic backdrop of the Manhattan skyline in New York City, underscoring Hyundai Motor’s confidence in its best-selling global SUV. The bold urban venue reflected the vehicle’s innovative spirit, celebrating TUCSON’s rich heritage as a global market leader while signaling a new era of versatile mobility.

                        Designed for ultimate versatility, the all-new TUCSON seamlessly transitions from sophisticated daily commutes to rugged weekend getaways. Guided by the “Art of Steel” design philosophy, it combines muscular exterior styling with a purposeful, tech-forward interior. Alongside the standard model, the debut of the rugged TUCSON XRT PRO further elevates its off-road capability. Integrated with Pleos Connect featuring Gleo AI1), an advanced Next-generation Hybrid System, and Hyundai’s first Smart Terrain Assist (STA)2), the all-new TUCSON lineup empowers customers with confidence and elevated convenience across diverse lifestyles and life stages.

                    Millions of families around the world count on the Hyundai TUCSON, and this is the best one we have ever built. Its combination of bold design, generous cabin space, seamless infotainment, and available hybrid efficiency sets a new standard for what customers should expect in this segment. TUCSON opens the most ambitious product offensive in our history, including more than 100 new and refreshed vehicles globally by 2030 — 58 in North America alone.
	                    José Muñoz
	                         President and CEO, Hyundai Motor Company
                    How Does “Art of Steel” Design Language Influence The all-new TUCSON’s Bold Look?
                        The all-new TUCSON embodies “The Boldest SUV” ideal through Hyundai Motor’s “Art of Steel” design language, combining structural strength with a commanding road presence. Every element, from muscular exterior proportions to refined interior spaces, reflects purposeful engineering and aesthetic vision.The exterior design centers on pronounced, muscular fenders that showcase the inherent tension and strength of steel. This aesthetic is balanced by restrained door surfaces and crisp body lines, reinforcing the all-new TUCSON’s bold SUV image.The redesigned body is longer, wider and taller, commanding greater visual presence while unlocking additional interior space. The long wheelbase model measures 4,700 mm in length (+60 mm), 1,905 mm in width (+40 mm), and 1,685 mm in height (+20 mm) compared to the previous model.The all-new TUCSON’s front design helps to improve pedestrian safety while enhancing forward protection in the event of a collision. Meanwhile, door opening angles expand from 73 degrees to 83 degrees compared to the previous generation, improving accessibility and ease of entry.New nature-inspired exterior colors3)  emphasize the vehicle’s unique design details:Ranger Green Pearl/Matte: A lush green with a color travel effect that shifts from greenish metallic silver to a reddish tone highlighting a bold, unified aesthetic.Kodiak Blue Pearl4): A deep blue with a color travel effect from intense violet to turquoise, revealing a dynamic depth that shifts with changing light angles.Driftwood Gray Metallic/Matte5): An earth-inspired gray with a subtle green-to-red color shift that changes with light, grounding the vehicle in the natural landscape.Red Rock Orange Pearl/Matte: A rugged canyon-inspired tone emphasizing off-road identity.

                    What New Lighting Signatures Define The all-new TUCSON?
                        The front design draws inspiration from architectural lighting principles. H-Edge lighting combines indirect center lighting with edge lighting to enhance horizontal proportions, creating a wider, more stable appearance. This lighting delivers a refined and futuristic front impression.At the rear, the sculptural Prism Rear Lamps sharpen the vehicle’s volume and outline, bolstering the all-new TUCSON’s commanding presence. The design creates the striking impression of light resting at the edge of a transparent lens, revealing an intricate internal pattern that delivers a high-tech, sophisticated signature.Beyond H-Edge and Prism designs, the all-new TUCSON introduces available Micro Pixel Lighting (MPL)6).  Utilizing 25,600 individual LED pixels, MPL enables precision beam patterns, rain guide, and dynamic welcome/farewell animations. Standard LED headlamps feature a two-in-one module design, while LED taillamps are standard across the lineup.

                    How Does The all-new TUCSON Redefine Cabin Comfort?
                        The all-new TUCSON’s interior design creates a furnished space that prioritizes visual refinement and thoughtfulness through furniture-inspired comfort and intuitive controls, delivering a premium user experience. Every surface, from soft cushioning to ergonomically positioned displays, supports stress-reduction, relaxation and a calmer cabin environment.The cabin redefines minimalism for SUVs through purposeful design. The two-layered instrument panel design separates form and function: a horizontal upper layer provides visual comfort and clarity, while a deep open tray below provides storage space. Soft, voluminous cushioning applied across the top of the instrument panel, doors and console armrest create a premium and relaxing interior, scaling home-based, furniture-like comfort to the automotive environment.To minimize driver distraction and reduce cognitive load, the cabin layout ergonomically positions controls within the driver’s natural line of sight. The Double D-Cut steering wheel pairs with a 9.9-inch slim display above the steering column to keep the driver’s visual field uncluttered. Below the center stack display, tactile buttons for frequent-use features including HVAC and audio settings provide intuitive control without the need for distracting screen-tapping while driving.An extended console armrest improves touchscreen ergonomics, prioritizing driver comfort. For added convenience, available dual 15W wireless charging pads are integrated into the console to eliminate cable clutter, while a hidden storage tray accommodates personal items to maintain the cabin’s minimalist aesthetic.The all-new TUCSON’s interior space (1,036 mm front headroom, 1,064 mm rear legroom, 1,470 mm front should room) creates a spacious, luxurious cabin environment. For extended rest, the available Ergo Motion Seat7) features a seven-cell pneumatic lumbar and bolster massage system with manual and auto modes. Additionally, the available four-link Relaxation Comfort Seat8) allows for a one-button recline to 10 degrees — perfect for breaks when parked.The steering column-mounted Shift-By-Wire (SBW) lever consolidates gear selection into an intuitive control stalk, eliminating the need to reach for a traditional center console shifter. An illuminated gear indicator and one-button park engagement simplify driving dynamics while strengthening the “Eyes on the Road, Hands on the Wheel” design philosophy.The Multi-Air Mode System provides sophisticated climate comfort by routing conditioned air through main vents, multi-vents, and floor-level distribution with active management, effectively eliminating uncomfortable direct airflow. Meanwhile, an available three-zone HVAC system9) allows front and rear occupants to customize their climate settings independently.The available 13.5V Metal-Coated Heated Glass10) offers a 15-minute full de-icing capability for harsh winter conditions. In the summer, the glass’s 60 percent solar energy rejection keeps the interior 2 degrees cooler, reducing air conditioning strain and fuel consumption. This transparent conductive coating technology integrates more than 20 layers of metal, dielectric and ceramic materials to provide functionality without visible wire patterns, preserving the cabin’s visual purity.Premium interior colors11) reflect a design philosophy that embraces various lifestyles:Black, Black/Dove Gray, Mud Gray/Dove Gray, Black/Brown packageXRT- and XRT PRO-specific: Black monotone with dark metal accents

                    How Does TUCSON’s Hybrid System Intelligently Balance Performance, Efficiency, and Comfort?
                        At the heart of the all-new TUCSON is Hyundai Motor’s Next-generation Hybrid System, designed for drivers who demand more than just fuel economy. Guided by the “Intelligent Efficiency” principle, the advanced powertrain redefines the hybrid experience by harmonizing efficiency with driving performance.Targeting up to 42 mpg12) and 0–60 mph acceleration in 8.5 seconds, this hybrid powertrain proves that leading efficiency no longer requires compromising performance or refined everyday drivability.The E-Traction system, applied exclusively to HEV models, further enhances handling performance by intelligently optimizing driving torque to reduce wheel slip during cornering. By increasing inner-tire grip, the system improves vehicle stability and control at the handling limit, contributing to a more precise, confident and refined driving experience.The class-leading HEV Stay Mode enables drivers to run features including air conditioning, heating, audio and device charging while the engine is turned off, creating an EV-like in-cabin experience that enhances quietness and comfort during breaks, outdoor activities or waiting periods.Whether selecting the spirited 1.6T-GDI (184 hp / 27.0 kgf·m) with eight-speed automatic transmission for driving performance or the HEV’s targeted 42 mpg for extended adventures, every powertrain option features the integrated electric water pump (EWP). This unified cooling system consolidates separate circuits, reducing weight while maintaining superior thermal performance, efficiency and reliability.The all-new TUCSON Plug-in Hybrid13)delivers a powerful combination of electric and gas propulsion, featuring a 1.6L turbocharged engine paired with a plug-in hybrid system that produces 292 ps and 38.7 kgf·m of torque. With an estimated 81 km of all-electric range, drivers can complete most daily commutes on battery power alone, minimizing fuel consumption and operating costs for routine trips. The 7.2 kW on-board charger enables rapid charging at home or public stations, seamlessly transitioning to gas-engine power for longer journeys.

                    How Does the Evolving Pleos Connect Drive Everyday Progress Inside the Vehicle?
                        The all-new TUCSON delivers an immersive digital cabin experience driven by evolving innovation.Pleos Connect, Hyundai Motor’s Android Automotive OS (AAOS)-based infotainment system, combines a 17-inch or 12.9-inch primary touchscreen display with a 9.9-inch slim display. Intuitive UI/UX features, including three-finger gesture controls and an expansive single-screen mode, help minimize distraction and make every drive smarter and more seamless.At the core of the experience lies Gleo AI14), an in-vehicle agentic AI that understands natural conversation and user context, reducing the need to navigate menus. Drivers can simply ask, “Find a hiking trailhead with parking within 30 minutes,” and the system provides relevant results based on the request’s context. This conversational interface reduces the need for screen interaction, enabling a more intuitive in-vehicle experience.Built on an AAOS foundation, Pleos Connect provides native integration of third-party services such as entertainment and productivity services, and gaming content, without requiring smartphone mirroring or manual connection steps. The infotainment system receives over-the-air (OTA) updates, ensuring the vehicle continues to evolve with consumer needs.
