[[PAGE 1]]
HERMES INTERNATIONAL, Société en Commandite par Actions (partnership limited by shares) with capital of €53,840,400.12,
Registered in the Paris Trade and Companies Register under number 572 076 396, whose registered office is
at 24, rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, 75008 PARIS
Half-year information report as at the end of June 2026
Solid sales momentum and excellent results in the first half
Revenue amounted to €8.2 billion
(+6% in the first quarter and +7% in the second quarter, at constant exchange rates)
Recurring operating profitability reached 41.0% of sales
Adjusted free cash flow grew by 18%
Paris, 29 July 2026
The group’s consolidated revenue in the first half of 2026 amounted to €8.2 billion, up 6% at
constant exchange rates and 2% at current exchange rates compared to the same period in 2025.
All the regions recorded growth, with the exception of the Middle East, which showed good
resilience in a challenging environment. The Americas, Japan and Europe excluding France
recorded remarkable progression in both the first and second quarters. Recurring operating
income amounted to €3.4 billion (41.0% of sales), slightly up.
In the second quarter, sales reached €4.1 billion, up 7% at constant exchange rates, marking a
slight acceleration from the first quarter, notably in France, in Japan and in the Middle East.
Axel Dumas, Executive Chairman of Hermès, commented:
“In the first half of 2026, Hermès delivered a solid performance, which reflects the strong
desirability of its 16 métiers and the trust of its clients. Convinced by the strength of our unique
artisanal model and in control of our key balances, we look to the second semester with
confidence.”
Sales by geographical area at the end of June
(at constant exchange rates unless otherwise indicated)
At the end of June 2026, all the geographical areas posted growth with the exception of the
Middle East, slightly down.
• Asia excluding Japan (+2%) continued its growth, notably in Greater China. Korea delivered
an outstanding performance. January saw the opening of the new store in Hanoi, Vietnam,
followed in early April by the new Sanlitun store in Beijing, China. The Hong Kong
Elements and Taipei Sogo Fuxing stores reopened at the end of April, after renovation and
expansion work. In May, the Hermès in the Making travelling exhibition, which showcases
the savoir-faire of our artisans was presented in Shanghai.
• Japan (+11%) recorded strong growth, with an acceleration in the second quarter. This
performance was supported by strong traffic and the loyalty of local customers. Following
the expansion and renovation of the Hilton Plaza East store in Osaka in May, the house
inaugurated its new store in Nagoya in June.

[[PAGE 2]]
H1 2026 Results
2
• The Americas (+15%) once again delivered a remarkable performance, following an exceptional first
quarter, with solid, balanced growth across all countries and métiers. In Los Angeles in June, the house
revealed the second chapter of the women’s fall-winter 2026 ready-to-wear collection, with great success.
• Europe excluding France (+9%) continued its solid momentum across all countries in the region. The
Berlin store in Germany reopened in May after renovation and expansion work. On 16 June, the house
inaugurated a new Hermès Maison at 166 New Bond Street in London in the United Kingdom. Spanning
six buildings and more than 2,000 square metres, this sixth Maison showcases Hermès’ exceptional
creativity and savoir-faire.
• France (+2%) posted a solid acceleration in the second quarter, driven by both local customers and a
recovery in tourist traffic.
• The Other area (-4%), which mainly comprises the Middle East, demonstrated remarkable resistance in
an unstable geopolitical environment. The second quarter showed a gradual recovery, driven by local
customers and the house’s value strategy.
Sales by sector at the end of June
(at constant exchange rates unless otherwise indicated)
At the end of June 2026, all the métiers, with the exception of Perfume and Beauty, delivered positive growth.
The Leather Goods and Saddlery, Ready-to-wear and Accessories, Silk and Textiles as well as Watches
métiers accelerated in the second quarter.
• Leather Goods and Saddlery (+10%) recorded a solid performance, with slightly higher growth in the
second quarter. The sector benefited from the high desirability of the collections in all the regions. The
new Cliquetis, Kelly Hobo and Double Longe models have been met with great success. Hermès
continued to increase its production capacities, with the opening of a twenty-fifth leather goods workshop
in Loupes (Gironde) in early April. Three further leather goods workshops are scheduled to open in the
coming years: Charleville-Mézières (Ardennes) in 2027, Colombelles (Calvados) in 2028 and Les
Andelys (Eure) by 2030. Hermès thus continues to reinforce its local anchoring in France through the
development of employment and training.
• The Ready-to-wear and Accessories sector (+2%) benefitted from a notable improvement in the second
quarter driven by strong momentum in ready-to-wear. The women’s fall-winter 2026 collection was
successfully unveiled in early March at the Garde Républicaine, followed by the second chapter of the
collection in June in Los Angeles, which generated tremendous enthusiasm.
• The Silk and Textiles sector (+10%) delivered a remarkable performance, with an acceleration in the
second quarter, driven by abundant creativity and a rich palette of colours, designs and shapes. To mark
the opening of Maison Bond Street in London, the Bouquet Final and Cocoricooooo scarves were
reinterpreted in tribute to the capital of the United Kingdom, while The New Hermès Record scarf was
unveiled in an exclusive edition created for the occasion, embodying the house’s creative vitality with
boldness and elegance.
• Perfume and Beauty (-4%) continued the development of its lines. The Perfume universe was enhanced
with a seventh creation in the Jardin collection, Un Jardin sous la Mer, together with a new Hermessence
fragrance, Musc Pallida. The first foundation in the Hermès Beauty Line, Plein Air, launched at the
beginning of the year, has met with great success.
• The Watches métier, stable over the first half, posted solid growth in the second quarter. The métier drew
on the strength of its iconic collections, including Cape Cod, and the enrichment of its offering. At the
Watches & Wonders exhibition in Geneva, the house notably unveiled a titanium skeleton version of its
Hermès H08 watch, equipped with the new H1978 calibre. The expansion of production capacities

[[PAGE 3]]
H1 2026 Results
3
continues with the extension of the watchmaking facility in Le Noirmont (Switzerland), scheduled for
completion by 2028.
• The Other Hermès sectors (+5%), which include Jewellery and the Home Universe, continued to grow,
revealing the full creative strength and singularity of the house. The ninth Haute Bijouterie collection,
Into the Horsescape, was unveiled to great enthusiasm in early July, at the Musée des Arts Décoratifs in
Paris. Meanwhile, the Home collections took centre stage at the Salone del Mobile in April, highlighting
the excellence of Hermès’ savoir-faire.
High profitability and strong cash flow growth
Recurring operating income amounted to €3.4 billion compared to €3.3 billion in the first half of 2025,
slightly up. Despite the negative impact of currencies, recurring operating profitability reached 41.0%,
compared to 41.4% at the end of June 2025.
Consolidated net profit (group share) remained stable at €2.2 billion. It includes, as in the first half of 2025,
the exceptional contribution levied on the profits of large companies in France. Excluding this contribution,
consolidated net profit (group share) amounted to €2.5 billion, representing 30.7% of sales.
Cash flow from operating activities grew strongly by 16% to €2.7 billion, driven by a stable change in
working capital requirement, resulting notably from effective inventory management and exceptional
sell-through rates on the latest collections.
Adjusted free cash flow reached €2.2 billion, up by 18%, after accounting for operating investments
(€0.3 billion) and repayment of lease liabilities (€0.2 billion).
After distribution of dividends of €1.9 billion and share buybacks dedicated to employee share ownership
plans for €0.2 billion, the restated net cash position amounted to €12.9 billion at the end of June 2026,
compared to €12.8 billion at the end of December 2025.
A sustainable and responsible model
In line with its commitments as a responsible employer, Hermès continued to create employment, increasing
its workforce by more than 600 people over the first six months of the year, including 300 in France. At the
end of June 2026, the group employed 27,107 people, 16,656 of whom are based in France.
In February, the house distributed a bonus of €3,000 to all its employees worldwide for 2025, in order to
share the fruits of growth with those who contribute to it daily.
In March 2026, Hermès conducted a new employee survey, entitled “Hermès Hears”, inviting all its
employees worldwide to share their views on their workplace well-being and their level of engagement. This
survey, which 90% of employees completed, highlighted their strong engagement as well as their pride in
belonging to the house.
Hermès pursued its action in favour of nature, successfully completing the first two steps of the Science
Based Targets for Nature (SBTN) initiative. The materiality assessment and the prioritisation of impacts
provide a rigorous scientific basis for setting ambitious and measurable targets. This independent validation
demonstrates the strength of Hermès’ approach and its commitment to placing biodiversity conservation at
the heart of its strategy.
Furthermore, Hermès participated in the launch of the fourth Livelihoods Fund, of which it has been a partner
since 2012. The fund combines action to fight climate change, support for the transition to regenerative
agriculture, and improvement of local livelihoods.

[[PAGE 4]]
H1 2026 Results
4
Finally, Hermès has been recognized by the Transparency Awards “Vigilance Plan” award, which recognizes
the clarity of its communication on its supply chain and the quality of its non-financial disclosures.
Other highlights
At the end of June 2026, currency fluctuations represented a significant negative impact of more than €360
million on revenue.
During the first six months of the year, Hermès International redeemed 94,846 shares for €160 million,
excluding transactions completed within the framework of the liquidity contract.
Outlook
In the medium-term, despite the economic, geopolitical and monetary uncertainties around the world, the
group confirms an ambitious goal for revenue growth at constant exchange rates.
The group continues its development with confidence, thanks to the highly integrated artisanal model,
balanced distribution network, the creativity of collections and the loyalty of clients.
Thanks to its unique business model, Hermès is pursuing its long-term development strategy based on
creativity, maintaining control over know-how and singular communication.
The theme for the year, Venture beyond, is an invitation to discover new horizons and renew our curiosity,
constantly.
Limited review procedures have been carried out on the condensed interim consolidated financial statements by the
Statutory Auditors in accordance with applicable regulations.
The half-year financial report, the press release and the presentation of the 2026 half-year results are available on
the group's website: https://finance.hermes.com
Upcoming events:
• 22 October 2026: Q3 2026 revenue publication
• 11 February 2027: 2026 full-year results publication
• 22 April 2027: Q1 2027 revenue publication
• 28 April 2027: General Meeting of shareholders

Microsoft to expand Azure Maia system to multi-gigawatt deployments
						Oct 12, 2026
					|
	Scott Guthrie - Executive Vice President, Cloud + AI
		Azure Maia 200 now in production; Azure Maia 300 coming in 2027
As we move into the era of Super Intelligence, Microsoft is entering a new phase of infrastructure. We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services.
The multigenerational Azure Maia program has become a foundational element of Microsoft’s AI infrastructure strategy. Maia 200 is now serving Microsoft production workloads, including Microsoft Copilot, and supporting the MAI team as they develop next-generation models, with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry to follow by end of year. Across these workloads, Maia 200 runs OpenAI models, Microsoft’s own MAI models and leading open-source model families. Insights from the scale of Microsoft’s AI services allow for unique co-design between hardware systems and software applications to optimize real-world use cases across enterprise applications and industry scenarios.
Maia 300 is a complete intelligent system designed for the new types of AI workloads emerging today: Long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversational experiences and sustained, multi-step agentic tasks. By improving efficiency across the system, we expect Maia 300 to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems. And in a full 96-accelerator configuration, it delivers up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200.
YouTube Video
Click here to load media
Maia 200: Driving the workloads that Microsoft runs at scale
The Azure Maia system is designed around the real-world workloads Microsoft runs at scale and the models we expect to build in the years ahead. Because silicon development takes years, our software and hardware teams collaborate early to anticipate architectures, scale and capabilities, translating those requirements into greater memory capacity, higher bandwidth and more accelerators operating as a single system.
That co-engineering is already delivering measurable efficiency gains. Maia 200 is deploying across the United States, Europe and Australia and delivering up to 1.7x more tokens per watt for built-in AI capabilities in Microsoft Teams, Copilot and Cowork experiences compared with leading GPU infrastructure.
Experience running our AI models and services on Maia 200 directly informed the design of Maia 300. Together, the two generations are designed to support a broad set of additional Microsoft’s AI services: multi-step agentic work that will help GitHub deliver coding experiences more efficiently; cloud-scale model serving that will help Microsoft Foundry support diverse architectures and deployment environments; inference and data generation for the MAI team; and latency-sensitive interactions that will help Dragon Copilot scale workflows and reduce clinicians’ administrative burden.
Maia 300: Scaling more useful AI within every megawatt
AI is becoming a foundational layer of every application, workflow and business process. As enterprises move beyond chat experiences to systems of agents that can reason, act and collaborate, AI infrastructure must deliver intelligence securely and efficiently at scale while continuously adapting as models and workloads evolve.
As the third generation of our Azure Maia program, Maia 300 is designed with an inference-first architecture optimized for long-context, memory-intensive and decode-heavy AI workloads. This involves balancing compute, memory bandwidth, networking and power efficiency at cloud scale.
Azure Maia 300 system
Key capabilities of the Maia 300 system include:
Less data movement, more useful compute: Moving data efficiently, rather than raw compute power, is increasingly the bottleneck in large inference systems. Maia 300’s software-defined dataflow architecture and AI-assisted kernel optimization work together to maximize locality, reduce data movement and improve utilization across compute, memory and networking resources. By treating dataflow as a first-class design principle, Maia 300 delivers a significant performance-per-watt advantage over traditional GPU architectures.
Higher memory bandwidth within every watt: As AI workloads become increasingly context and memory-bound, Maia 300 delivers industry-leading HBM bandwidth per watt. Eight HBM4 stacks provide 18.0 TB/s of peak memory bandwidth within a 950-watt TDP, enabling efficient execution of large models and long-context workloads. Specialized kernel support uses on-die SRAM as a software-managed scratchpad, reducing pressure on HBM.
Chiplet architecture for enhanced efficiency: A new multi-chiplet architecture separates compute, memory-controller and I/O functions, improving efficiency, scalability and cost structure. Compute chiplets are built on TSMC’s N2P process node to maximize performance-per-watt.
Larger context, richer intelligence: By designing for advanced low-precision formats, including enhanced MXFP4, Maia 300 reduces memory and bandwidth requirements for both computation and KV-cache storage. The result is larger context windows, higher throughput and improved model efficiency within the same power envelope.
Scale-up networking at datacenter scale: Maia 300 treats networking as a seamless extension of the software-defined dataflow architecture. Rather than moving data through separate communication layers, dataflow operations span compute, memory and network resources as a single system. High-bandwidth interconnects between Maia accelerators are optimized for tensor parallelism, while a custom AI transport delivers performant and reliable scale-up communication across accelerators and racks. The AI-optimized transport leverages Ethernet-based networking infrastructure to enable a unified topology that scales efficiently from a single rack to datacenter-scale deployments.
Higher AI throughput from every rack: Maia 300 rack systems bring together 96 accelerators within a 167-kilowatt power envelope, delivering 27.6 TB of HBM capacity and 1.7 PB/s of aggregate HBM bandwidth across a high-speed scale-up domain. That density allows Microsoft to serve more simultaneous AI interactions and larger workloads from each rack, improving datacenter capacity and the economics of expanding AI services.
Maia 300 will begin production deployments in 2027. For more information on Maia 300 architectural details, read our technical paper.
Maia 300 at a glance
Azure Maia is at the heart of our Frontier Transformation
The future will not be defined by a single model or a single piece of silicon or a single innovation. Model and silicon choice are inherent in our vision for Frontier Transformation. Our focus is on developing responsible, affordable and scalable platforms that will help everyone amplify their intelligence to drive breakthrough outcomes that matter for them.
Microsoft is unique because we are able to optimize from silicon to systems to agent on an open, heterogenous and model diverse platform our customers can count on for their AI transformation, today and in the years ahead. This platform is at the heart of Frontier Transformation, and Azure Maia is a foundational component of our approach to expand access, accelerate innovation and help customers capture more value from AI.
Next month at Microsoft Ignite 2026 in San Francisco and online we’re looking forward to sharing more information on our strategy, technology adoption trends and success in Frontier Transformation.
For more details, photos and videos, visit our Maia 300 site.
Scott Guthrie is responsible for a set of hyperscale cloud computing solutions and services including Azure, Microsoft’s cloud computing platform, generative AI solutions, data platforms and information and cybersecurity. These platforms and services help organizations across the globe solve urgent challenges — and transform for the future.

Microsoft 365 and LinkedIn leadership update
						Oct 1, 2026
					|
	Microsoft Corporate Blogs
		Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO, and Ryan Roslansky, Executive Vice President of LinkedIn and Microsoft 365, shared the below communications with Microsoft and LinkedIn employees this morning.
SATYA NADELLA MESSAGE
After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky has decided to leave Microsoft and embark on his next chapter.
As Ryan and I have been discussing our roadmap and work ahead, we felt this was the right moment for this change. Ryan will stay through the end of the calendar year as an advisor to me and will support on the transition.
Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position. With Copilot, we are executing rapidly against our vision to build a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task, with Office fully embedded in Copilot and vice versa! Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible. Last week’s launch was an important milestone in that journey, and the strong response from customers, partners, and the broader ecosystem reinforced both how far we’ve come and how much opportunity remains ahead.
At LinkedIn, we remain focused on our core vision of creating economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce, helping our 1.3 billion members access the knowledge, insights, and opportunities they need to navigate rapidly changing professional and labor markets.
Effective today we will make the following changes:
Sumit Chauhan and Lan Ye will report to Charles Lamanna.
Jon Friedman will report to Jacob Andreou.
Dan Shapero will continue as CEO of LinkedIn and Mohak Shroff will continue in his role, both reporting to me.
Over his nearly two decades at Microsoft, Ryan has helped shape how people around the world find opportunity, build their careers, and get their work done. I’ve always appreciated his clarity of thinking and I’m deeply grateful for everything Ryan has built, for the leaders and teams he has developed, and for his friendship and counsel.
Please join me in thanking Ryan for his extraordinary contributions to LinkedIn and Microsoft, and in wishing him the very best in what comes next.
Satya
RYAN ROSLANSKY MESSAGE
Team,
In 1996, as a college freshman, I taught myself to code so a few friends and I could help other students find a place to live around campus. I didn’t know much. I did know the internet was about to change how people found things, and I wanted to be as close to that as possible.
In 2009, Jeff Weiner made me his first hire at LinkedIn. I’ve spent the nearly 18 years since working on a much bigger version of that same idea: helping people find opportunity, and then helping them do great work once they have it.
This has (obviously) been the best professional experience of my life.
As a product manager, I got to build dozens of features that are still around today (some good, some not so good!). When I became CEO in 2020, the world was months into a pandemic that changed what work even meant. Nobody hands you a playbook for that. This team wrote one anyway. Since then, LinkedIn has passed a billion members and nearly tripled its business, and every bit of that belongs to the people who built it.
Last year, Satya asked me to help build the future of M365. Once again, the old rules didn’t apply. AI was rapidly changing how professionals work, and the world’s largest productivity suite needed to lead the way. That meant figuring out what Copilot, and the future of work, should look like as one ecosystem.
We still have a ways to go, but the progress over the past year has been inspiring to watch. A lot of talented people set aside their own roadmaps to make that happen. Thank you. I know it wasn’t easy.
Satya, thank you. When LinkedIn joined Microsoft, you gave us room to build, and then trusted many of us with a lot more. I’ve learned more from you than I can fit in an email, and I’m grateful for the friendship that came with it.
All of which made this a hard decision. I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day. But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area. My wife Leigh gives her time to more local organizations than I can keep track of. Our youngest daughter just started high school, and our dog Buddy remains deeply committed to the trails on the Peninsula!
I thought about this for a long time. It’s the right call. The work now goes to leaders who are set up to take it further. I can’t wait to see what they do with it.
Over the years, people have asked me what’s kept me so energized and motivated in this work. I think the answer is that I got to spend my career working where doing good and doing well are the same thing. In technology, that’s the best place to operate.
Most companies start by focusing on doing well, so doing good becomes a compromise. It’s the last slide of the PowerPoint, or a separate .org. But when doing good is built into the product itself, it becomes a real competitive advantage. When we build valuable products, people find jobs, they hire, they learn skills, they start companies, they run companies. That creates value for members, customers and the world. And for our business too.
Not many companies get to work this way, and not many people get the chance to build something like it. We do.
That matters more now than it ever has. Technology will continue to touch every job on the planet, and the people building it will decide what kind of world it helps create. I can’t think of a better group to figure that out than the people reading this note.
Thank you for the best 18 years I could have asked for.
RR

documents.title: New Microsoft data innovations unlock what only your business knows - The Official Microsoft Blog
documents.raw_text:
New Microsoft data innovations unlock what only your business knows
						Sep 28, 2026
					|
	Jessica Hawk - CVP, Azure Product Marketing
		Every organization has knowledge that is uniquely its own: the way its business operates, the data it has built over time, the expertise of its people and the context behind thousands of everyday decisions.
As powerful AI models become more widely available, that unique business intelligence matters more than ever. The difference will come from how effectively organizations combine those models with the data, expertise and business context that make them unique.
Turning that intelligence into lasting advantage requires three elements to work together: human ambition to set the direction, intelligence grounded in the organization’s unique knowledge and trust to provide the foundation for operating at scale. Microsoft’s approach is designed to bring those elements together so organizations can build on what they know and create greater value over time.
That value can compound through a continuous learning loop, where AI draws on an organization’s data and expertise, improves the systems and experiences it creates and generates better outcomes over time without making the organization dependent on any single model provider.
Today at the European Microsoft Fabric + SQL Community Conference in Barcelona, we are introducing advances across Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databases that help organizations put their data estate at the heart of a successful AI strategy.
Fabric IQ: Bring your unique business context into Microsoft Copilot
As Microsoft Copilot evolves across Home, Code and Autopilot, access to trusted business context becomes essential. Fabric IQ brings governed business context into Copilot, grounding experiences in the Power BI semantic models, metrics, relationships and business definitions organizations already trust.
With Fabric IQ in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Cowork now generally available, users can ask business questions and receive answers grounded in governed Power BI data, while Cowork can use those insights as part of broader multistep work. Integration with the new Code experience is coming through the Frontier program.
That means when someone asks Copilot for the latest sales forecast or another critical business metric, the answer can be grounded in the same semantic model that powers the organization’s reports, helping avoid confusion about which number is correct. For Power BI customers, this extends the semantic foundation they already have into Microsoft Copilot while preserving existing access controls and governance.
I experienced this myself recently as I was preparing for a sales review and asked Copilot, “What’s our latest sales forecast?” With Fabric IQ, that answer was grounded in the same governed Power BI semantic model that powers the team’s sales reporting, using the same business definitions and metrics my team already trusts. So, instead of spending the meeting uncovering and debating whose number was right, the team was able to get straight to what the numbers mean and focus on what we do next. That’s exactly the kind of experience we want to create.
For Fabric and Power BI customers, this capability is on by default in Copilot Chat and Cowork and extends the semantic foundation they already have into Microsoft Copilot while preserving existing access controls and governance.
IQ Sharing in Microsoft Fabric: Share unique business context without giving up control
Business knowledge does not stop at the boundary of a team or business unit. Organizations increasingly need to collaborate across customers, partners and broader ecosystems while maintaining control over the information they share.
IQ Sharing in Fabric, now in preview as part of Fabric IQ, breaks down company boundaries by enabling organizations to securely share data and the business context that gives it meaning, while maintaining governance over the underlying assets. Starting with key Fabric IQ artifacts and context, IQ Share is designed to evolve beyond preview to help customers discover, share and activate trusted context wherever it’s needed.
Together with OneLake mirroring and shortcuts, these investments create a more open foundation for sharing governed data and context across organizations, platforms and ecosystems.
Observability in Microsoft Fabric: Maintain visibility and control as AI scales
As organizations put more workloads on their unified data platform, they need to understand system health and address issues before they affect business and AI outcomes.
Observability in Fabric helps teams move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive operations. Cross-workspace monitoring and an enhanced Monitor Hub provide a unified view across jobs, capacities, workspaces and workloads, while Operations Agents and Activator help teams investigate issues, identify root causes with AI and automate responses.
Together, these capabilities help organizations maintain oversight as they scale data and AI.
Fabric Apps: Build applications directly on governed business data
AI is transforming how applications are created, but enterprises still need a secure, governed path from idea to production. Fabric Apps brings application development directly to governed data in Microsoft Fabric, helping organizations build and scale AI-powered business applications faster.
With new capabilities for data connectivity, transactional workloads, backend logic, storage and policy-controlled access, developers can move from prototype to production on a unified data foundation. These experiences bring application creation closer to where enterprise data and insights already live, helping more people turn data into action.
Agentic data engineering: Automate the work, stay in control
A continuous learning loop is only as good as the data behind it, which must be prepared, refined and improved without pause. As those environments become more complex, organizations need automation that can take on more of that work without pushing people or controls out of the loop.
Earlier this year, we shared our vision for autonomous data engineering. Now, new agentic data engineering features in Fabric bring that vision to life, bringing autonomous execution to complex data engineering initiatives while keeping organizations in control. Engineers define the outcome and set the boundaries. Inside those limits, the agent plans and executes the work, validates the results and refines the approach.
SQL Server on Azure Local: Keep critical data and workloads where you need them
Maintaining control over business knowledge also means having flexibility over where critical data and workloads run.
Now generally available, SQL Server on Azure Local brings SQL Server and Azure services into local environments, giving organizations more choice to run workloads closer to their applications and operations. SQL Server on Azure Local with disconnected operations, now in preview, extends that flexibility to environments where cloud connectivity is interrupted, restricted or unavailable.
These options give organizations operating across regulated, local, edge and disconnected environments greater choice over where their critical data and workloads reside and operate.
Database Hub in Fabric: Simplify database management with agentic assistance
Intelligent applications depend on operational data. Teams need a clear view of the databases that power those applications and practical tools to manage them.
Building on its introduction at FabCon Atlanta, Database Hub in Fabric is now in public preview. It provides a central control plane for managing SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB and SQL databases in Fabric, helping administrators monitor and govern their database estate.
Complementing this management experience, specialist database agents for SQL and PostgreSQL in Database Hub in Fabric and Visual Studio Code, coming soon to public preview, help teams investigate issues, understand performance bottlenecks and identify optimization opportunities within their development environment.
Together, these capabilities help teams understand their database estate and make more informed operational decisions.
Build AI on the knowledge that makes your business different
Our goal is straightforward: help organizations use the best AI models and tools available while turning their proprietary data, expertise and workflows into an advantage that grows more valuable over time. That direction is reflected across today’s announcements as the data foundation comes into focus.
At Ignite, we’ll broaden this story across the full Microsoft Frontier ecosystem, connecting data, applications, agents, governance and infrastructure into one system that turns AI ambition into business outcomes.
Explore the complete set of announcements across Microsoft Fabric and Azure Databases in today’s blog from Arun Ulagaratchagan, Executive Vice President of Azure Data.
Jessica Hawk leads Azure Product Marketing at Microsoft, driving strategy and storytelling across the full Azure portfolio. Her team defines how Azure shows up in the market — helping customers and developers tap into the platform’s full potential across cloud, data, AI and developer innovation.

documents.raw_text:
Salesforce Partners
			Announcing Koa: Salesforce’s First CRM Reasoning Model, Built on NVIDIA Nemotron
			September 15, 2026
			5 min read
		Media Library
Koa is trained with 27 years of Salesforce CRM intelligence to enable agents to reason through the complex, multistep tasks required for enterprise work
The collaboration also brings NVIDIA open models and accelerated computing into Missionforce, giving government and regulated organizations control over their model, data, and deployment environment
SAN FRANCISCO, September 15, 2026 — Salesforce and NVIDIA today announced Koa, Salesforce’s first CRM reasoning model for Agentforce, built on NVIDIA Nemotron. Developed through deep technical collaboration with NVIDIA, Koa is purpose-built to help agents reason through complex, multistep workflows and use the right tools to get work done.
Koa was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super with a proprietary synthetic dataset modeled on enterprise knowledge from nearly three decades of CRM deployments. The result is a reasoning model grounded in how businesses run — their processes, workflows, and operational policies. In Salesforce’s CRM benchmark, a model benchmark that includes a suite of real-world tasks like updating an opportunity, routing a case, or scheduling a follow-up, Koa already matches or exceeds leading model performance on CRM actions with three times fewer errors. Salesforce controls the model weights and performs post-training and inference entirely within its own trust boundary, giving customers a specialized, Salesforce-hosted option to power their Agentforce use cases.
Salesforce and NVIDIA are also bringing Nemotron-based models and accelerated computing into Missionforce, extending that same control over model, data, and deployment environment to government and regulated organizations. Together, the companies are bringing mission-specific AI to private clouds, air-gapped networks, and other secure environments.
“The most valuable thing Salesforce has built isn’t our platform — it’s the accumulated knowledge of how enterprise business actually works. With Koa, the knowledge is put inside the model itself. We trained a reasoning engine that understands the structure of a deal, the lifecycle of a service case, and the workflows that vary across industries. That’s a different kind of intelligence, and it runs entirely inside your trust boundary.” — Marc Benioff, Chair and CEO, Salesforce
“AI is creating a much larger opportunity for software. Every company needs useful AI, tailored to its knowledge, expertise, and work. NVIDIA Nemotron open models give Salesforce the foundation to turn decades of enterprise expertise into specialized AI with Koa, creating a CRM model that can reason and securely take action.” — Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA
What makes Koa different
No customer data was used to train the Koa reasoning model. Its training corpus was built entirely from synthetic scenarios that reflect the reasoning, tool use, and decision-making skills Agentforce agents perform across CRM workflows: generating leads, qualifying opportunities, and resolving service cases across the customer lifecycle.
Rather than relying on generic content, these scenarios were built to simulate real-world enterprise workflows across more than 14 industries, including manufacturing, financial services, healthcare, and travel. Each scenario paired a persona with specific tasks then mapped the sequence of actions and tool calls an agent must take to complete them.
To post-train the model, Salesforce applied Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with NVIDIA NeMo RL, NeMo Gym, and NeMo AutoModel. By training on a targeted set of prioritized enterprise tasks, the model developed deeper expertise and learned not only to produce the right answer but to take the right action, step by step, to reach a goal.
NVIDIA Nemotron open models gave Salesforce the control to build CRM intelligence into the model itself. Salesforce controls the weights and runs Koa within its own infrastructure, ensuring that no customer data crosses the trust boundary during inference.
Koa is already in use inside Salesforce, including an agent in Slack that helps employees find information and complete everyday tasks in Slack, and is now moving into customer pilots with 1-800Accountant, Baxter Credit Union (BCU), Engine, Formula 1, UChicago Medicine, and Xero.
“Accounting requires navigating tax rules, financial data, documents, and the unique circumstances of every customer. Koa gives our agents the reasoning to work through that complexity step by step and use the right tools along the way. That means we can extend more of our accountants’ expertise across every customer interaction and help people get to the right outcome faster.” — Ryan Teeples, Chief Strategy Officer, 1-800Accountant
“Our members come to us with goals, whether that’s buying a home, managing their money, or planning for what’s next. Koa can help our Digital agents understand the full complexity and context behind those goals and reason across the information, tools, and policies needed to move them forward. It gives us a powerful way to make every interaction more intelligent, personal, and useful.” — John Sahagian, SVP and Chief Data Officer, Baxter Credit Union
“At Engine, we’re building the future of business travel, and that starts with equipping our teams to deliver exceptional service. Business travel has countless moving parts, and what we need from AI isn’t a model that sounds confident — it’s one that can reason precisely through complex, multi-step problems. Collaborating with Salesforce and NVIDIA on a reasoning model purpose-built for Agentforce lets us push that vision further, faster.” — Elia Wallen, Founder and CEO, Engine
“Some of the most important work in healthcare happens behind the scenes, coordinating information, navigating complex processes, and making sure the right next step happens at the right time. Koa can work across those longer, multi-step workflows and help our teams manage that complexity more effectively. That creates more time and capacity for what matters most, caring for patients.” — Andrew Chang, Chief Marketing Officer, UChicago Medicine
					Related
								Why We Post-Trained Our Own Reasoning Model
				6 min read
								Salesforce Expands Missionforce with Purpose-Built AI and New Partnership with OpenAI to Advance Mission Intelligence
				4 min read
Mission-specific intelligence
For many government and highly regulated organizations to deploy AI, they must control the model and training data and deploy in specialized environments — private clouds, classified networks, and fully air-gapped systems — that never touch public infrastructure.
Salesforce is bringing NVIDIA models and accelerated computing into Missionforce to enable customers in highly sensitive industries to train, tune, and deploy mission-specific models on their own critical data.
Post-trained NVIDIA models will power agents for Missionforce Operations, a product that digitizes and automates complex government workflows, including procurement, supplier management, and logistics. Trained on an organization’s operational data and terminology, these specialized models enable agents to reason through back-office processes and act within the customer’s environment, including air-gapped networks. The companies are also working to bring post-trained NVIDIA models into additional Missionforce capabilities to enable customers to build and run models on their own infrastructure for specialized workloads.
Availability
Koa: Available to select pilot customers now in Agentforce; general availability expected winter 2026 in U.S. regions.
Missionforce Operations: Product generally available now in U.S. regions. Post-trained NVIDIA models available to select customers in October 2026.

Salesforce helps organizations of any size become agentic enterprises — integrating humans, agents, apps, and data on a trusted, unified platform to unlock unprecedented growth and innovation. Visit www.salesforce.com for more information.

documents.title: Siemens and Salesforce Deepen AI Partnership to Redefine Industrial Sales and Service
documents.raw_text:
Salesforce Partners
			Siemens and Salesforce Deepen AI Partnership to Redefine Industrial Sales and Service
			September 15, 2026
			4 min read
		Media Library
Siemens’ Teamcenter will work with Agentforce to bring engineering-grade answers directly into sales, service, and customer workflows.
Agentforce qualifies every inbound lead for Siemens’ 18,000 sellers, converting inbound interest into productive sales conversations and revenue growth.
SAN FRANCISCO — September 15, 2026 — Today at Dreamforce, Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the #1 AI CRM, and Siemens (SIEGY), a leading technology company focused on industry, infrastructure, mobility, and healthcare, announced a new chapter in their partnership: by combining Agentforce with Siemens’ Teamcenter Service Lifecycle Management (SLM), Siemens and Salesforce are helping industrial companies become agentic enterprises at scale — putting engineering-grade answers directly into sales, service, and customer workflows.
Agent-to-agent AI is transforming industrial service
The result is a new level of industrial intelligence in the front office. Questions that once had to go back to engineering can now be answered in seconds, directly in the customer workflow. A service technician can identify the right spare parts for a specific serial number before the first site visit. A sales representative can quote only those upgrades that are technically valid and manufacturable. And a customer can find and order the right part without waiting for an engineer or calling a hotline.
“Siemens and Salesforce are showing what it means to become an agentic enterprise at industrial scale,” said Marc Benioff, Chair and CEO of Salesforce. “We’re bringing the best of our technology, expertise, and industry knowledge together to reinvent how work gets done and how customers are served. This is a blueprint for the AI era: deep collaboration that goes beyond connecting technology to accelerate transformation, unlock new growth, and create entirely new value for customers.”
“For decades, the expert knowledge of the engineer has been separate from the person servicing the machine in the field. We are closing an important gap,” said Roland Busch, President and CEO of Siemens AG. “By embedding our digital twin into the commercial workflow, we are putting a virtual engineer in the hands of service technicians and salespersons. Siemens brings industrial AI, Salesforce enterprise AI. Together, they create a critical building block for an industrial AI operating system that connects engineering, operations and business.”
For manufacturers, the impact of this agent-to-agent connection is immediate and transformative.
The ability to compress processes from weeks to hours unlocks faster service, more reliable quoting, and new opportunities to grow aftermarket revenue – a business that grows around six times faster and carries roughly four times the margin of new equipment sales, according to industry analysis. By connecting product truth with customer context, Siemens and Salesforce help manufacturers move beyond one-time equipment sales toward deeper customer relationships, and lay the foundation for predictive, performance-based service models.
From thousands of unqualified leads to total engagement
Siemens has also deployed Agentforce, modernizing its inbound sales development with AI agents. This gives customers greater flexibility in how they buy through AIforce, a trusted enterprise AI harness that brings the whole of Salesforce — the data, workflows, business logic, actions, and governance — into every agentic interface.
Siemens received over 2,500 unqualified leads a month and had no way of knowing which ones were worth sellers’ time; it turned to Agentforce to convert more inbound interest into productive sales conversations at scale for 18,000 sellers. The leads flow into Sales Cloud, where they are engaged, assessed, and routed by two AI agents working in tandem: an engagement agent and a qualification agent. The engagement agent reaches out to incoming leads and moves interested prospects to the qualification agent, which vets each one before handing off the strongest opportunities to the appropriate seller.
The engagement agent uses CRM data to personalize email outreach, and each email contains a secure public key that identifies the lead without exposing their internal record ID. When the prospect follows the qualification link, that key lets the qualification agent retrieve their sales record, confirm or add information, and save details like budget and timeline needs as the conversation progresses. Today, Siemens engages 100% of these inbound leads across 132 countries.

								Salesforce Unveils AIforce, Bringing the Full Power of Its Platform to Any Interface
				7 min read
Streamlining partner onboarding
Siemens’ global partner ecosystem faces a common bottleneck: Prospective distributors search the company’s site, fill out an intake form, and wait for further outreach. Looking ahead, Piper, an AI SDR agent, will eliminate that wait, building a personalized pitch on the spot and booking qualified partners directly with a partner account manager.
Once a partner signs on, an employee will hand off a new supplier to Slackbot, which will orchestrate onboarding behind the scenes — running certification, financial, and risk checks and surfacing decisions in Slack — while Agentforce Operations, powered by Regrello, will handle the final onboarding steps in SAP, no human clicks required. The result: supplier onboarding will be orchestrated end-to-end, simplifying the process from weeks to days.

Salesforce Partners
			Salesforce and Anthropic Announce Claudeforce: The #1 AI Meets the #1 AI CRM
			August 26, 2026
			5 min read
		Media Library
Expanded partnership brings Claude’s reasoning together with the data, workflows, business logic, actions, and governance of the Salesforce platform to power trusted enterprise action directly in Claude
SAN FRANCISCO, August 26, 2026 — Salesforce and Anthropic are announcing Claudeforce, an expanded strategic partnership bringing Claude’s intelligence and reasoning together with Salesforce’s trusted enterprise harness to make its data, workflows, business logic, actions, and governance securely accessible to power agentic experiences wherever work happens.
The Claudeforce partnership launches with Salesforce in Claude, a Plugin with 37 prebuilt sales skills that enable sellers and agents to reason over live revenue context, automate pipeline updates, and take governed action right from Claude — with the power of Salesforce directly where sellers work. The companies plan to introduce more integrations across Claude, Salesforce, and Slack, expanding each company’s use of the other’s technologies.
Salesforce in Claude is made possible by AIforce — Salesforce’s trusted enterprise harness that brings all your business data and workflows to any agent through MCP servers, APIs, and CLI tools, without complicated and costly integrations. Salesforce in Claude marks a new era of enterprise AI. For decades, enterprise software required users to manually navigate static UI to get work done. Now that agents can access the data, workflows, and rules directly, software is a system that powers every interface.
“We’re bringing together the world’s #1 AI and #1 CRM — the best of both worlds. Today, we’re launching Claudeforce, running directly on top of Salesforce via our new AIforce UI harness, Headless 360, Data 360, Tableau, and Slack. Here, the UI is the AI — allowing you to build custom apps dynamically and answer any enterprise question. Probabilistic intelligence alone doesn’t run a company, and deterministic systems don’t reason. By fusing Claude’s extraordinary reasoning with the trusted data, workflows, and governance every enterprise runs on, we’re delivering a dynamic interface that thinks, reasons, and acts. This is how every business will run.” – Marc Benioff, Chair & CEO, Salesforce
“We believe frontier intelligence should be safe, trusted, and deeply capable, which is why the world’s leading businesses turn to Claude for their most important work. Salesforce in Claude brings this same frontier intelligence into the systems where much of the world’s commercial activity happens. Through this partnership, companies can point Claude at the customer information and business context that they’ve been building in Salesforce for decades, and use it to actually run and grow their businesses.”  – Dario Amodei, CEO & Co-Founder, Anthropic
One partnership, intertwining AI built with data built on trust
The Claudeforce partnership brings together the best of both worlds — Claude brings intelligence and judgment, reasoning, adapting, and deciding in real time. Salesforce provides the data, rules, and trusted workflows that turn that judgment into enterprise-ready action. The partnership contains:
1. Salesforce inside Claude
The Claudeforce partnership launches with Salesforce in Claude, a Plugin that understands the sellers’ entire revenue cycle and acts on it, giving them an AI CRO —  with 37 prebuilt sales skills including meeting prep, deal health review, and pipeline review.
These skills were built by Salesforce and Anthropic, engineered specifically to draw on Claude’s reasoning, agentic tool use, and generative UI — not generic CRM prompts wrapped around an API but the capabilities that extend what Claude can do. This includes an onboarding experience that reads a seller’s enterprise context — Salesforce, Slack, and any connector in Claude — to stand up a tailored dashboard with their accounts, pipeline, and live data surfaced in interactive views Claude generates.
No two companies run sales exactly the same, so Salesforce in Claude routes actions through Salesforce to help ensure business rules are always enforced when an action is taken. Setup is seamless. An admin connects Salesforce in Claude a single time, with authentication and permissions managed centrally, and every seller on the team gets access from day one — no per-user setup, no new permissions model to build, no re-auditing account by account.
2. Claude inside Salesforce
Claude combines multistep reasoning and complex task execution with Anthropic’s rigorous approach to safety and interpretability. Claude is available in Agentforce — serving as a reasoning model for the Atlas Reasoning Engine, powering Agentforce Vibes and Agentforce Coworker by default, and available in Agent Builder.
Through Amazon Bedrock, Claude is available within the Salesforce Trust Boundary, allowing customers, including those in regulated industries, to deploy domain-specific AI while keeping data and AI workloads secure.
					Related
								Salesforce Agentic Enterprise Index: Agent Deployments More Than Double Year over Year
				9 min read
								How Much Free Will Should Your AI Agents Have?
				7 min read
3. Slack: Where humans and agents work together
Slack, the multiplayer work OS, brings people and agents together in the flow of work. By embedding Claude directly into Slack — the central workspace where teams already operate — Salesforce is bridging the gap between team dialogue and autonomous enterprise action.
Through this expanded partnership, Claude is the default model for Slack and serves as the intelligent backbone across every layer of the Slack experience: powering Slackbot to supercharge personal productivity by default, augmenting team decision-making via Claude Tag, and accelerating multiplayer coding as a founding partner for Slack Code. Rather than managing disparate tools, teams can now reason through complex decisions alongside Claude in Slack and instantly execute governed, high-value actions in Salesforce — all without ever leaving the flow of work.
4. A partnership built on mutual adoption
Salesforce and Anthropic are also strategic customers of one another. This reciprocal adoption makes each company both a builder and a customer of the hybrid architecture they are bringing to market together.
Salesforce is Anthropic’s preferred CRM and connects communication, workflows, and agents through Slack, its preferred multi-player work platform for internal teams. Salesforce Shield, Backup, and Sandboxes support security, resilience, and development. Building on that foundation, new capabilities, spanning headless experiences, connected data, and automation, will power stronger scale across customer engagement.
Claude is the AI model powering Slackbot for Salesforce customers and employees. Internally, Slackbot has transformed how Salesforce employees work, with Slackbot driving 8.1M hours of annualized productivity gains, up over 2x quarter-over-quarter. Claude is the default model for Slack AI, Slackbot, Salesforce in Claude, Headless 360, Agentforce Coworker, and Claude Code across Salesforce’s engineering organization. Salesforce will make Claude Code and Claude Enterprise available to all of its developers and knowledge workers as the company’s preferred AI assistant and productivity tools, and Claude is the first LLM provider fully integrated within the Salesforce Trust Boundary.
Availability
Salesforce in Claude is available to select pilot customers now and expects to launch in open beta in September 2026.
Additional prebuilt skills will begin launching in late 2026.
About Salesforce
Salesforce helps organizations of any size become Agentic Enterprises — integrating humans, agents, apps, and data on a trusted, unified platform to unlock unprecedented growth and innovation. Visit www.salesforce.com for more information.
About Anthropic
Anthropic is a frontier AI company whose mission is to steer the trajectory of AI to advance human progress. We are best known for building Claude, the intelligence platform trusted by millions of people and businesses worldwide. Anthropic is a public benefit corporation — a for-profit committed to operating in service of social and public good — and controlled by a Long Term Benefit Trust, a group of independent experts in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise.
Pricing and packaging are subject to change. Availability may vary by region and is governed by customer agreements. Customers should base purchasing decisions on products and services currently available.

UPDATE
                        October 15, 2026
        Open up to new possibilities with iPhone Duo
                    Pre-orders begin Friday, October 16
                Starting this Friday, customers can pre-order iPhone Duo — featuring a foldable design — along with beautiful new accessories.
                 Beginning Friday, October 16, at 5 a.m. PT, customers can pre-order iPhone Duo on apple.com and in the Apple Store app.
                 iPhone Duo delivers Apple’s largest iPhone display ever in a foldable design. Opened, it is the thinnest iPhone ever, with an inner display that is 50 percent larger than the display on iPhone 18 Pro Max — providing a large canvas for viewing content, gaming, and multitasking. Closed, the 5.4-inch outer display delivers 90 percent of the screen area of iPhone 18 Pro in a compact, pocketable design.1 iPhone Duo is also built to last and features a precision-engineered hinge that offers a smooth, satisfying feel with every use. Powered by A20 Pro, iPhone Duo delivers pro performance along with a dual-battery architecture for impressive all-day battery life. iOS 27 is reimagined, remaining familiar and intuitive while adapting to the versatile ways users can interact with iPhone Duo. And with Siri AI,2 powered by Apple Intelligence,3 iPhone Duo also brings powerful AI capabilities together with a user’s personal context to become an intelligent personal hub with privacy and security at its core.
                 Customers shopping in-store or online for iPhone Duo can connect with Apple Specialists for personalized support and get assistance with ways to save and pay, including leasing with Apple Upgrade,4 financing options, and carrier deals, as well as learn how to protect their products with AppleCare+ or AppleCare One. Customers can also take advantage of convenient home delivery or arrange for pickup at their local Apple Store at a time most suitable for them.
                Closed, iPhone Duo delivers 90 percent of the screen area of iPhone 18 Pro in a pocketable design. Opened, it showcases Apple’s largest-ever iPhone display.
                 Ways to Save Directly with Apple
                 Upgrading to iPhone Duo is incredibly simple with a variety of flexible payment options. Customers can choose from great leasing and financing options or select one of the exceptional carrier deals — and since iPhone retains its value longer than other smartphones, they can maximize their savings through Apple Trade In.5
                 Apple Trade In
Trading in a current device is a great way to save on iPhone Duo. With Apple Trade In, customers can receive an instant credit ranging from $175 to $885 when trading in an eligible iPhone 13 or higher. That credit can then be used to lower their monthly payments across Apple Upgrade, Apple Card Monthly Installments,6 or one of the incredible carrier deals.
                                With great financing options, customers can save by shopping directly with Apple. They can also trade in an eligible device and receive instant credit.
                 Apple Upgrade
With Apple Upgrade, provided by Klarna, it’s easy for customers to get their hands on iPhone Duo with a lease term that’s best for them. Apple Upgrade offers 12- and 24-month leasing options for iPhone, with prices starting as low as $57.99 (excluding taxes and any trade-in credit) per month for a 24-month lease for iPhone Duo. At the end of their lease term, eligible customers can upgrade their device to the latest generation, purchase it with a one-time payment, or simply return it and exit the program.
                 More Value with Carrier Deals Directly with Apple
Apple partners with the major wireless carriers to offer incredible deals, including up to $1,200 in credit toward iPhone Duo when trading in iPhone 14 Pro Max or higher.7 Customers can activate their new phone with AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon — all in one place.
                 Apple Card Monthly Installments
In the U.S., Apple Card customers can pay for their new devices over time at 0 percent APR when they choose to check out with Apple Card Monthly Installments at Apple and earn 3 percent Daily Cash back all up front. It takes as little as a minute for customers to apply for Apple Card and start using it right away.† Tracking payments is just as simple, with installments automatically grouped into one easy-to-manage balance in the Wallet app.
                 Explore iPhone Duo
                 iPhone Duo features an advanced camera system that enables all-new experiences made possible by its breakthrough design. The 48MP Fusion Main camera shoots sharp photos with zero shutter lag, and users can get closer to the subject with an integrated optical-quality 2x Telephoto. The 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera captures wider fields of view and enables macro photography, while the Center Stage front camera can automatically take photos and videos in any orientation, so users don’t have to rotate iPhone for landscape selfies. A new FaceTime camera placed underneath the inner display helps users connect with friends and family, whether iPhone Duo is held open or propped on a surface for hands-free calls.
                 The expansive display on iPhone Duo supercharges productivity with Split View multitasking and seamless app switching, and a reimagined yet familiar iOS experience introduces entirely new ways to interact with iPhone. iOS also adapts to content on iPhone Duo by reacting as it folds, reorienting when turned to the side, and switching to the appropriate display when flipped over. iPhone Duo can also enter StandBy on either the outer or inner display — even when it’s not charging — turning the device into a photo frame, a hub for widgets, a clock, and more.
                                    The expansive display on iPhone Duo enables Split View multitasking and seamless app switching for supercharged productivity.
                                    Content reacts as iPhone Duo folds, reorients when it’s turned to the side, and switches to the appropriate display when it’s flipped over.
                                    iPhone Duo can enter StandBy on either the inner or outer display and transform into a photo frame, a hub for widgets, a clock, and more.
                 Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence — profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational, with personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, and onscreen awareness to help users find what they need and get things done. Rolling out in beta in English with iOS 27, Siri AI is even more useful on the large inner display, where iPhone Duo users can keep Siri open alongside an app and ask about what’s onscreen. And with Siri mode in Camera, users can get information and take action on what’s in front of them.
                 iPhone Duo is splash-, water-, and dust-resistant with an IP68 rating,8 and is available in two refined colors: star white and night sky.
                iPhone Duo customers can choose between two refined colors: star white and night sky.
                 Get Ready to Upgrade with Apple
                 Getting ready early is the best way to secure the new iPhone Duo. Right now, customers can configure their device, choose accessories, secure leasing or financing pre-approval, and arrange their trade-in ahead of the availability-day rush. By saving these choices to their shopping bag before 9 p.m. PT on Thursday, October 15, they are able to check out with a single click the moment pre-orders go live at 5 a.m. PT on Friday, October 16.
                 Customers get the very best of Apple when shopping directly online or in-store. Knowledgeable Specialists can provide personalized guidance from start to finish on everything from discovering the latest trade-in offers and additional ways to save, to safely and securely transferring data with Personal Setup. Customers can also discover how to go further with their new devices through free Today at Apple sessions. With updated offerings like “Say Hello to iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo” and “Tips: What’s New on iOS 27,” these hands-on classes are the ultimate way to explore the capabilities of the latest products.
                 Designed for iPhone Duo
                 To complement iPhone Duo, Apple is introducing beautiful new accessories. The iPhone Duo Folio — available in navy blue and taupe — features an integrated kickstand that supports a wide range of angles for reading, viewing content, or FaceTime, and folds away neatly when not in use. The iPhone Duo Case — available in sand and navy blue — is thin and light, with a protective two-part design that wraps around both sides of the device. Both cases are compatible with MagSafe, Qi2 25W, and Qi-certified chargers. With built-in magnets that align perfectly with iPhone Duo, they offer a magical attach experience and fast wireless charging.
                                    Available in taupe and navy blue, the iPhone Duo Folio features a kickstand that supports a wide range of angles.
                                    Available in taupe and navy blue, the iPhone Duo Folio features a kickstand that supports a wide range of angles.
                                    The light yet protective iPhone Duo Case comes in complementary sand and navy blue options.
                                    The light yet protective iPhone Duo Case comes in complementary sand and navy blue options.
                 Protection for Every Product
                 AppleCare plans protect a user’s new iPhone Duo from accidents like drops and spills and, in many regions, theft and loss too — all at a great value.9 In available markets,10 customers can choose AppleCare+ or AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss for their new iPhone Duo. AppleCare One Individual, where offered, provides the same benefits as AppleCare+ with Theft and Loss, at the same monthly price — but extends coverage to two more devices. Customers in the U.S. can also choose AppleCare One Family to cover every eligible Apple product across their Family Sharing group, with new purchases, upgrades, and devices the family already owns covered automatically at no additional cost.11 Learn more at apple.com/applecare or in Settings on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.
                                With AppleCare One Family, customers in the U.S. can protect their new iPhone Duo as well as every eligible Apple product in their Family Sharing group.
                 Try Apple One
                 New and qualified returning subscribers who purchase iPhone Duo can unlock three months of Apple One for free. Apple One bundles up to six Apple services — including Apple TV, Apple Music, up to 2TB of iCloud+ storage, and more — into one convenient plan across multiple Apple devices.‡

documents.title: Bünyamin Aydın’s new collection, “From Earth to Sky,” soars with iPad Pro
documents.raw_text:
apple stories
                                        Bünyamin Aydın’s new collection, “From Earth to Sky,” soars with iPad Pro
                                The Les Benjamins designer brought together Turkish heritage, 1970s rock ’n’ roll influences, and futurism for a landmark fashion show in Cappadocia shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max
                    Download Video
                    “From Earth to Sky” celebrates 15 years of the Istanbul-based lifestyle brand Les Benjamins, bringing together Anatolian heritage, avant-garde design, and the magic of iPad Pro with Apple Pencil Pro.
                    creatives
                        October 14, 2026
                 Long before the sun rises in Cappadocia, Türkiye’s Rose Valley is already awake. Crews are on the move, models refresh their makeup, and three giant hot-air balloons — neon green, yellow, and pink — float above a landscape that looks like it belongs on Mars.
                 The scene is set for Les Benjamins designer Bünyamin Aydın’s most ambitious project yet. “From Earth to Sky” celebrates 15 years of the Istanbul-based lifestyle brand and brings together Anatolian heritage, avant-garde design, and the magic of iPad Pro with Apple Pencil Pro. Shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max by French filmmaker Neels Castillon, this fashion show is like no other.
                 The project began to take shape during a research trip to Cappadocia in early 2026. Aydın used iPad Pro and Apple Pencil Pro, alongside iPhone 17 Pro Max to record the extraordinary terrain, shooting photographs and 4K video at 60 fps.
                     Native flowers Bünyamin Aydın encountered in Cappadocia, Türkiye’s Rose Valley became the heart of his latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.
                     Native flowers Bünyamin Aydın encountered in Cappadocia, Türkiye’s Rose Valley became the heart of his latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.
                 Aydın’s creative process seldom takes place behind a desk, so he appreciates the flexibility iPad Pro offers with its thin, light form factor and battery life that can last him up to two days. “It’s the ultimate workstation on the go,” Aydın says. “That gives me freedom.”
                 Three native flowers he encountered in the region — spiky green Echinops, flutelike pink trumpets, and wild yellow tulips — became the heart of this latest collection, inspiring 10 striking looks and three custom-built hot-air balloons.
                 For Aydın, Les Benjamins represents the intersection of people and their cultures, and “From Earth to Sky” is no different. Born in Germany, the designer was raised with what he describes as “German discipline and Turkish heart” — a duality that runs through his work. “The canvas is the West; the paint is the East,” he says of a collection that combines contemporary silhouettes with Turkish fabrics and Silk Road influences.
                 iPad Pro with the powerful M5 chip became the creative nexus for the entire project. After research trips, Aydın would assemble photographs, fabric references, and early designs in the Freeform app, where evolving mood boards could be easily shared or exported to keep work ticking along. “Freeform allowed me to bring my team into my creative journey instead of simply giving them finished ideas,” he says.
                 The multitasking features on iPad Pro became integral as the workflows multiplied. Aydın could use its intuitive windowing system to work on an active sketch in Procreate, refer to photos from his travels, and research local flora in Safari, all while Background Tasks exported files for his collaborators.
                                iPad Pro with M5 became the project’s creative nexus, allowing Aydın (left) to assemble photographs, fabric references, and early designs in the Freeform app and share mood boards with his team.
                 And then there were the hot-air balloons. Working in Procreate, Aydın and his team designed a single structure as a starting point, then rapidly duplicated, altered, and redrew it until three final forms emerged from dozens of variations.
                 To bring the designs to life, Aydın collaborated with Pasha Balloons, one of Cappadocia’s hot-air balloon pioneers. “I would send my sketches to them, and they would use their engineering know-how to make sure they could actually fly,” he says with a smile. These technical drawings would then go straight back into Procreate for review and refinement.
                 Finding the right colors was vital. In addition to the electric hues of the balloons, Aydın also worked with cream, blue, and natural tones. “These are the colors of the earth and the sky,” he explains. The Ultra Retina XDR display on iPad Pro — which uses tandem OLED technology — became a key tool, while True Tone helped Aydın achieve the saturation he wanted, regardless of ambient lighting.
            We were working on high‑resolution images, creating multiple layers and playing with textures. That’s usually when things start to slow down. But that never happened on iPad Pro. It felt just like working on a desktop.
            Bünyamin Aydın, Les Benjamins designer
                Using iPad Pro and Apple Pencil Pro, Aydın designed the show’s colorful hot-air balloons in Procreate.
                 Apple Pencil Pro helped draw the line from idea to iterative design. “Working with regular pen and paper feels very natural, but the hover feature on Apple Pencil Pro lets me preview every stroke before I even make it, so I can see any mistakes beforehand,” he says. “It’s like a supernatural tool.”
                 An avid gamer, Aydın compares his relationship with Apple Pencil Pro to the muscle memory he developed while playing his favorite titles. Squeezing, double-tapping, and switching to the eraser now feel like reflexive actions, which enabled him to move quickly through variations without the tool interrupting the idea. And the low latency made the creative experience feel more immersive and responsive than ever.
                 “We were working on high-resolution images, creating multiple layers and playing with textures. That’s usually when things start to slow down,” he says. “But that never happened on iPad Pro. It felt just like working on a desktop.”
                To bring the hot-air balloons to life, Aydın and his team collaborated with Pasha Balloons, one of Cappadocia’s ballooning pioneers.
                “The canvas is the West; the paint is the East,” Aydın (right) says of a collection that combines contemporary silhouettes with Turkish fabrics and influences gathered along the Silk Road.
                 Back in Rose Valley, months of planning and work are finally coming to life.
                 Even before the sun touches the horizon, Castillon’s iPhone 18 Pro Max is already rolling. Three runways, gigantic hot-air balloons, and natural light that continues to change with every passing minute mean there is little room for error.
                 The new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture allows Castillon to begin filming in low light before narrowing the aperture as the sun comes up. Camera operators use Pro controls like histogram and white balance to keep the look consistent across multiple cameras as the sky changes from pink to blue.
                 Working with iPhone 18 Pro Max brings the immediacy Castillon loves as a director. “When I see something beautiful, I want to film it right away,” he says. The A20 Pro chip and improved thermal management also give the production the sustained performance and reliability it needs to capture heavy 4K video throughout the event.
                 Just as Aydın’s show travels from past to future, movement drives Castillon’s visual treatment. Custom-built drones each carry two iPhone 18 Pro Max models, with their 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide cameras focused on enhancing the sense of vertiginous speed while fitting the massive balloons into frame.
                 Footage captured at 4K 120 fps allows Castillon to highlight elements like rippling fabric in cinematic slow motion, while a slower shutter speed turns quick drone passes into a painterly impressionistic motion blur.
                Aydın also worked with French filmmaker Neels Castillon, who captured footage of the new collection using iPhone 18 Pro Max.
                 Castillon’s treatment also creates a dreamlike, psychedelic look. He uses ProRes RAW to preserve flexibility for color grading in post-production, as Cappadocia’s pale hues meet saturated pinks, yellows, and greens. “I’m a huge nerd for color, and the tones are really accurate on iPad Pro,” he says.
                 While his team records video, Castillon shoots stills with the 48MP Fusion Main camera, using the new texture and grain controls in Photographic Styles 3 to bring some of the tactile character he loves in analog photography into the images.
                 As feeds from the whirling drones come into Castillon’s production control center, synchronizing them begins right there on location. He reviews footage and makes selections on MacBook Pro with M4 Max; its nano-texture display helps reduce glare from the sun overhead.
                 With the performance in full swing, Castillon’s focus switches from crane to drone to capture the opening look: a Turkish caftan and a tree branch representing Anatolia, an homage to Turkish rock icon Barış Manço. The show’s scale is huge, but Aydın believes its potential is larger still.
                 For him, “From Earth to Sky” is a chance to bring Turkish culture to a global audience without losing sight of its roots. “I see my role as that of a translator and a bridge between East and West,” Aydın says. “I hope this project makes Turkish people proud.”
                 “From Earth to Sky” was shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max. Check it out on @apple beginning October 14.
                Aydın (center) poses with models at the Les Benjamins fashion show in Cappadocia, Türkiye.
