PRESS RELEASE
                        October 13, 2026
        Meet Apple HomeView, a new way to enjoy entertainment, stay connected, and manage the home
                    Apple HomeView is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI and built with privacy and security at its core
                            Powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, Apple HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place.
                 CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today introduced Apple HomeView, designed to be central to the home and personal to everyone in it. With a stunning 7-inch Liquid Retina display, HomeView brings entertainment, connection, and smart home management together in one place, from playing music and making FaceTime calls to home monitoring and hands-free automations with voice control — all designed with privacy and security at the core.1 HomeView recognizes users by their faces, adapting so they can access their personal content in Messages, FaceTime, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My. HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that’s profoundly more capable and conversational, with broad world knowledge that powers richer music discovery and onscreen awareness. When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled device, it can also draw on a user’s personal context, such as their Calendar, Messages, and relevant information across their apps, to provide more helpful, personalized responses.2
                 Designed to fit in any space, HomeView can be placed on a tabletop as the center of the home or wall-mounted to fit in spaces like the entryway or hallway. Pre-orders start today, with availability beginning November 13.
                 “Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” said Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of Worldwide Marketing. “It recognizes your face to shift from a household screen to your own experience, fills the room with incredible sound, keeps you connected to the people who matter most with FaceTime, and makes it easy to control your smart home. And it’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure.”
                                    HomeView brings people together around one shared experience, while recognizing each user and adapting to them privately.
                                    HomeView brings people together around one shared experience, while recognizing each user and adapting to them privately.
                                    HomeView brings people together around one shared experience, while recognizing each user and adapting to them privately.
                 Elegantly Designed for Any Space
                 HomeView features a beautiful aluminum design with a 7-inch Liquid Retina display connected to a domed speaker base by a stainless steel hinge that provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height. The perfect addition to a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table, HomeView comes in four beautiful colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — each finished with a matching cable.
                                    HomeView is available in four beautiful colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.
                                    A Liquid Retina display connected to a domed base by a stainless steel hinge provides a smooth tilt for comfortable viewing on tabletops of any height.
                                    HomeView comes with a color-matched USB-C cable.
                 The elegant design and Liquid Retina display seamlessly blend into any space while remaining clearly visible from across the room. It features adaptive display technologies, including True Tone, that react to changing light throughout the day. Automatic brightness adjusts from 500 nits — bright enough to stay vivid and easy to see even in a sunlit room — down to just 0.3 nits, making it ideal for the nightstand. The HomeView interface intelligently adjusts based on the user’s distance, showing simpler information that’s viewable from across the room and richer detail as they step closer.
                 A separate wall-mounted HomeView model — available in space gray and silver — offers the same 7-inch Liquid Retina display, powerful set of features, and rich audio. It can be attached to a wall using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, with options for self-installation or professional installation.
                                Available in space gray and silver, the wall-mounted HomeView can be attached using three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home, extending the experience to more places.
                 A Personalized Experience for Each User in the Home
                 HomeView recognizes up to six people and delivers a personalized experience for each one. Each user gets their own personalized Home Screen with apps and widgets. Personal content stays private from others, while shared photo albums and music can be easily enjoyed by everyone in a household, including guests.
                                HomeView can recognize up to six users by their face, and each user can personalize their Home Screen apps and widgets.
                 Featuring Siri AI, Powered by Apple Intelligence
                 HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and advanced Apple silicon. Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding and onscreen awareness. With broad world knowledge, anyone in the home can ask Siri about virtually any topic and get an answer.
                HomeView features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri that is profoundly more capable and conversational.
                 With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information from Messages and Calendar, playlists on Apple Music, and more by drawing on their personal context. Users have the ability to customize the expressiveness and pace of Siri’s voice on their paired and compatible device so that it’s just right for them. That customization carries over to HomeView, allowing users to go back and forth with Siri in a conversation like never before.3 Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, which uses iCloud to privately sync history across a user’s products, so they can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.
                 With Siri AI built into HomeView, even users without an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad will benefit from Siri AI’s broad world knowledge; ability to have rich, natural conversations; and improved music discovery.
                                    With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, Siri AI does more for each person — taking action across apps and surfacing relevant information by drawing on each user’s personal context.
                                    Conversations that start on HomeView seamlessly continue in the Siri app, so users can pick up the conversation on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro.
                 With powerful new features and unrivaled privacy protections, Siri remains the world’s most private digital assistant.
                 Faces for Every Style
                 Users can personalize HomeView with a collection of playful and informative faces that display information at a glance, taking full advantage of the vibrant Liquid Retina display. The Photos face brings cherished memories to life with stunning Portrait-style depth effects that keep the subject sharp while creating a beautifully blurred foreground and background. By selecting a shared album, users can turn HomeView into a living photo frame that loved ones near and far can help fill. The Flow face dynamically responds to physical presence and movement, transforming HomeView into a piece of interactive art. And even Snoopy comes to life on HomeView, with animations that reflect the time of day, the weather, sporting events, and holiday moments.
                            Users can customize HomeView with a collection of playful faces that display useful information at a glance, taking full advantage of the Liquid Retina display.
                 Rich Entertainment Anywhere in the Home
                 HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system. Two custom full-range drivers in the display keep everything sounding crisp and clean while delivering room-filling Spatial Audio. A down-firing woofer and two force-cancelling passive radiators are built into the base, offering incredible bass extension. Powered by Apple silicon and real-time system sensors, advanced computational audio continuously optimizes loudness and bass response at any volume. The wall-mounted version delivers rich sound with two custom drivers and computational audio tuned specifically for on-wall placement.
                HomeView offers an exceptional listening experience through a custom-engineered acoustic system.
                 HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Music, complete with animated album art and lyrics, as well as Apple Podcasts, Apple News,4 Apple TV, and compatible third-party audio and video apps.5 With Handoff, users can continue listening to a song they were playing in the car or on a walk by placing their iPhone in front of the HomeView display. By setting up multiple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, and AirPlay-compatible speakers around the house, users can enjoy music throughout the entire home with multiroom audio.
                HomeView is the perfect way to enjoy Apple Podcasts and Apple Music.
                 Connecting Users to What Matters Most
                 HomeView makes it effortless for users to stay in touch and get things done around the house. FaceTime and Center Stage keep everyone framed perfectly, even when participants are moving around the room.6 Messages can be read and answered by voice or with the onscreen keyboard. Intercom lets users broadcast a quick message to a single room or the whole house — reaching other HomeView and HomePod speakers, as well as personal devices like iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch. In the kitchen, HomeView is the perfect sous chef, converting recipes from the web into step-by-step instructions with hands-free timer control and help with ingredient tracking, so users can stay focused on what’s cooking.
                                    HomeView makes it easy for users to communicate and get things done around the house, whether they’re hopping on a FaceTime call, looking up a recipe, or setting a timer hands-free.
                                    HomeView makes it easy for users to communicate and get things done around the house, whether they’re hopping on a FaceTime call, looking up a recipe, or setting a timer hands-free.
                                    HomeView makes it easy for users to communicate and get things done around the house, whether they’re hopping on a FaceTime call, looking up a recipe, or setting a timer hands-free.
                 With Find My, users can check in on loved ones who have shared their locations with them, or track down a misplaced iPhone, AirPods charging case, or personal item with an AirTag attached. And with Live Activities, HomeView surfaces timely, at-a-glance information, like the song that’s currently playing, an active timer, or an incoming Intercom message from another room.
                 The Ultimate Smart Home Dashboard
                 HomeView allows users to securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice using Siri AI — viewing camera feeds, adjusting the thermostat and lights, locking doors, or closing the blinds. The Home Modular face offers instant access to users’ favorite accessories, while the Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds at once, letting users keep an eye on doorstep deliveries and pets playing in the yard.
                With HomeView, users can securely control their smart home by touch or with just their voice by using Siri AI.
                 With a supported iCloud+ subscription, HomeView works with compatible cameras to deliver intelligent, end-to-end encrypted recognition of people, familiar faces, pets, packages, and vehicles, notifying the household the moment someone arrives at the front door. With video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video footage, HomeView helps users quickly understand what happened in a video clip without even watching it.7 Offering added peace of mind, HomeView also detects the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and alerts users on their iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.
                 HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — a new lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.8 Together, they help users understand what’s happening inside and outside, manage access, keep the home at just the right temperature, and so much more.9
                HomeView also works with Apple Home Collection — Apple’s first lineup of smart home cameras, thermostats, and a lock — as well as other Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories.
                 Private and Secure by Design
                 Like every Apple product, HomeView was built with privacy and security at its core. HomeView and the A18 chip include Secure Exclaves: protected and compartmentalized runtimes used to process camera and microphone data separately from the rest of the system. Isolation features added across many core components of the silicon work in tandem to protect Secure Exclaves and keep them segregated from the rest of the system. Data that is processed and analyzed in Secure Exclaves cannot be accessed by the HomeView software, apps, the user, or Apple. To ensure that personal content stays private to each individual, even when HomeView is shared by the whole household, content in apps like Messages and Calendar is only surfaced when the enrolled user is recognized by their face, and when their paired iPhone or iPad is present and has been recently unlocked.10
                 Siri requests on HomeView can use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, which extends the privacy of the device to the cloud. When processed in Private Cloud Compute, data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.
                 Apple HomeView and the Environment
                 HomeView was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. HomeView is made with 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure base and in the enclosure of the wall-mounted model, 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards, and 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets. HomeView meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based11 and designed to be recycled.
                 Pricing and Availability
Customers in Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, the UK, and the U.S. can pre-order Apple HomeView in silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray for $299 (U.S.), and Apple HomeView (Wall Mounted) in space gray and silver for $299 (U.S.), starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app. Customers in Singapore can pre-order starting Thursday, October 15, at 9 a.m. SGT. Both models will be available in these countries beginning Friday, November 13. Customers in South Africa will be able to pre-order Apple HomeView and Apple HomeView (Wall Mounted) through Apple Authorized Resellers, with availability beginning Friday, November 13. Apple HomeView is not available for sale in the European Union, as Siri AI is currently unavailable in iOS in the EU. Apple is working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward.
HomeView (Wall Mounted) will be available with a choice of three purpose-built mounts from Schneider Home. Power Mount USB‑C Wall Connector, available starting at $59.95 (U.S.), and Power Mount AC Wired, available starting at $79.95 (U.S.), can be ordered starting today from apple.com/store and in the Apple Store app. Power Mount PoE Wired will be available starting in early 2027 for $129.95 (U.S.).
Siri AI on HomeView is available in English in the U.S., Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK.
Canadian French-language support will be offered later via a free software update.

Sony Innovation Fund to Exhibit at CEATEC 2026
documents.raw_text:
Tokyo, Japan — Sony Group Corporation("Sony") today announced that it will exhibit at CEATEC 2026, which will be held from October 13 to 16, 2026, at Makuhari Messe in Chiba, Japan. The exhibit, themed "Where Ideas Grow Through Co-Creation," will showcase the activities of Sony Innovation Fund, which works with startups and other partners to co-create new businesses through investment and incubation.
Through Sony Innovation Fund, Sony invests in startups and promotes business development and incubation with the aim of creating new businesses. By connecting diverse ideas, technologies, and talent and nurturing their potential, Sony aims to contribute to the development of next-generation industries while aiming to create new experiences and new forms of inspiration.
At the CEATEC 2026, Sony will introduce its innovation support initiatives across the Sony Group, as well as companies that became independent from Sony Group with support from Sony Innovation Fund. Visitors will also be able to explore products and services from companies in which the Sony Innovation Fund has invested since its establishment in 2016. The exhibit highlights how ideas grow through co-creation and evolve into new businesses and sources of value.
	For more information, please visit the dedicated website.
	Rendering of the Sony booth
		Main Exhibits
		Sony Innovation Fund
	Sony Innovation Fund, Sony's corporate venture capital initiative, will highlight its investments in startups with innovative technologies, business models, services, and products that have the potential to shape the future. It will also present examples of business development support through internal incubation and business co-creation, together with the background to the initiative's establishment and its activities to date.
		Sony Acceleration Platform
	Sony Acceleration Platform supports innovation both within and outside Sony and facilitates collaboration with a wide range of partners. The exhibit will introduce an approach that combines the investment capabilities of Sony Innovation Fund with Sony Acceleration Platform's business development expertise to strengthen support for startups, from sourcing and identification through growth support.
		Exhibiting Startups　＊Listed in exhibition order
		augment AI Inc.
	augment AI Inc. was established as an independent company by the development team that led Sony's smartwatch business, following the transfer of related trademarks and patents from Sony Group. The company will showcase wena X, a next-generation smartwatch that has raised approximately 600 million yen through an ongoing crowdfunding campaign.
		Qoly Corporation
	Qoly Corporation carries forward certain technologies developed through Sony's medical robotics research.*1 The company develops, manufactures, sells, and provides support for microsurgery*2 assistance robots and related products. As an example of Sony's corporate incubation initiatives, Qoly will present its proprietary technologies and their potential for future development.
		*1Prototype microsurgery-assistance robot announced by Sony in 2024
		*2Microsurgery: A type of surgical procedure performed under a microscope to manipulate delicate tissues such as small blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatic vessels.
		YOAKE entertainment Co., Ltd.
	YOAKE entertainment Co., Ltd. operates IRC APP on Soneium, the blockchain developed by Sony Block Solutions Labs Pte. Ltd. The company will present its efforts to connect global fan communities in the entertainment sector and create new fan engagement experiences.
		Pictoria Inc.
	Pictoria Inc., which creates intellectual property and content by combining AI-based technologies with entertainment, will exhibit Picto STAND, an interactive digital signage system that enables conversations with AI characters.
		Litpla Inc.
	Litpla Inc. operates experiential entertainment facilities for children and families in Japan and overseas, including the next-generation theme park Little Planet. The company will introduce initiatives in the LBE*3 field developed through collaborations with Sony's entertainment businesses and Sony Innovation Fund. Visitors will also be able to experience interactive entertainment firsthand.
		*3LBE: Location-Based Entertainment
		LENZO, Inc.
	LENZO, Inc., a semiconductor startup focused on building next-generation computing infrastructure, will present a collaborative initiative combining Sony's high-performance CMOS image sensors with ultra-low-power AI semiconductors based on LENZO's proprietary CGLA architecture. The initiative aims to enable high-speed, real-time recognition and analysis at the edge.
		TIER IV, Inc.
	TIER IV, Inc., a deep-tech company leading the development of Autoware, an open-source software platform for autonomous driving, will showcase a collaborative use case featuring cameras equipped with Sony CMOS image sensors, optimized for Level 4 autonomous driving with seamless Autoware integration.

documents.title: Support for Communities and Individuals Affected by the Flash Floods and Mudslides in Nepal and China
documents.raw_text:
The Sony Group extends its deepest sympathies to all those affected by the flash floods and mudslides that occurred in Nepal and China on August 26, 2026.
	Sony Group Corporation and Sony Group companies in China will donate approximately 28 million yen in total to support relief efforts for communities and individuals affected by the disaster.
	This donation consists of RMB 1 million (approximately 23 million yen) contributed by Sony Group companies in China and USD 30,000 (approximately 5 million yen) from the "Emergency Disaster and Recovery Fund for Children,"*1 jointly operated by Sony Group Corporation and Save the Children Japan.
	The Sony Group sends its sincerest condolences to all those affected and wishes for a full and swift recovery for the region.
		*1:For more information on the "Emergency Disaster and Recovery Fund for Children," please visit the following website.
Sony Group Portal - Emergency Disaster and Recovery Fund for Children

documents.title: Further Support for Communities and Individuals Affected by the 2026 Kumamoto Earthquake
documents.raw_text:
The Sony Group is providing additional donations to support relief efforts for the communities and individuals affected by the earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture in Japan on July 28, 2026.
	As announced on July 30, the Sony Group donated 50 million yen as emergency relief for affected communities and individuals through a fund*1 jointly operated with Save the Children Japan and through the Japanese Red Cross Society. *2
	Subsequently, the Sony Group has collected donations from employees in Japan and overseas, and the total amount has reached approximately 28 million yen as of September 4. Combining these employee donations with matching donations of 28 million yen from the Sony Group, support from Sony Group companies, and the previously announced 50 million yen, the total support will amount to approximately 110 million yen. These additional donations will be provided to Save the Children Japan, the Japanese Red Cross Society, and other organizations.
	The Sony Group sends its sincerest condolences to all those affected and wishes for a full and swift recovery for the region.
		*1：For more information on the "Emergency Disaster and Recovery Fund for Children," please visit the following website.
Sony Group Portal - Emergency Disaster and Recovery Fund for Children
		*2：Donations through the Japanese Red Cross Society are remitted in full to the donation distribution committees established by the affected prefectures to support the livelihoods of people in the disaster-affected areas.

Contribution to support earthquake relief
          SPRING, Texas – ExxonMobil today announced a $500,000 donation to the American Red Cross to support relief efforts following the June 2026 earthquakes in Venezuela.
The contribution will support the American Red Cross and its global Red Cross network as they provide critical assistance to communities impacted by the disaster. The organizations will use the funds to address urgent humanitarian needs and support recovery efforts where help is needed most.
“Our thoughts are with the people and communities affected by the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela,” said Alvin Abraham, global manager of corporate giving at ExxonMobil. “Our contribution aims to help ensure affected communities receive the care and resources they need.”
Donations to the American Red Cross designated for Venezuela earthquake relief efforts will provide a range of support services, including emergency shelter, relief supplies, cash assistance, health care, safe water and sanitation, psychosocial support, family reunification services, and other recovery assistance for people impacted by the earthquakes. ExxonMobil commends the first responders, volunteers, and community leaders working tirelessly on the ground to support relief efforts.

documents.raw_text:
Press Release
                            Visa Direct Launches Stablecoin-Powered Money Movement as Pilots Move to Production
                        Inyo Global becomes the first enabler to bring Visa Direct's stablecoin-enabled prefunding into production, making stablecoin-powered money movement available for businesses that run cross-border payments through Visa Direct.
                10/15/2026
    SAN FRANCISCO — Today, Visa (NYSE: V) announced the next phase of its stablecoin strategy as Visa Direct stablecoin capabilities advance from pilot stage to commercial deployment. The milestone marks an important step in bringing stablecoin-enabled money movement into real-world commercial operations. In the initial rollout, Inyo Global, a Visa Direct processor, is the first enabler of this new offering, powering it for eligible Visa Direct clients and partners.¹
Over the past year, Visa Direct has worked with clients and partners to explore how stablecoins can help improve the way businesses fund and move money across borders. As interest in faster, more flexible just-in-time funding solutions continues to grow, Visa is now seeing those efforts move beyond experimentation and into day-to-day business operations.
As part of this next phase, Visa is working with Inyo Global, a payments infrastructure provider serving money transmitters, fintechs, banks and payment businesses, to bring Visa Direct's stablecoin-enabled prefunding to market. Inyo has integrated the capability into its platform, giving the businesses it serves the option to prefund cross-border payouts through Visa Direct with USDC in near real time, rather than relying solely on traditional funding windows.²
Through a single connection, Inyo's platform lets businesses onboard users, manage fraud and compliance, accept payments and send domestic and international payouts across more than 180 countries, powered by Visa Direct.
"The next chapter for stablecoins is adoption," said Vira Platonova, Global Head of Visa Direct. "Over the last several years, we've worked with several partners and clients to explore how these technologies can improve money movement. We're now seeing those efforts translate into live implementations, helping businesses access more flexible and efficient ways to fund and move money globally through Visa Direct, starting with Inyo Global as our first enabler."
Visa Direct Head Vira Platonova will discuss how stablecoins are reshaping global money movement during several Money20/20 USA sessions next week.
From Pilot to Production
ln 2025, Visa introduced stablecoin prefunding and payout pilot programs through Visa Direct.
The pilots demonstrated how stablecoins could support cross-border funding, liquidity management and global money movement for eligible clients.
Today, those capabilities are moving from pilot programs and into real-world commercial operations.
Inyo Global is the first enabler to bring Visa Direct's stablecoin prefunding capability into commercial production.
"Innovation in money movement is ultimately about creating a better experience for customers, and that's exactly our focus at Inyo," said Robson Dantas, Chief Product and Technology Officer and co-founder at Inyo Global. "By integrating Visa Direct's stablecoin-enabled prefunding into the Inyo platform, we're giving the money transmitters, fintechs and payment companies we serve a new way to fund their payouts, one that is available around the clock and runs through the same Inyo APIs they already use."
The implementation builds on Visa's broader efforts to connect traditional payment infrastructure with blockchain-enabled technologies. By offering stablecoin funding and moving money, Visa is helping clients explore new ways to improve efficiency while maintaining the reliability, security and scale of Visa's global network.
Visa’s work with Inyo Global reflects growing demand for stablecoin-powered solutions that can help businesses manage liquidity, fund payment activity and move money internationally with greater speed and flexibility. As adoption continues to accelerate, Visa is working with clients and partners to bring stablecoin-enabled capabilities to additional money movement use cases around the world.

Visa (NYSE: V) is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating transactions between consumers, sellers, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses and economies to thrive. We believe that economies that include everyone everywhere, uplift everyone everywhere and see access as foundational to the future of money movement. Learn more at Visa.com.

    SAN FRANCISCO — Visa (NYSE: V), a global leader in digital payments, is building a fan-first pro football platform designed to connect more directly with fans, teams, communities, and culture. The company is announcing new partnerships with the Los Angeles Rams, Los Angeles Chargers, Kansas City Chiefs, Washington Commanders, Dallas Cowboys, Houston Texans, and Philadelphia Eagles, and long-term renewals with the San Francisco 49ers, New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Pittsburgh Steelers, alongside current partnerships with the Chicago Bears and Baltimore Ravens.

As pro football drives commerce moments across travel, ticketing, dining, merchandise, and entertainment, Visa will help clients and merchants connect with fans and participate in those moments throughout the season through these team relationships. documents.title: Data: stablecoins gain traction in business payments
documents.raw_text:
Press Release
                            Visa Data Shows Stablecoins Gaining Traction in Business Payments
                        New Visa data shows nearly 17%¹ of stablecoin-linked card volume is occurring across business and commercial card programs, underscoring growing adoption of stablecoins for settlement, treasury management and cross-border commerce.
                10/01/2026
    SAN FRANCISCO AND MIAMI — Today, Visa (NYSE: V) shared new data showing the growing adoption of stablecoins across business payments and commercial card programs, underscoring how stablecoins are increasingly being used as financial infrastructure.
The findings come as businesses, financial institutions and payment providers increasingly explore stablecoins for settlement, treasury management, payouts and cross-border commerce.
New Visa data shows:
Approximately 17% of stablecoin-linked card volume in FY26 year-to-date occurred across business and commercial card programs.
Visa today supports more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs spanning consumer, business and commercial card activity. Payments volume across these programs has grown nearly 200% year over year.
Businesses are increasingly exploring stablecoins for settlement, treasury management, payouts and cross-border commerce.
"Businesses aren't looking for new payment technologies for the sake of innovation. They’re looking for trusted, reliable ways to move money," said Mark Nelsen, Global Head of Product, Commercial and Money Movement Solutions, Visa. "What's changing is that stablecoins are increasingly becoming part of the conversation around real business applications, from supplier payments and treasury operations to cross-border commerce."
The Shift from Trading to Payments
For years, stablecoins have been associated with trading activity within digital asset markets, helping users move between cryptocurrencies and transact on crypto exchanges.
Today, businesses are increasingly putting stablecoins to work for payments, treasury operations and liquidity management.
Recent industry research from Allium found that payments are now the fastest-growing stablecoin use case, with annual payments volume estimated between $401 billion and $527 billion. The largest business payment categories include service fees ($56 billion), payroll ($43 billion) and supplier payments ($28 billion).² Among the payment flows analyzed, B2B payments had the highest cross-border share, with 43% of volume occurring across borders.²
Visa is seeing that trend reflected across its own ecosystem. In FY26 year-to-date, approximately 17% of stablecoin-linked card volume occurred across business and commercial card programs, reflecting growing interest in stablecoins for settlement, treasury management and cross-border commerce.
Supporting the Next Generation of Money Movement
Visa continues to expand its stablecoin capabilities across settlement, money movement and payment acceptance. Through initiatives spanning stablecoin settlement, Visa Direct pre-funding and payouts, Visa is helping connect stablecoin innovation into real-world payment flows.

Rio Tinto releases third quarter 2026 production results
14 October 2026
                    share
Strong operational performance at Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore
    MELBOURNE, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Rio Tinto Chief Executive Simon Trott said: “We delivered strong operational performance in the third quarter. Oyu Tolgoi copper production increased 29% year-to-date, with the operation running at a ~450 kt annualised rate in the quarter, and global iron ore sales are up 3% year-to-date. The Simandou iron ore mine hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in the quarter as the project continues to ramp up.
“We are finishing the year with momentum, with significant opportunities to accelerate improvements in safety, productivity and reliability through implementation of our operating system. We remain on track for a $1.8 billion annualised productivity benefit run-rate by the end of 2026. Our major projects remain on schedule and budget, underwriting our growth profile to 2030.
“We made further significant steps in decarbonising our business in the third quarter, with our Pacific Aluminium smelter repowering arrangements now well progressed.
“Today, we announce that we have achieved more than $2 billion1 of capital release year-to-date, as we actively manage our portfolio with discipline to maximise long-term value, as part of the $5 to 10 billion capital release program.”
Executive Summary
Operational excellence: ~1% YTD increase in copper equivalent (CuEq2) production, driven by growth from Oyu Tolgoi copper and Pilbara iron ore.
Copper: Oyu Tolgoi production increased by 27% YoY in Q3 and 29% YTD. At Kennecott, we successfully completed the rebuild of the flash converting furnace at end-August ahead of plan.
Iron ore: Q3 global iron ore sales were 90.8 Mt, up 3% YoY, while Pilbara sales increased 2% YoY. Simandou hit an annualised production run-rate of ~10 Mtpa (100% basis) in Q3 as the project ramps up and remains on track to reach a 60 Mtpa production run-rate during H2 20283.
Aluminium: Consistent, stable performance across the full operating system. Pacific smelter repowering arrangements are now well progressed, following the Tomago and Bell Bay power agreements in Q3.
Lithium: Production up 33% YTD despite adverse weather impacting Q3 operations. Fenix 1B ramp-up continues to progress well.

Rio Tinto, Tasmanian Government and Commonwealth Government secure the future of Bell Bay Aluminium until 2031
01 October 2026
                    share
      MELBOURNE, Australia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Rio Tinto, the Tasmanian Government and the Australian Government have reached agreement to secure the ongoing operation of Bell Bay Aluminium in northern Tasmania through to the end of 2031.
Under the arrangements, Hydro Tasmania will continue supplying electricity to Bell Bay Aluminium until 31 December 2031, and the Australian and Tasmanian Governments will provide additional support to continue operations as Tasmania’s energy system evolves.
The additional support will help maintain Bell Bay Aluminium’s international competitiveness and its ongoing contribution to the Tasmanian economy.
Rio Tinto Aluminium & Lithium Chief Executive Jérôme Pécresse said: “These agreements will provide Bell Bay Aluminium with an operating pathway through to 2031, and increased certainty for our people, suppliers and the northern Tasmanian community.
“Bell Bay Aluminium has been part of Tasmania's heritage for 71 years, and we are proud of the jobs, exports and economic value it creates for the State.
“With these agreements in place, we can continue to safely deliver high-quality aluminium products for our customers in Australia and around the world.
“I would like to thank the Tasmanian and Australian Governments, Hydro Tasmania, our workers and everyone else who contributed to securing this outcome.”
About Bell Bay Aluminium
Bell Bay Aluminium is 100% owned by Rio Tinto and began operating in 1955. It was the first aluminium smelter in the Southern Hemisphere and produces about 190,000 tonnes of aluminium a year.
The smelter supports about 550 full-time employees and indirectly supports more than 1200 jobs. It spends about A$260 million annually with 180 suppliers.
Rio Tinto's integrated Australian aluminium production chain of bauxite mines, alumina refineries and aluminium smelters is a significant economic driver, employing over 5000 people directly and supporting thousands more Australian livelihoods.
Bell Bay’s current power supply arrangement with Hydro Tasmania ends on 31 December 2026.

Financial results for the year ended 30 June 2026
Strong cash generation, with majority of earnings from copper, increase returns and investment in growth
“A contracting colleague was fatally injured at BMA last month. It was a tragic event, and while investigations continue, his loss sharpens our
focus on safety above all, and on the controls that protect our employees and contractors every day. We will learn from this event to further
improve safety.
FY26 was a strong year for BHP. We delivered record iron ore production and shipments at WAIO, ~2 Mt of copper for a second year running
and a stronger result in coal. We met or beat guidance across much of the portfolio and achieved industry-leading cost positions.
This reliability, together with strong prices, drove a big lift in earnings with Underlying EBITDA increasing to ~US$33 bn. As a result of this,
alongside unlocking of capital from undervalued assets and investing in growth, net debt fell to below US$9 bn, while returning substantial
cash to shareholders through a final dividend of 99 US cents per share, the largest in four years.
Copper is the engine that is driving BHP’s growth. For the first time, Copper contributed more than half our Underlying EBITDA and generated
significant free cash flow, which means our copper growth is self-funding. We have a well-defined project pipeline across Chile, Australia and
Argentina that can potentially lift copper production by around 40% by FY35. At Escondida, we approved US$0.5 bn in pre-commitment
funding for a new concentrator ahead of a final investment decision in CY27-28. In Australia, we continue to advance our copper growth

Arizona to Vicuña on the Argentina-Chile border, while maintaining exposure to future opportunities through our investment in Faraday
Copper and an MOU with Sierra Gorda SCM.
In iron ore, we announced plans for Ministers North, a new mine in the Pilbara. The project will help sustain WAIO production above 305 Mtpa
and further strengthen one of the most competitive businesses in the global mining industry.
Beyond copper and iron ore, Stage 1 of our Jansen potash project in Canada is 84% complete and on track for first production in mid-CY27.
Jansen is expected to operate for more than 60 years and establishes BHP in a new commodity that is essential to food security.
Demand for what we mine is building. Copper demand alone is set to grow from about 34 Mtpa today to more than 50 Mtpa by 2050. We expect China
to continue producing ~1 Btpa of steel this decade while it also invests heavily in its power grid, the United States is investing in copper-intensive
technology, and India is importing more of the raw materials it needs as the fastest growing major economy.
Our commitments to social value and partnerships with customers and communities make a positive difference. Our operational emissions
are down about a third since FY20 and we remain on track for our FY30 target, we spent a record amount with Indigenous businesses in FY26

BHP is well set for what comes next. We have significant opportunity to further lift performance across our assets and a clear pathway for growth. We

Economic outlookxvii
In FY26, the global economy and commodity markets demonstrated considerable resilience despite a backdrop of
heightened geopolitical tension, trade policy uncertainty and shifting monetary and fiscal settings. Copper prices rose
strongly to new record highs, while steel raw material prices recorded positive year-on-year growth. Activity was supported
by a strong uplift in technology-related investment, particularly into artificial intelligence (AI) and the supporting physical
infrastructure, including electrification, even as conflict in the Middle East disrupted key trade flows and lifted energy and
freight costs. The combination of resilient growth and accelerating investment added impetus to the trends that have long
supported commodity demand, such as population growth, urbanisation and rising living standards.
Global economic growth is expected to moderate to around 3% in CY26 from 3.5% in CY25, before improving in CY27.
Fiscal policy in major economies, investment linked to digital infrastructure, electrification and artificial intelligence, and
ongoing government efforts to strengthen energy security and supply-chain resilience are expected to support activity and
commodity demand.
Following a strong start to CY26, China’s economic growth moderated over recent months owing to weak domestic
demand. Nevertheless, a reacceleration of fiscal support expected in H2 CY26 should help keep growth broadly consistent
with the official 4.5% to 5% target range for CY26. While growth remains uneven across sectors, with domestic demand
softer and the property sector continuing to act as a drag, exports have continued to perform strongly, helping to sustain
industrial activity and demand for imported raw materials. India is expected to remain the fastest-growing major economy,
although activity is likely to moderate from the strong pace seen earlier in the year as higher energy costs and weather-
related disruptions weigh on momentum. Nevertheless, infrastructure investment, strong domestic demand and continued
industrialisation remain important sources of support in India. AI-related investment is supporting US growth as well as
manufacturing and export activity in parts of northeast Asia. Europe faces a more challenging near-term environment, but
investment in energy security, defence and industrial resilience is providing some support to the economy.
Commodity demand
Demand for our commodities remained resilient in FY26, despite the Middle East conflict.
Chinese policymakers set a calibrated growth target for CY26 with policies that continue to support metals-related
manufacturing activity. In H1 CY26, machinery and electronics output remained robust, but automobile production fell as
the phase-out of tax incentives for electric vehicle purchases weighed on domestic demand. Housing construction declines
have persisted, although there are indications of demand-side stabilisation in the largest urban centres. Chinese steel and
copper end-use demand has been relatively stable because of healthy goods exports led by strong shipments to emerging
markets and solid demand for capital goods.
Indian commodity demand continued to grow strongly with steel industry margins improving in H1 CY26 following the
extension of safeguard duties in late December 2025 and benchmark prices rising to a two-year high in April 2026. Copper
demand in India softened in H1 CY26 amid conflict-related energy and supply-chain disruptions but sustained electric
vehicle growth underpinned demand. We expect the country’s economic growth to remain resilient, supported by strong
fundamentals and domestic demand, despite external vulnerabilities.
A growing global focus on building resilience, digitalisation and electrification are expected to lead to higher investments in
the physical economy. These drivers sit alongside the enduring forces that have long supported commodity demand:
population growth, urbanisation and rising living standards, which collectively are expected to drive demand for steel, non-
ferrous metals and fertilisers for decades to come.
For the review and outlook relating to our individual commodities please refer to the relevant sections below.
Costs and inflation
The cost environment has shifted materially as a result of the conflict in the Middle East. Higher energy prices have raised
inflation across key regions, both directly and through their flow-on effects across supply chains. In Australia, this has
added to already elevated domestic inflation, while Chile and Canada have experienced renewed pressure after inflation
was starting to ease back towards central bank targets, which has affected costs at projects such as Jansen.
Labour market conditions vary across key regions. In Australia, mining sector wage growth remains elevated amid
continued labour market tightness in some parts of the country. In Canada, labour market conditions are softer, with
subdued hiring and some spare capacity. In Chile, mining employment remains strong while labour costs continue to be
influenced by changes in labour regulation.
Other mining input costs have also been affected by disruption to trade flows through the Strait of Hormuz, with significant
upward pressure on sulphuric acid, diesel and ammonia markets. Cost impacts elsewhere are expected to be more
moderate, with higher energy and transportation costs flowing through to other mining consumables.
Against this backdrop, the relative cost position of individual producers remains important. Operations with structurally
advantaged cost positions, disciplined cost management and reliable access to critical inputs, such as BHP, are better
placed to navigate periods of market disruption and cost volatility.

Commodity review and outlook
Spot copper prices on average were 26% higher in FY26, with H2 FY26 experiencing
increases of nearly 40% as copper moved to >US$13,000/t (US$5.90/lb). The copper
price continues to be supported by strong fundamentals on the demand and supply
side, driven by a compelling narrative for copper-intensive sectors, particularly
electrification and data centres and the risk of future supply deficits.
Global demand is expected to grow at around 2.8% in CY26, a little slower than
previously expected due to the impact of the Middle East conflict, but at a greater
pace than the 2.1% growth experienced in CY25. Multiple countries have seen copper
consumption negatively impacted due to the Middle East conflict, this includes
indirect impacts due to the integrated nature of global supply-chains – for example, a
lack of gas to heat copper for fabrication, or a lack of plastics for wire insulation. In
the US however, copper demand growth is accelerating as unprecedented
investment into data centres boosts requirements for power networks, cabling, and
electrical equipment.
Recovery in production from previously disrupted mining operations and new supply
additions are expected to lead to solid production growth. However, given the robust
demand outlook, the market is likely to remain tight and require additional copper
units to remain in balance. These units could be supplied through increased scrap
recovery and novel sources, such as pyrites and gold concentrates, while
substitution and thrifting act to reduce the quantity of copper required. However,
supply risks remain, with further disruptions, the slow development pipeline, grade
declines, trade barriers, fragmented scrap supply-chains, and rising scrap collection
costs all substantial headwinds.
Copper fundamentals remain attractive. Demand is expected to grow from ~34 Mtpa

Commodity review and outlook
Iron ore prices (Argus 62% Fe iron ore fines CFR China) averaged US$105/dmt in FY26,
up 4%, supported by resilient Chinese demand and elevated cost support from higher
energy and freight costs due to the Middle East conflict. In response to the changing
quality of mainstream mid-grade iron ore fines, Price Reporting Agencies (PRAs)
introduced new 61% Fe indices. The Argus 61% Fe index averaged US$104/dmt in H2
FY26, up 3% from H1 FY26.
Chinese iron ore demand remains resilient, with seaborne iron ore net imports
increasing 6% (an annualised rate of ~1.2 Btpa in H2 FY26) in response to weaker
domestic iron ore supply and scrap. Domestic iron ore production has been constrained
by environmental and safety restrictions, while scrap availability is limited amid subdued
construction activity. Elsewhere, iron ore demand was more mixed, with consumption
continuing to expand in India and emerging Asian economies, following the
commissioning of new Blast Furnace (BF) capacity. Developed Asia and Europe also
showed signs of recovery, the latter driven by the Carbon Border Adjustment
Mechanism incentivised domestic steel production. In contrast, imports into the Middle
East fell sharply, although a gradual recovery is likely if conflict-related tensions ease.
Looking ahead, we maintain our view that China’s real steel production will plateau
around the 1 Btpa level for the rest of the decade. In the medium-term, scrap will play an
increasingly important role in steelmaking and result in a declining profile for Chinese
pig iron production. In the long run, the seaborne iron ore trade is likely to undergo
steady diversification as demand grows in emerging economies.
India, historically a major iron ore exporter, saw imports grow to 12 Mt in CY25 and this
has continued into CY26 with imports rising further. This trend reinforces the view that
India is undergoing a structural shift towards net imports, as domestic iron ore supply
lagging behind steel capacity growth – with some market expectations of imports above
80 Mt by 2030.
Seaborne supply is expected to rise as production from existing supply basins
normalises and new capacity comes online, including Simandou in Guinea. However,
declining grades and resource depletion will require significant investment from
incumbent producers simply to maintain current output and could support future
fundamentals.

Commodity review and outlook – Steelmaking coal
Steelmaking coal prices (PLV FOB Aus) rebounded by 28% in H2 FY26, supported by
a recovery in seaborne demand and supply shocks.
Indian pig iron production growth remained robust, sustaining the country’s position
as the largest seaborne steelmaking coal importer.
The Middle East conflict temporarily impacted steelmaking coal markets through
higher energy prices and gas shortages, encouraging the diversion of semi-soft
coking coals into power generation and reducing supply available to steelmakers.
In May, a tragic mine accident in China triggered widespread coal mine suspensions,
causing a domestic shortage of Premium Hard Coking Coal (PHCC) and creating a
regional price differential whereby seaborne PHCC imports were cheaper than
domestic coal. Given China’s scale in coal production and demand, policy
developments in China remain a key determinant for seaborne coal dynamics.
Outside of China, supply increased through restarts and new mine ramp-ups in
Australia, US and Russia. Barring any adverse impact from conflicts and abnormal
weather, and in a supportive price environment, this trend is likely to continue in the
near term.
Over the longer term, we expect that higher quality steelmaking coals, such as those
produced by our BMA assets, will attract a premium due to their greater ability to
enable lower greenhouse gas emission intensity of blast furnaces. In addition, robust
hard coking coal imports from emerging Asian economies such as India, will lead to
growing and resilient demand for decades to come. The scarcity value of higher
quality steelmaking coals may increase over time, particularly given the restrictive
royalty regime in the major seaborne supply region of Queensland is not supportive
of long-term capital investment in steelmaking coal assets in Queensland.

BMA remains one of the largest suppliers of higher-quality steelmaking coal in the
global seaborne market.xxvi To deliver on our medium-term operational targets at
BMA, we remain focused on improving supply chain resilience by rebuilding raw coal
inventory levels, while normalising strip ratios and further improving productivity.

with our plan to cease mining by the end of FY30. We are focused on extracting
value from the asset, while also progressing studies on future land use, and
supporting the community as it prepares for when BHP ceases mining.

Commodity review and outlook
In FY26, potash spot prices have moved 23% higher to US$342/t Vancouver FOB. This
increase was supported by strong demand, driven by biofuel mandates in Southeast
Asia, a re-stocking cycle in China and improving demand in Brazil. This has been
underpinned by early settlement of the CY26 Chinese annual contract and India settling
their CY26 contract at a multi-year high.
Fertiliser markets were heavily affected by the Middle East conflict, particularly nitrogen
and phosphate, owing to their exposure to natural gas, urea and sulphuric-acid
feedstocks. Muriate of Potash (MOP) is not directly impacted by these feedstocks and
therefore the impact has mostly been limited to increasing freight costs, resulting in
delivered prices moving higher in response. The relative price movements across the
fertiliser complex have further consolidated potash’s affordability, reinforcing its value
proposition for growers and supporting demand resilience. However, farmers continue
to face elevated overall input costs despite potash's relative affordability.
The recent price rally is expected to be tempered in CY27 amidst moderating demand in
price-sensitive regions and sufficient supply.
Longer term, we continue to believe that potash will benefit from durable trends: rising
population, improving diets, reduced availability of arable land, and the need to correct
the persistent global potassium deficit in agricultural soils. These attractive demand
fundamentals will cement the role of potash as a commodity pillar within BHP's portfolio
over the long term.
Business outlook
Jansen Stage 1 (JS1) is achieving its critical path milestones set in the updated January
2026 cost and schedule estimate, and first production remains on track for mid-CY27.
In June 2026, BHP completed a detailed review of cost and schedule estimates for Stage
2 of the Jansen potash project (JS2) and confirmed that the total investment estimate for
JS2 increased from US$4.9 bn to US$6.9 bn (including contingencies) with first
production estimated in late-FY31.xxvii
Given the higher forecast capital intensity for the Jansen project (including Stages 1 and
2 and potential future expansions), we recognised an impairment charge of US$2.3 bn
(before and after tax) in FY26 in relation to our investment to date in the Jansen project.
Jansen is a world class asset and is expected to operate at the low end of the cost curve
when fully ramped up.
