documents.title: FY26 Full Year Results - Results speech pdf
documents.raw_text:
[[PAGE 1]]
Financial results for
the year ended
30 June 2026
Presentation &
speech
18 August 2026

[[PAGE 2]]
BHP INVESTOR
1
Brandon Craig
Slide 1: Accelerating performance, delivering growth1
Welcome to today’s presentation of BHP’s results for the 2026 financial year.
My name is Brandon Craig, and I’m joined by our Chief Financial Officer, Vandita Pant. As Chief Executive Officer, it
is a pleasure for me to host this call with all of you this morning.
But let me begin by saying that BHP is in great shape. Mike has left us a strong platform with a tier 1 portfolio, an
operating system that continues to improve, and a balance sheet that allows us to invest through the cycle. I intend
to build on this strong foundation by adding even greater pace, improving our operational practices, and focusing on
our customers and markets.
Today, we have great momentum, which you will see in our operational and financial results. The opportunity now is
to accelerate performance. To lift safety, productivity and growth to the next level – while maintaining the discipline
that has served shareholders well over many years.
That is the agenda I am focused on as Chief Executive Officer… accelerating performance, delivering programmatic
growth, and strengthening our foundations for the future.
Note: Footnotes references reflect slide footnote numbering. Refer to FY26 Results Presentation (slides 34 to 37) for footnotes. Year references
refer to financial years.

[[PAGE 3]]
BHP INVESTOR
2
Slide 2: Disclaimer
But none of that matters if our people don't go home safely.
So let me start with that.

[[PAGE 4]]
BHP INVESTOR
3
Slide 3: Safety remains our top priority
Only a few weeks ago, a colleague of ours, working for a contracting partner, never made it home.
His loss is deeply felt across BHP, the mining community in the Bowen Basin, and in particular at Peak Downs Mine.
Our thoughts are with his loved ones.
As a leader, this is deeply personal. And speaking for BHP, we are committed to learning from this and improving
safety further. Our teams are working through the investigation, and leaders across our global operations are re-
verifying our critical controls for higher-risk activities.
We have made significant progress over recent years – strengthening our safety culture and our systems to meet
our aspiration to eliminate fatalities and high-potential injuries from BHP. But progress is not the measure. The only
acceptable number is zero, and we are not there yet.
We will continue to embed the BHP Operating System, which underpins safe operations. We will invest more and
move faster on technology. And we will continue to enhance safety standards and work together to implement them.

[[PAGE 5]]
BHP INVESTOR
4
Slide 4: Operational excellence driving value, growth and returns
Turning now to our results.
BHP’s 2026 financial year performance consolidates our position as the world’s leading mining company1.
We are the world’s largest copper producer2, and for the second consecutive year we produced around 2 million
tonnes of copper, which contributed more than half of our annual EBITDA for the first time. Our commitment to
operational excellence also delivered record production at Western Australia Iron Ore.
This strong operating performance, along with proceeds from the Antamina silver streaming transaction, has enabled
the Board to determine a dividend for the June half of 99 US cents per share.
This takes our full year dividend to US$8.7 billion.

[[PAGE 6]]
BHP INVESTOR
5
Slide 5: Mining remains undervalued
The world has always relied on mining – and today is no different. Yet despite this, mining now represents a much
smaller share of global equity markets than it did just 15 years ago.
A lot of capital is flowing into Artificial Intelligence, data centres and the energy transition. And countries and
companies are increasingly focused on energy and food security, supply chain resilience and industrial capacity.
This means demand today for commodities – such as copper – is much more broad-based than during China’s boom
in the late 2000s.
So if global progress develops along these pathways – as we expect – mining will be required more than ever. And
as the world’s biggest miner, this provides significant opportunities for BHP.

[[PAGE 7]]
BHP INVESTOR
6
Slide 6: Asset quality and commodity selection are key to value
It is also why we have been so deliberate in our portfolio choices over decades. It is central to value creation.
BHP commodities must benefit from global megatrends and have sufficiently diverse demand drivers for resilience
through the cycle. They must have large, global, seaborne markets. Value must be captured upstream – in line with
our capabilities. And they must have steep cost curves, so we can apply our operational expertise to deliver leading
margins.
Within those commodities, we seek the best possible assets. Very large, long life, low cost and expandable. Assets
that we can operate for decades, and that generate robust margins and returns.
The takeaway – BHP has tier 1 assets in commodities the world needs. This is a truly differentiated portfolio and
provides a meaningful and durable competitive advantage.

[[PAGE 8]]
BHP INVESTOR
7
Slide 7: The next decade: more velocity and ambition, same discipline
Now, as good as BHP’s position is today, we have always challenged ourselves to do better.
That means focusing on three priorities.
• Accelerating performance – leveraging the BHP Operating System and technology – to unlock the next horizon
of safety, productivity and capability.
• Delivering disciplined, programmatic growth and developing the next generation of growth options in future-
facing commodities.
• And strengthening our foundations across safety, social value and talent, and deepening partnerships, to
further increase our resilience.
So: greater ambition… more velocity... but the same discipline.
Let me explain this briefly.

[[PAGE 9]]
BHP INVESTOR
8
Slide 8: BOS is driving operational improvement
It has been seven years since we implemented the BHP Operating System. BOS creates a safer and more productive
workplace, and enables continuously improving performance. It’s about culture, systems and behaviours, as much
as underlying operational disciplines and practices.
The more we embed BOS, the better we perform. Vandita will talk to some examples of where we have seen
improvement shortly.
Few companies have been able to stick consistently to a system of this nature, which matters because these systems
won’t just generate results overnight – you need to keep at it for years and decades.
We assess BOS maturity through an Operational Excellence Index – or OEI – and since 2020 we have increased
our score from 36 to 521. Over this period, we have actioned around 7,000 initiatives right across the business. And
in their first year of implementation, these delivered cost savings of more than US$5 billion3. But there is still so much
more we can do.
To capture this value, I have tasked our teams to deliver significant, sustained improvement towards a company-
wide mark of 65. That is beyond what is considered to be ‘world-leading’ based on external benchmarks2. Our
aspiration is to pursue the limits of performance and push out the productivity frontier.

[[PAGE 10]]
BHP INVESTOR
9
Slide 9: Technology will amplify BHP’s competitive advantages
And while BOS creates the foundation for performance improvement, technology accelerates it. Simply, BOS and
technology are mutually reinforcing.
Technology is already creating value across our business. By the end of 2026, technology initiatives were delivering
incremental EBITDA at an annual run rate of almost US$500 million. We aim to increase that to beyond US$650
million by the end of 20271.
But many of our examples to date are ‘single point’ applications – just the first wave of value creation. Applying
technology to integrate the entire supply chain – from pit to port – means we can optimise the whole system more
dynamically. That will liberate more productive hours, which means more production, leading then to lower cost.

[[PAGE 11]]
BHP INVESTOR
10
Slide 10: Creating programmatic growth…2
While I am passionate about the potential to accelerate performance improvement, I’m also focused on value-
accretive volume growth.
Our world-class portfolio of high-quality growth projects is estimated to deliver 3 to 4% per year growth over 2027 to
2035, including around 5% per year in our copper business. I’m focused on ensuring we deliver this on time and on
budget.
But to continue this rate of growth beyond 2035 we need to build the next generation of high-quality options. This
means:
• More partnerships and adjacencies – like we have with Sierra Gorda in Chile and Rio Tinto in the Pilbara.
• More creativity in the way we think about growth – like our investment in Faraday Copper.
• And more ambitious exploration and early-stage investments – to secure the next big deposits like Vicuña.
Note: See "Forward-looking production information, assumptions and copper equivalent methodology" on slide 37.

[[PAGE 12]]
BHP INVESTOR
11
Slide 11: …which is not being fully valued yet
Now, while investors understand the quality of BHP’s portfolio, we believe there is more value to be recognised in
the growth we have ahead of us. For example, many in the investment community model growth of around 2% per
year3 through to 2035 – well below our estimates of 3 to 4%2.
We have a track record of doing what we say we will do and meeting our guidance reliably1.
So our job is clear: safely accelerate performance; execute our projects well and build the next generation of options;
and develop the strategic relationships that build our resilience.
With that, I’ll hand over to Vandita to take you through our financial performance.

[[PAGE 13]]
BHP INVESTOR
12
Vandita Pant
Slide 12: Financial performance
Thanks, Brandon.
This has been another great year financially. Our portfolio delivered high margins and strong cash flow, which allowed
us to invest in our growth and deliver very healthy shareholder returns.
Let me take you through the numbers.

[[PAGE 14]]
BHP INVESTOR
13
Slide 13: Driving earnings through delivery
Underlying EBITDA for the year was US$33 billion, up 27%, with a margin of almost 60%. Underlying attributable
profit was US$13 billion, up 30%. And return on capital employed was 26%.
After exceptional items, including a US$2.3 billion non-cash impairment relating to Jansen, our total attributable profit
increased by 9%, to almost US$10 billion.
Cash flow generation was strong, and our balance sheet strengthened, with net debt below US$9 billion.
Based on the strength of these results, and proceeds from the Antamina silver streaming agreement, we determined
a final dividend of US$5 billion.
This brings our full year dividend to US$8.7 billion – the highest in four years.

[[PAGE 15]]
BHP INVESTOR
14
Slide 14: Macro tailwinds reinforced by operational excellence
The earnings waterfall reflects a familiar theme.
While higher prices were a clear tailwind – up 35% for copper and 3% for iron ore – our operational performance and
cost discipline enabled us to fully capture that benefit.
Across the group, unit costs improved over 6%3 (slide 15), despite currency pressures, inflation, and higher diesel and
acid prices.

[[PAGE 16]]
BHP INVESTOR
15
Slide 15: Strong performance achieved across the portfolio
This strong performance was achieved across the portfolio.
Our copper business generated a record US$18 billion of EBITDA – 54% of the Group total – at a margin of 70%.
Our operational performance, combined with a US$4.5 billion contribution from by-products, saw unit costs improve
by 10% at Escondida and over 70% at Copper SA. An impressive result.
WAIO achieved record production and shipments. It was another year in which we delivered a real cost decline, with
C1 unit costs up just 1%.
And in steelmaking coal, BMA continues to improve performance, with production up around 10% over the last two
years and the highest stripping volumes in five years.

[[PAGE 17]]
BHP INVESTOR
16
Slide 16: BOS has contributed to improved operational performance
This slide shows the clear correlation between BOS and performance. The higher the OEI, the more stable and more
productive our operations. And this can be seen across assets, processes and over time.
It’s this last point that’s very important. As Brandon said, you don’t realise these benefits sustainably overnight.
At WAIO, steady improvements in rail productivity have supported record shipments. At Copper SA, we have
improved operational stability, with year-on-year records at the smelter since the last major maintenance campaign.
And at Escondida, we have delivered record material mined and record concentrator throughput, helping to offset
the impact of grade.
This has a real impact on the bottom line.

[[PAGE 18]]
BHP INVESTOR
17
Slide 17: WAIO continues to be the industry’s lowest cost producer
Take WAIO as an example. It has remained the world's lowest-cost major iron ore producer for a 7th consecutive
year. And it has reduced costs in real terms post-Covid – the only major producer to do so1.
In 2026 alone, this had compounded to a cost saving of over US$100 million, on a real basis2. Our 2027 guidance
suggests that we will maintain our cost leadership.

[[PAGE 19]]
BHP INVESTOR
18
Slide 18: Turning operational excellence into margin expansion…
Why are we so focused on operational excellence?
Firstly, because it provides resilience through the cycle. In addition, inflationary environments drive higher marginal
costs, resulting in higher commodity prices across the industry.
This gives reliable operators of low-cost assets – like BHP – the ability to capture higher margins. You can see this
in our cash flows.

[[PAGE 20]]
BHP INVESTOR
19
Slide 19: …and resilient cash flow through the cycle
Our diversified portfolio, by design, is another competitive advantage. It supports resilient cash flow across market
conditions. That allows us to invest in growth and deliver strong returns to shareholders.
As this slide shows, at spot prices we expect to generate around US$50 billion in attributable free cash flow over the
next five years1,2. That is after funding our investment in growth. And even under a sustained multi-year downside
commodity price scenario, we still expect to generate around US$15 billion of free cash flow over the period1,2.
In short, BHP’s unique combination of scale, performance and diversification supports significant and resilient cash
flows.

[[PAGE 21]]
BHP INVESTOR
20
Slide 20: Enhancing returns through disciplined capital allocation
Our Capital Allocation Framework – CAF – is how we maximise value from that cash. The discipline it instils has
served shareholders well for over a decade now.
The foundation of CAF is our consistently strong margins and cash flows.
• Average margins over 50% over the past 25 years1; and
• Net operating cash flow above US$15 billion in all bar one year since 2010.
We also continue to release value from our capital base and assets. This includes the potential to unlock around
US$10 billion in undervalued capital, with US$6.3 billion of this already executed in the last nine months2.
On top of this, we received almost US$1 billion in cash during the year from previously announced non-core asset
sales3.
This has allowed us to:
• Maintain a very strong balance sheet;
• Deliver attractive returns to shareholders; and
• Continue to invest in our high-quality growth.

[[PAGE 22]]
BHP INVESTOR
21
Slide 21: A capex program set to deliver 5% p.a. copper growth
We now expect capex of around US$11 billion per year, on average, over the medium term. This is in nominal terms,
at constant FX rates3. This reflects updated estimates for Jansen Stage 2 and changes in FX, partly offset by
improved capital productivity across the rest of the portfolio.
More than half of our growth spend will go to copper – and approximately two-thirds if we include investment in our
non-operated joint ventures.

[[PAGE 23]]
BHP INVESTOR
22
Slide 22: BHP’s copper capex program is self-funded
An important feature of our copper capex program is that it is entirely self-funding at consensus prices1,3. This is a
result of being the largest copper producer, which provides a large base of cash flows today, and our approach to
sequencing and partnerships, which allows us to manage spend.
This gives us confidence that we can deliver our four attractive copper projects at the same time, even without higher
copper prices.
And once these projects ramp up, not only will they drive meaningful production growth, they will also deliver
significant incremental cash flows. Add to that the cash flows from our iron ore and potash businesses, and we have
even more flexibility to fund growth, keep our balance sheet strong, and provide attractive cash returns to
shareholders.
With that, I'll hand back to Brandon.

[[PAGE 24]]
BHP INVESTOR
23
Brandon Craig
Slide 23: Business update
Thanks, Vandita.
For BHP, the implications are clear. The world needs more of the commodities we produce. But the key question is
where they will come from.

[[PAGE 25]]
BHP INVESTOR
24
Slide 24: WAIO and BMA: tier 1 assets underpin resilience
WAIO is an asset I know well, and which continues to deliver year in, year out.
At this asset, we have delivered real cost discipline, which is reflected in unit costs, margins and free cash flow. It is
worth repeating – WAIO produces around US$10 per tonne more free cash flow1 than its closest peer, and our goal
is to increase this margin further.
Our plans to progressively increase production and lower unit costs position this outstanding asset to generate value
well into the future.
Shifting to metallurgical coal. BMA is home to some of the world’s best steelmaking coal – an ingredient that will
remain critical to steelmaking for decades.
Having spent a fair bit of time there as well, I know what that business is capable of and firmly believe its best years
are in front of it.
We have a plan to improve performance and returns, and that plan doesn’t include selling the business. Our ongoing
focus on strengthening the supply chain and cost productivity is expected to lift production and reduce costs over the
medium term. And we believe there is potential to invest further if fiscal conditions improve.
While WAIO and BMA are exceptional businesses, we are also broadening the portfolio.

[[PAGE 26]]
BHP INVESTOR
25
Slide 25: The attractiveness of Jansen and potash
Jansen will add an attractive new earnings stream, and we are very focused on its delivery.
Stage 1 remains on track for first production mid next calendar year. And we firmly believe it will be another tier 1
asset for BHP – very large, long life, low cost and expandable.
Once ramped up, it is expected to deliver around US$1 billion of EBITDA per year, per stage, with margins above
60%1. A great example of why we focus on the commodities that we do.
Jansen also adds something the rest of the portfolio does not. It will make BHP stronger because potash demand
drivers and key customer markets are differentiated from our other commodities. That means prices are less
correlated4, driving even more stability in earnings and cash flow.

[[PAGE 27]]
BHP INVESTOR
26
Slide 26: BHP’s project delivery track record is solid
Now, growth only creates value if we deliver it well. Project delivery is therefore a core part of my agenda.
We have a solid track record in this area. Over the past decade, around 80% of our projects have come in on time
and on budget – the best of the diversified miners1.
But Jansen has highlighted that we need to further improve our major project performance and we are very focused
on this.
Embedding BOS and technology into projects is at the centre of our approach, and I’m excited to see how much
further we can improve our project execution – just as we have seen across operational performance.

[[PAGE 28]]
BHP INVESTOR
27
Slide 27: Expanding the world’s largest copper business3
While potash broadens our portfolio, copper remains our largest and most important growth opportunity.
Our lower-risk pathway represents growth of around 50% by the mid-2030s, to around 2.5 million tonnes per year of
attributable copper equivalent production. This includes over half a million tonnes, in copper equivalent terms, of by-
products – by itself, the size of a significant copper producer.
This is attractive, capital efficient, predominantly brownfield growth that will further increase the proportion of our
earnings from copper.
This is an exciting position to be in. The world needs more copper. And BHP has the assets, options and capability
to help supply it…
Note: See 'Forward-looking production information: assumptions and copper equivalent methodology' on slide 37.

[[PAGE 29]]
BHP INVESTOR
28
Slide 28: Escondida: world-class asset quality and operating capability
…Assets like Escondida, which continues to perform strongly. It remains a world-class copper asset that we intend
to invest in further.
We have just approved around US$500 million in pre-commitment funding1 for Escondida’s new concentrator and
expect to make a final investment decision in 2027 or 2028.
As we move towards that point, the project continues to improve. The optimised scope is expected to deliver higher
throughput, production and returns, with the updated capital estimate reflecting the larger scale and design
improvements.
It is a great example of our project delivery approach and the way we continuously look to optimise our projects.

[[PAGE 30]]
BHP INVESTOR
29
Slide 29: Copper SA: growing production, cash flow and returns
At Copper South Australia:
• we delivered the highest production at Olympic Dam in 20 years; and
• our unit costs declined to just 32 cents per pound, benefiting from US$2.3 billion of by-product revenue.
As a result, we set new records for EBITDA and free cash flow2.
This consistency in performance provides a strong platform from which to invest.
We are looking at ways to accelerate production growth and look forward to providing an update on Copper South
Australia at our site tour later this year.

[[PAGE 31]]
BHP INVESTOR
30
Slide 30: Vicuña: advancing to Stage 1 FID4
We are also progressing the next generation of copper mines – notably, the Vicuña Joint Venture with Lundin Mining.
During the half, Vicuña received environmental approval for Stage 1 as well as approval under Argentina’s RIGI
scheme – which provides fiscal stability for 40 years. Most recently, Vicuña signed a royalty agreement with the San
Juan province.
These are key milestones as we progress towards a final investment decision on Stage 1 – potentially as early as
the end of this calendar year.
Once all three stages are fully developed, Vicuña has the potential to be a global top 5 copper, and global top 5 gold,
producing asset.
Note: Top 5 copper and gold producer based on 10-year average once Stage III fully ramped up with ~500ktpa of copper and ~800kozpa of
gold.

[[PAGE 32]]
BHP INVESTOR
31
Slide 31: BHP: an attractive investment case
So, in closing, BHP is a company in tremendous health.
We are delivering operationally, financially, have an industry-leading growth pipeline, and we are investing in the
project capability to deliver it for value. This is a platform for success, and a testament to the hard work of our teams
across the world.
The agenda from here is clear.
• First, accelerate performance, using BOS and technology to deliver safer, more stable operations and lower
unit costs.
• Second, deliver disciplined, programmatic growth with industry-leading project execution capability.
• And third, build on our foundations and strengthen our resilience.
Across all three, discipline remains central.
Our competitive advantage is not about any single asset. It is the combination of world-class assets, operational
excellence, disciplined capital allocation, technology, and a balance sheet that allows us to invest consistently
through the cycle.
I am truly excited about what the future holds for BHP, and what we can deliver together.
Thank you for your support.

BHP INVESTOR

▪ Company to expand investments across the entire AI ecosystem
▪ Discussing strategies to strengthen partnerships with global venture firms and investors in future technology fields such as AI data centers and optical-based systems
Seoul, September 18, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today the launch of its corporate venture capital (CVC) brand, “SK hynix Ventures,” aimed at expanding strategic partnerships within the global AI ecosystem and securing future innovative technologies.
To mark the occasion, SK hynix held the inaugural “SK hynix Ventures Day” in Silicon Valley, where executives shared investment strategies with global venture capitalists and startup representatives while discussing future technological cooperation to respond to shifts in the AI industry.
The event was attended by CEO Kwak Noh-Jung and key executive leadership, alongside representatives from global VC firms and executives from leading startups.
	▲ SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung outlining the vision for ‘SK hynix Ventures’ and commitment to expanding the global AI ecosystem at the inaugural ‘Ventures Day’ held in Silicon Valley, U.S. on the 17th (local time)
	▲ (Local time) On the 17th, the ‘Ventures Day’ event is held in Silicon Valley, USA, marking the launch of SK hynix’s new CVC brand, ‘SK hynix Ventures.’
Expanding Beyond Tech Sensing to Become a Strategic Partner in the AI Ecosystem
Since 2015, SK hynix has operated a CVC organization, pursuing both direct investments and indirect investments via fund commitments in promising early-stage startups within the semiconductor and emerging tech sectors. By investing in enterprises across key regions including the U.S., China, Israel, and Japan, the company has achieved returns exceeding twice its cumulative investment to date. Furthermore, it has accumulated a track record of discovering new supply chains and customers by pursuing technological collaborations—such as joint equipment development and Proof of Concept (PoC)—with portfolio companies.
While past CVC activities focused primarily on “Tech Sensing” to explore future technology trends and “Path Finding” to discover new business opportunities, the company now plans to expand its CVC scope. Driven by recent advancements in AI technology and industry expansion, the role will evolve from simply discovering promising companies to leading collaborative innovation across the entire ecosystem.
Discussing Cooperation in AI Computing, Data Centers, and Optical Interconnect
Through SK hynix Ventures, the company plans to broaden its investment scope from traditional semiconductors and emerging tech to the broader AI ecosystem. SK hynix aims to discover technologies and companies with high growth potential in core AI industry sectors—including AI computing, data centers, system software, and optical interconnect—and continually expand its CVC investments.
Meanwhile, the event was attended by promising startups in the U.S. AI computing and data center technology sectors. These companies shared perspectives on future technological innovations, discussing the growing importance of computing, memory, and system software innovations driven by advanced AI models, alongside the performance and power efficiency of optical-based systems for AI data centers.
“Competitiveness in the AI era stems not just from rapidly securing innovative technologies, but from ecosystem capabilities where customers, partners, and startups create new value together,” said Kwak Noh-Jung, CEO of SK hynix. “Through SK hynix Ventures, we will support the growth of promising companies and grow into a global partner that jointly designs the future of AI infrastructure based on strategic investments and technological cooperation.”
About SK hynix Inc.
SK hynix Inc., headquartered in Korea, is the world’s top-tier semiconductor supplier offering Dynamic Random Access Memory chips (“DRAM”) and flash memory chips (“NAND flash”) for a wide range of distinguished customers globally. The Company’s common shares are traded on the Korea Exchange, its American Depositary Shares are traded on NASDAQ, and its Global Depository Shares are listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange. Further information about SK hynix is available at www.skhynix.com, news.skhynix.com.

documents.title: SK hynix Holds Groundbreaking Ceremony for HBM Production Base in Indiana, “Beginning a New Future for US-Korea AI” | SK hynix Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
▪ Investing over $4 billion in Indiana fab and first ‘Made in USA’ next-generation HBM mass production in U.S. to begin in H2 2029
▪ Help stabilize the U.S. semiconductor supply chain and contribute to strengthening U.S. national security and economy
▪ Establishing a semiconductor ecosystem with more than 100 partners and creating 7,000 direct/indirect local jobs
▪ MOU with Purdue University for R&D collaboration on next-generation advanced packaging technology
▪ Recruitment of USFK(US Forces Korea) veterans, contributing to a stronger US-Korea alliance
▪ CEO Kwak Noh-Jung “We will become the most trusted partner in the U.S., where top-tier customers, R&D capabilities, and partners align”
Seoul, August 28, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) is opening a new future for AI cooperation between the United States and South Korea by establishing a first next-generation High Bandwidth Memory(HBM) production hub in the US.
▲ Groundbreaking ceremony for SK hynix’s AI memory advanced packaging production base is taking place in West Lafayette, Indiana, U.S. on the 27th (local time)
SK hynix announced today that it held a groundbreaking ceremony for an advanced packaging* production facility for AI memory on the 27th(local time) at the Holloway Gymnasium, Purdue University, located in West Lafayette, Indiana.
* Advanced Packaging: An advanced semiconductor back-end technology that combines multiple chips into a single package or stacks them vertically to enhance performance, overcoming the physical limits of micro-fabrication processes that shrink chip sizes.
The groundbreaking ceremony was attended by prominent US government and political figures, including Indiana Governor Mike Braun, US Senator Todd Young, Purdue University President Mitch Daniels, and Chairman of the Korea-US Alliance Foundation Robert Abrams. Kang Kyung-wha, Ambassador of South Korea to the United States, was also present at the event. From the SK Group, Vice Chairman Yu Jeong-Joon, Vice Chairman Lee Hyung-hee, CEO of SK hynix Kwak Noh-Jung attended.
▲ Main attendees taking a photo at the groundbreaking ceremony for the AI memory advanced packaging production base held in West Lafayette, Indiana, U.S. (Seventh from the left Purdue University President Mitch Daniels, SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung and Indiana Governor Mike Braun)
Investment of Over $4 Billion for First US HBM Production Base Creating Synergy with Korea
The Indiana fab, with a total expected investment of over $4 billion, is scheduled to open its cleanroom by October 2028 and initiate mass production of next-generation HBM in the second half of 2029. It is projected to grow into a key HBM production hub in the US led by a workforce of approximately 1,000 personnel during anticipated commercial operations.
Notably, the Indiana fab marks SK hynix’s first HBM production base established in the United States, featuring an operation framework closely integrated with production in South Korea. Cutting edge wafers produced by SK hynix in Korea will be delivered to Indiana, where they will undergo advanced packaging and testing before Made in USA products are supplied to US customers.
Furthermore, an “Advanced Packaging R&D Testbed” will be built alongside the production lines, enabling customers, universities, and business partners to collaboratively develop next-generation packaging technologies and rapidly execute prototype fabrication and performance validation.
As competition to expand AI infrastructure intensifies, the Indiana fab, which connects
SK hynix’s Korea-US HBM production, is expected not only to help stabilize the U.S. semiconductor supply chain but also to contribute to strengthening the national economy and security in the AI era.
“SK hynix’s historic investment in West Lafayette is further proof that Indiana is leading the way in rebuilding America’s semiconductor industry,” said Senator Young. “This project will create good-paying jobs, strengthen our national and economic security, and ensure the technologies of the future are developed and manufactured here in the United States. I was proud to help make this investment possible through the CHIPS and Science Act, and I look forward to seeing the impact it will have on Hoosiers and our country for decades to come.”
Indiana Governor Mike Braun remarked, “This project will usher in the next generation of American innovation, bring thousands of good-paying jobs to Indiana and supercharge regional economic development. It’s a win for Hoosiers, a win for our economy and a great leap forward for Indiana in the race to be the best in the industries of the future.”
Strengthening the Local Ecosystem and Bilateral Economic Cooperation with Local and National Companies
SK hynix’s investment in Indiana is expected to foster a virtuous cycle of strengthening the US semiconductor ecosystem and enhancing economic cooperation between South Korea and the United States.
Currently, more than 100 companies are being considered as suppliers for materials, components, and equipment for the West Lafayette facility, which will support the stable operation of the Indiana fab and further solidify the US AI ecosystem. SK hynix also plans to create approximately 7,000 direct and indirect jobs with local and national companies during construction of the advanced packaging facility and subsequent commercial operations.
Kang Kyung-wha, South Korean Ambassador to the US, stated, “SK hynix’s investment in Indiana is not merely an investment in semiconductor manufacturing facilities, but the establishment of the first AI memory production facility and R&D center in the United States, creating a unique model for nurturing semiconductor talent and strengthening collaboration with the government and external organizations.”
MOU for R&D Collaboration with Purdue University and Veteran Recruitment Program
At the groundbreaking ceremony, SK hynix also signed a Memorandum of Understanding(MOU) with Purdue University for research and development collaboration in the field of advanced packaging.
Through the MOU, both parties will strengthen R&D cooperation and will jointly research system integration and advanced packaging technologies, including HBM. In addition,
SK hynix plans to expand efforts on cultivating and recruiting world-class talent from across the Midwest.
During the event, a recruitment partnership was also established to honor the special historical connection with Indiana, which deployed approximately 140,000 troops during the Korean War. SK Group agreed to provide new employment and career opportunities for discharged USFK service members. To this end, SK Group will participate as a hiring corporation in the ‘USFK Veterans Job Platform’ operated by the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry(KCCI) and the Korea-US Alliance Foundation, thereby contributing to the robust partnership between the two nations.
Kwak Noh-Jung, CEO of SK hynix, declared, “Today marks the day when the United States and SK hynix embark on a new future of AI together.” He added, “The United States is the epicenter of AI innovation, bringing together premier customers, top-tier R&D capabilities, and partners and Indiana fab will become a gateway to deliver first Made in USA HBM proudcts.” He emphasized, “We will expand our investments and collaboration in the US, grow together, and become the most trusted partner in shaping the future of AI in America.”
▲ SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung presenting the AI memory vision and commitment to expanding cooperation with the U.S. at the groundbreaking ceremony held in West Lafayette, Indiana, U.S. on the 27th (local time)

documents.title: SK hynix Accelerates 40 Trillion won Share Repurchase and Cancellation Program, Pursues Shareholder Return Expansion to ‘Over 50% of FCF’ | SK hynix Newsroom
documents.raw_text:
▪ Board approves resolution on August 19 to repurchase and fully cancel 40 trillion won of treasury shares
▪ Decision reflects the view that intrinsic value—driven by business competitiveness and cash generation capability—is underrepresented in current share price
▪ Largest treasury share cancellation in the history of the South Korean listed companies; to be executed ahead of schedule within program period
▪ Company to expand shareholder return target from the previous “within 50% of cumulative FCF” to “over 50%”
▪ Parallel execution of share repurchases/cancellations alongside dividends; Fixed dividends and special dividends also under consideration to expand payouts
Seoul, August 19, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com) announced today that its Board of Directors has approved a resolution to repurchase and fully cancel 40 trillion won worth of its own shares. The Company also revealed plans to return “over 50% of cumulative Free Cash Flow(FCF)” generated during the program period(2025-2027), adopting a framework centered on the parallel execution of share repurchases and cancellations alongside cash dividends.
Following the Board meeting held earlier today, the Company formally disclosed the share repurchase and cancellation resolution along with the shareholder return plan via a regulatory filing.
The decision stems from the assessment that the Company’s intrinsic value—underpinned by its business competitiveness, robust cash generation capability, and mid-to-long-term growth potential—is not fully reflected in its current stock price.
SK hynix continues to record record-breaking financial performance, maintaining its leadership in the AI memory market. As of the end of the second quarter of this year, the Company’s net cash stood at approximately 69 trillion won, demonstrating significantly improved cash generation capability.
The total planned amount for the share repurchase is 40 trillion won. Based on the closing stock price of 1,662,000 won on the day prior to the Board resolution, this represents approximately 24.07 million shares, or about 3.3% of total issued shares(730,492,365 shares). The repurchase period is scheduled to run for approximately three months starting August 20, with all repurchased shares set to be cancelled upon completion of the acquisition.
This initiative accelerates the execution of the existing shareholder return program ahead of schedule. In November 2024, SK hynix announced a program to execute shareholder returns within the range of 50% of its three-year(2025-2027) cumulative FCF, noting that it would consider early execution prior to the program’s expiration if FCF increased meaningfully due to improved operational performance.
The 40 trillion won program marks the largest treasury share cancellation ever conducted by a South Korean listed company. The Company noted that progress toward its financial health targets remains on track, affirming its commitment to maintaining a stable financial structure while delivering sustained shareholder value.
Through today’s regulatory filing, SK hynix announced plans to pursue an expansion of its total shareholder return target from the previous “within 50% of cumulative FCF” to “over 50% of cumulative FCF”. Under the framework, shareholder returns will be executed through a dual-track approach running share repurchases/cancellations alongside cash dividends, while options to expand payouts—including the existing fixed dividends and special dividends—are also under consideration.
SK hynix emphasized that it intends to pursue additional shareholder returns within the program period through the parallel execution of share repurchases/cancellations and dividends, by taking into account cash flows, market conditions, and distributable profits, adding that specific details regarding scale and execution will be announced following Board approval at the time of its third-quarter earnings release.

documents.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark PCs Available Today — A New Beginning for Windows PCs
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:
	NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops are available today from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI — with additional systems to follow — bringing RTX acceleration and NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform to slim, premium Windows PCs for creation, gaming and local AI.
	RTX Spark delivers up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and up to 128GB of unified memory — enabling AI developers, creators and gamers to run frontier AI models locally, render 90GB+ 3D scenes and play AAA games at 1440p at over 100 frames per second, all on a slim, portable device.
	Day-one support across local AI agents, creative apps and major games helps users put RTX Spark to work immediately — from editing with Adobe Photoshop and Premiere to running Hermes and OpenClaw agents and playing titles including Gears of War: E-Day and NBA 2K27 with NVIDIA DLSS 5.
NVIDIA today announced the availability of NVIDIA RTX Spark™ laptops, bringing together RTX graphics and NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform in slim, premium Windows PCs for accelerated creation, immersive gaming and powerful local AI — rolling out from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI.
Combining decades of NVIDIA innovation into a single superchip, RTX Spark delivers up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance to run large language models and AI agents locally. On a single device, creators, developers and gamers can move seamlessly between their everyday workflows and emerging AI agents on the familiar Windows platform.
“RTX Spark brings the power of NVIDIA AI, RTX graphics and CUDA together with Microsoft Windows in one PC for creating, gaming and running personal AI agents,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Together with Microsoft and our PC industry partners, we’re bringing creators, developers and gamers a new generation of Windows PC, built for the work they do today and the personal AI agents they’ll work with next.”
“We’re building Windows to be the platform for hybrid intelligence, where AI can run locally when it makes sense and reach the cloud when needed,” said Yusuf Mehdi, executive vice president at Microsoft. “Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark unlock powerful new local compute for creators and developers, expanding what they can create, build and run on Windows.”
A New Beginning for Windows PCs
RTX Spark brings NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform to a new generation of portable Windows PCs.
At its foundation is a single superchip combining an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and an NVIDIA Grace CPU with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance. That shared memory allows demanding creative projects and local AI models to run simultaneously and efficiently. MediaTek collaborated with NVIDIA on the custom CPU design, contributing to its best-in-class power efficiency, performance and connectivity.
All of NVIDIA’s platform innovation comes together in RTX Spark — NVIDIA CUDA®, DLSS, OptiX™, Reflex, G-SYNC®, TensorRT™ and hardware-accelerated video — in a device that fits in a messenger bag. Slim, efficient designs and all-day battery life bring these capabilities wherever users create, develop and play.
From Tool to Teammate
RTX Spark gives users the capabilities to deploy local AI agents that turn the PC from a tool into an everyday teammate that can complete tasks, generate assets and write code.
Users can put agents to work immediately. Guided setup and easy installers help users get started with agents, including GitHub Copilot, Hermes, OpenClaw, Perplexity, Pi and WorkBuddy, without requiring a command line.
“Personal AI becomes more useful when it can work with your tools and help get things done,” said Dillon Rolnick, CEO at Nous Research, creators of Hermes Agent. “We brought Hermes to RTX Spark so people can put open AI models and agents to work locally on a Windows laptop, with greater control over their data and the freedom to shape AI around their own workflows.”
NVIDIA’s models and tools build on that ecosystem. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, a 74-billion-parameter model optimized for tool calling and multistep tasks, brings more capable local AI to supported RTX Spark configurations.
The NVIDIA OpenShell™ secure runtime and Microsoft Execution Containers help users control agent permissions, while NVIDIA agent skills let compatible agents work with tools including NVIDIA Broadcast, RTX Remix and Omniverse™ libraries. For example, compatible agents can adjust Broadcast effects during a stream or batch-process recorded clips, all on a local PC.
That experience extends across devices with NVIDIA PAIR, letting RTX Spark serve AI inference to compatible Windows, Linux and macOS computers on a home network while keeping other PCs free for creating and gaming.
Create, Innovate, Play
RTX Spark helps creators move from an idea to finished content wherever they work, with the ability to edit 8K 4:2:2 video and render large 3D scenes up to 90GB, even when unplugged.
With the arrival of RTX Spark, Adobe is enhancing its industry-leading creative applications, including Photoshop, Premiere and Substance 3D, with NVIDIA TensorRT acceleration in AI-editing features. In Premiere, creators can work faster across some of the most intensive parts of post-production, from playback and rendering to effects, color grading and more. Photoshop and Premiere offer native RTX Spark support through beta releases available at launch, with Substance coming soon.
“Creatives are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible across image, video, audio and 3D, and they need tools that can keep up with their ambitions,” said Deepa Subramaniam, vice president of product marketing for creative professionals at Adobe. “By combining NVIDIA’s advanced computing technology with Adobe’s industry-leading creative applications, we’re delivering enhanced experiences that empower creatives to bring their ideas to life with greater power and speed.”
For enhancing recorded content, NVIDIA Broadcast 2.3 lets creators remove background noise from existing recordings and shape their voice with Studio Voice Mic Profiles. Beta RTX Video features enable up to 4K super resolution and 4x frame generation.
In ComfyUI, new RTX Video nodes can turn 15 frames-per-second (fps) AI-generated video into smoother 60 fps footage and convert it to high dynamic range without requiring per-use cloud inference charges.
Code, Test and Deploy With One Machine
As AI shifts software development from writing code to directing agents, work often spans a laptop, a cloud AI model and a cloud virtual machine for testing.
RTX Spark brings coding, testing and prototyping onto one machine. Native CUDA support lets developers run models and agents locally, keeping locally processed code and context on their device with a path to deploy across more than 150 million NVIDIA RTX™ AI PCs and NVIDIA GPUs in the cloud. Windows Developer Config streamlines setup, while Windows Subsystem for Linux provides familiar Linux tools used in cloud development.
NVIDIA Skills, an open source GitHub repository, teaches agents to use NVIDIA CUDA-X™ tools and libraries, helping developers build NVIDIA-accelerated apps without CUDA expertise.
NVIDIA and Microsoft have readied developer tools for RTX Spark, including the first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm, the first Python build that is native by default, the first native Conda installer, support for 97% of the top 15,000 Python packages, and coding agents such as GitHub Copilot and Pi.
Game Ready With Hundreds of Games
RTX Spark brings immersive gaming to the same portable Windows PC used for creating and developing, with NVIDIA Blackwell RTX graphics enhancing image quality and accelerating performance in supported titles.
Launch support spans single-player adventure and online multiplayer games including Cyberpunk 2077, Fortnite, Gears of War: E-Day, Marvel Rivals, World of Warcraft and NBA 2K27.
NBA 2K27 showcases that immersive experience, using NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature to enhance lighting and material details for greater realism. A new 2x faster AI model, available today, boosts DLSS 5 frame rates by up to 1.4x. NVIDIA’s suite of RTX gaming technologies — DLSS, ray tracing, G-SYNC and Reflex — bring sharper visuals, smoother gameplay and greater responsiveness.
“Bringing the energy of NBA basketball to life means making every detail feel authentic,” said Peter Kavic, senior producer for visual concepts at 2K. “We worked with NVIDIA to bring ‘NBA 2K27’ to RTX Spark, using DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to deliver richer lighting and boost the visual quality of materials to deliver a jump in photorealism on a new generation of slim laptops and compact desktops.”
Availability
RTX Spark laptops are available globally today from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI through their websites and major retailers, starting at $2,599, with a limited-time promotion for new Perplexity users. Pricing and configurations vary by region.
The lineup of RTX Spark laptops includes ASUS ProArt P14 and P16, Dell XPS 16, HP OmniBook Ultra and OmniBook X 14, Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n, Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra, and MSI Prestige N16 Flip AI+ and Prestige N16.

documents.title: Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA Expand Strategic Partnership to Advance Safe Highly Automated Driving in the Next Decade
documents.raw_text:
News Summary:
	Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA will extend their partnership to jointly develop the next generation of driver assistance and automated driving systems.
	The collaboration combines Mercedes-Benz automotive engineering and MB.OS with the NVIDIA Hyperion compute and sensor architecture, Alpamayo Stack software and Halos safety system to accelerate the development of automated vehicles.
Mercedes-Benz and NVIDIA today announced that they will extend their strategic partnership to advance the next generation of automated driving systems. The collaboration brings together Mercedes-Benz’s automotive engineering and safety expertise and its MB.OS operating system with NVIDIA’s accelerated computing and AI technologies.
“NVIDIA is our most important strategic partner in automated driving. Together, we developed the first Mercedes-Benz assistance system for urban point-to-point driving for the western world,” Jörg Burzer, member of the board of management of Mercedes‑Benz Group AG and chief technology officer, development and procurement. “The expansion of our partnership marks a significant milestone and reflects the mutual trust we have built over the years. Together, we aim to bring further pioneering innovations to the road, offering our customers the best automated driving experience while upholding the high safety standards they expect from a Mercedes-Benz.”
“Accelerated computing is giving vehicles the intelligence to understand the world and reason through complex driving situations,” said Ali Kani, vice president of automotive at NVIDIA. “Mercedes-Benz brings the engineering excellence and commitment to safety this transformation demands. Together, we’re building on NVIDIA Hyperion to bring that intelligence and full-stack safety to the road and make autonomous driving an everyday reality.”
Mercedes-Benz’s MB.OS operating system supports new driving functions and over-the-air updates, working with NVIDIA Hyperion’s in-vehicle computing and sensor architecture. NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack provides full-stack driving software with AI reasoning capabilities, supporting point-to-point urban assistance, active safety and automated parking. NVIDIA Halos adds to the Mercedes-Benz safety foundation, including a parallel safety stack that adds redundancy and guardrails. Together, these technologies support advanced driver assistance and the development of future SAE-Level 4 applications, including robolimousines.
Beyond automated driving, Mercedes-Benz also relies on NVIDIA technologies for vehicle engineering simulation and within MO360, its digital production ecosystem — from virtual planning to AI-based applications. The two partners are working to further enhance efficiency, flexibility and quality across the global production network.

documents.title: Volvo Cars and NVIDIA Expand Partnership to Advance Safe Automated Driving
documents.raw_text:
Volvo Cars today announced it is expanding its partnership with NVIDIA to unlock new levels of safety in automated driving technology in future cars from Volvo, building on the companies’ decade-long collaboration.
Guided by Volvo Cars’ pioneering safety knowledge and powered by the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, the technology will enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. This includes everything from highways and busy urban streets to parking scenarios.
The technology will make its debut in a next-generation Volvo car as part of the company’s recently announced largest-ever product push.
Volvo Cars will combine its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA’s AI and accelerated computing technologies. These include the Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Halos OS, and Alpamayo Stack driving software.
Together, the companies will raise the bar for AI-enabled car safety while making driving feel easier and more effortless for customers, with a gradual introduction of eyes-off and mind-off driving.
Volvo Cars brings nearly a century of real-world safety research and its human-centric approach to this development. The ambition is to set a new benchmark for automated driving that is safe, convenient and worthy of customer trust.
“Volvo has been synonymous with car safety for almost 100 years,” said Håkan Samuelsson, president and CEO of Volvo Cars. “By working with NVIDIA, we bring together two distinct strengths: industry-leading safety knowledge and world-class AI technology. That combination gives us a unique opportunity to create safer and more attractive cars for our customers.”
“Accelerated computing has transformed the car into an intelligent machine that can understand the world around it,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Volvo has spent nearly a century protecting people on the road. Together, we’re combining Volvo’s extraordinary vehicle safety systems with NVIDIA Hyperion and Halos to build a new generation of cars that make driving safer and more effortless.”
This expanded partnership marks another milestone in the companies’ long-standing collaboration, which began in 2017. Volvo Cars is bringing the industry’s most advanced computing capabilities into its next generation of electric cars, establishing it as a leader in software-defined cars.

                    Inside Boston’s MassRobotics, founders and Intel experts gathered to solve a critical challenge: how to scale intelligent edge AI prototypes into robust, real-world robotic deployments.
      Print
      Email
      Copy Link
  Copied
        Artificial Intelligence (AI)
    Nagesh Puppala, general manager of robotics at Intel with robotic arm.
    To: Robotics Developers
From: Intel
Inside MassRobotics, the energy felt equal parts robotics lab, startup accelerator and Boston innovation hub. Founders, engineers and developers gathered for Intel’s Building Physical AI at the Edge workshop, bringing together people working across autonomous systems, industrial automation, healthcare robotics, computer vision and edge AI.
At the center of the conversation was a challenge facing robotics companies everywhere: How do you scale intelligent robots from promising prototypes into real-world deployments?
                                Read more
                                        Previous
                                        Next
    Nagesh Puppala, general manager of robotics at Intel, joined the MassRobotics community to dig into the technologies behind that transition, including real-time AI inference, sensor processing, workload consolidation, power efficiency, software portability and edge compute.
Intel’s strategy is focused on giving robotics developers an open, scalable foundation for Physical AI, bringing AI inference and real-time control together while supporting open ecosystem. The goal is to help developers build robotics systems that can perceive, reason and act in the real world, and scale those systems across industries and use cases.
But the real story at MassRobotics was the people in the room: entrepreneurs asking hard questions, engineers trading ideas and startups building what’s next.
The question is no longer simply whether Physical AI can work. It’s how we scale it.
And in Boston, there was no shortage of people ready to build the answer.

documents.title: Intel Offers Day-0 Support for Meta's Muse Spark Open
documents.raw_text:
News
                    Intel Offers Day-0 Support for Meta's Muse Spark Open
                    Data Center Silicon Built for 816B Scale
      Print
      Email
      Copy Link
  Copied
        Artificial Intelligence (AI)
    Meta’s official open-weight release of Muse Spark Open, an 816 billion-parameter any-to-text model, represents a major milestone in multimodal AI and the most capable U.S. open-weights model released to date. Deploying an 816 billion-parameter architecture requires extreme memory efficiency and hardware-level low-precision acceleration. Intel has enabled day-0 support across Intel® Xeon® processors and Intel data center GPU platforms, Intel® GPU D-series, through targeted low-bit model quantization.
Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized open-weight model. Trained specifically for agentic coding workflows, it delivers higher first-attempt accuracy, reliable tool calling and deep codebase understanding across the repositories developers use.
This open-weight model is strong in code generation, debugging and codebase understanding. The 1 million-token context window handles entire projects, including complex dependencies, legacy code and thousands of files, without requiring tasks to be broken into smaller pieces.
Muse Spark Open also supports multimodal understanding, including audio, video, image and document comprehension.
For agentic use cases, Muse Spark Open was built to plan, act, observe and self-correct over extended workflows. It is trained to browse the web, including multimodal content, use an agentic harness to spawn and coordinate subagents for decomposable work, and leverage computer-use capabilities across desktop, mobile and browser environments.
Data Center Silicon Built for 816 Billion-Parameter Scale
Large language models at the scale of Meta’s Muse Spark Open highlight the growing infrastructure demands of advanced AI workloads. At hundreds of billions of parameters, they require substantial memory capacity, efficient low-precision compute, power efficiency and architectures that can bring these capabilities into existing data center footprints.
Muse Spark Open has been tested and is running on the upcoming Intel® GPU D-series, today. This early work reflects Intel’s commitment to day-0 support for emerging AI models and gives customers an early path to begin evaluating Muse Spark Open on Intel silicon.
The image above shows Muse Spark Open inference running on four Intel® GPU D-series GPUs. Each GPU provides 160 GB of memory, offering sufficient capacity to run Muse Spark Open across four GPUs.
Intel® GPU D-series is designed for the demands of large and agentic AI models. Built on the Intel® Xe3P architecture, it features:
32 Xe3P cores256 Intel® XMX enginesDedicated hardware acceleration across a broad range of data types, including MXFP4160 GB LPDDR5x memory capacity, with options up to 480 GB
These capabilities are well aligned with large-model inference, combining low-precision compute with high memory capacity to support models such as Muse Spark Open efficiently. Its 350W air-cooled PCIe form factor also simplifies deployment. A compact four-card configuration can host an 816 billion-parameter-class model within conventional air-cooled data center racks, helping reduce infrastructure complexity for organizations evaluating frontier-scale AI.
    Muse Spark Open on Intel® Xeon® Processors
Designed for high-capacity CPU inference, Intel® Xeon® processors support INT4 weight-only quantized (WOQ) inference, reducing memory footprint while leveraging Intel® Advanced Matrix Extensions (Intel® AMX) to accelerate AI matrix operations.
Given the size of the model, Intel® Xeon® processors provide a practical path for offline inference by taking advantage of large system memory capacities, enabling organizations to run workloads privately and replicate deployments across existing Intel® Xeon® infrastructure in their data centers.
Intel is announcing day-0 support for Muse Spark Open on Xeon processors. For step-by-step instructions on running Muse Spark Open on Xeon processors with SGLang, see the SGLang cookbook. Intel is also working closely with the vLLM community to add Xeon recipes.
Software Support and Enablement
Intel’s Upstreaming First software strategy helps enterprise AI engineering teams deploy both quantized variants using standard open-source tools.
Full upstream support for compressed tensors, such as MXFP4, and GPTQ (INT4 WOQ) in mainline vLLM enables hardware-accelerated matrix execution, continuous batching and PagedAttention across multinode deployments. Native upstream integration for microscaling (MX) execution and Intel XPU-optimized kernels in SGLang drives high-throughput continuous batching and low-bit inference for complex, multiturn agentic workflows.
To maximize efficiency on Intel silicon without sacrificing accuracy, Intel quantized MXFP4 and INT4 variants directly from Muse Spark Open’s original BF16 weights using vLLM’s native quantization tool, llm-compressor, powered by the AutoRound quantization algorithm.
Intel’s AutoRound algorithm optimizes rounding and clipping-range parameters layer by layer, helping preserve Muse Spark Open’s fine-grained reasoning capabilities even at ultra-low bit widths.
The MXFP4 weights, in compressed-tensors format, target Intel® GPU D-series GPUs to use native hardware acceleration, while the INT4 weights, in GPTQ format, support Xeon processors in weight-only quantization mode to minimize memory footprint and latency.
Combining upstream support in vLLM and SGLang with hardware-tailored MXFP4 and INT4 WOQ execution gives enterprise teams the performance and agility needed to run Meta’s 816 billion-parameter Muse Spark Open on day 0.
Summary
Intel® Xeon® processors offer an alternative approach for offline inference with Meta’s Muse Spark Open 816 billion-parameter model. Additionally, the upcoming Intel data center GPU, Intel® GPU D-series, is designed for the demands of large and agentic AI models and provides 160 GB of memory per GPU. A compact four-card configuration can host Muse Spark Open within conventional air-cooled data center racks.

Aviation Capital Group orders 75 Airbus A320neo Family aircraft
  Toulouse, France, 16 October 2026 - Aviation Capital Group LLC (ACG), a premier global full-service aircraft asset manager, headquartered in Newport Beach, California has signed a firm order for 75 A320neo Family aircraft, taking its total historical order for the type to 190 aircraft.“ACG’s portfolio strategy is focused on new-technology narrowbody aircraft that are most in-demand with airlines globally. Placing the largest order in our nearly 40-year history is a statement of confidence in the long-term future of air travel and in ACG’s important role as a conduit between airlines, aircraft and capital,” said Thomas Baker, Chief Executive Officer and President of ACG. “This major investment reinforces our long-term and important partnership which dates back to 2007 when ACG placed its first order with Airbus. ACG will be able to offer its customers the A320neo Family well into the next decade,” said Benoît de Saint-Exupéry, Airbus EVP Sales of the Commercial Aircraft business. “We salute ACG’s selection of the A320neo Family - the world’s most modern and efficient single aisle aircraft.” The A320 Family is the world’s most popular single-aisle aircraft, having won more than 20,400 orders globally. The Family includes the A320neo and the A321neo, which both offer unparalleled range and performance. The Family offers at least 20% fuel savings and CO₂ reduction compared to previous generation single-aisle aircraft, while maximising passenger comfort with one of the widest single-aisle cabins in the sky.

documents.title: Shell takes final investment decision to double LNG Canada capacity
documents.raw_text:
Shell takes final investment decision to double LNG Canada capacity29 Sept 2026Calgary − Shell Canada Energy, an affiliate of Shell plc ("Shell"), today announced a final investment decision on LNG Canada Phase 2, which will double production capacity at the facility in Kitimat, British Columbia.
"LNG Canada is a core part of our Integrated Gas portfolio, helping to supply LNG to customers in Asia at a time when diversity of energy supplies and energy security are increasingly important,” said Cederic Cremers, Shell’s Integrated Gas President. “Phase 2 supports Shell’s strategic objective to be the world’s leading integrated gas and LNG business by connecting Canadian resources with Shell’s global LNG portfolio, trading capability and customer reach.”
Phase 2 will add two LNG processing units, known as trains, increasing LNG Canada’s total production capacity from 14 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) to 28 mtpa. Shell has a 40% interest in LNG Canada and will receive nearly 6 mtpa of additional LNG from the expansion. Commercial operations are expected to begin in the early 2030s.
The investment is consistent with Shell's disciplined capital allocation framework and is expected to generate double-digit returns while supporting long-term cash flow growth.
The facility in Kitimat is positioned to supply cost-competitive gas to Asian markets, where demand for LNG is expected to increase significantly. According to Shell's LNG Outlook 2026, global LNG demand is expected to rise by around 60% by 2040 and around 65% by 2050, driven by growing energy demand and the need for secure, flexible and reliable energy supplies.
Notes to editors
LNG Canada is a joint venture comprised of Shell (40%); PETRONAS (25%); PetroChina Company Limited (15%); Mitsubishi Corporation (15%); and Korea Gas Corporation (5%). The facility is operated by LNG Canada Development Inc.
LNG Canada will continue to operate under an equity lifting structure, whereby each joint venture participant is responsible for the offtake of its proportionate share of LNG production and for bringing its share of gas supply.
At Capital Markets Day 2025, Shell reaffirmed its goal to remain a leading integrated gas and LNG player through to the 2040s.
The investment in LNG Canada Phase 2 is expected to generate an internal rate of return higher than the hurdle rate for Shell’s Integrated Gas business.
The Phase 2 expansion will add two LNG processing units, known as trains, within LNG Canada's existing Kitimat facility, as well as an additional LNG storage tank, condensate tank, loading berth, and expanded utility and process systems. Coastal GasLink will expand the capacity of the existing 670-kilometre pipeline through the construction of five new compressor stations.
Liquefied natural gas (LNG)
Global demand for LNG is expected to increase from 422 mtpa in 2025 to nearly 700 mtpa by 2050, an increase of around 65%. To meet the growing demand, significant additional investment will be needed in new LNG liquefaction plants – such as LNG Canada Phase 2 – through the 2030s and 2040s.
Globally, on average, the life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions intensity of electricity produced from LNG is around 40% lower than for electricity produced from coal, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).
Shell in Canada
Shell Canada is an integrated energy company with all of Shell’s global businesses represented, including Upstream, Integrated Gas, Downstream, and Renewables and Energy Solutions. That means we do everything from exploration, gas production, refining and manufacturing, to providing fuels and developing energy solutions for our customers.

documents.title: Shell completes sale of interest in Gulf of America platform
documents.raw_text:
Shell completes sale of interest in Gulf of America platform22 Sept 2026Houston − Shell Offshore Inc., a subsidiary of Shell plc, has completed the previously announced agreement to sell its 50% non-operated working interest in the Na Kika platform and associated fields in the Gulf of America as well as its 100% owned Coulomb tieback.
Shell received approximately $840 million in cash proceeds, reflecting adjustments between the effective date of July 1, 2025, and closing. The assets were acquired by a subsidiary of Talos Energy and an affiliate of Ridgewood Energy.
The transaction supports Shell’s efforts to actively shape its portfolio to ensure a resilient and increasingly competitive Upstream business.
Notes to editors
The total consideration announced at signing was $1.7 billion, before customary adjustments and certain contingent payments.
Shell will receive uncapped upside-linked payments through 2027 and overriding royalty interests (ORRI) on production from new Na Kika tiebacks, subject to conditions.
For 2025, Shell entitlement share of production from these assets was 37,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. According to Shell’s modeling, Na Kika and Coulomb will not be meaningful contributors to production by 2030.
The deal includes buyers assuming certain decommissioning obligations and providing security with respect to such obligations.
Shell Trading US Company will retain rights to offtake from Na Kika and Coulomb through negotiated agreements with the buyers.
The Na Kika semi-submersible platform began producing in 2003. Production from the Coulomb tieback began in 2005.
BP, as operator of Na Kika, holds the remaining 50% working interest in Na Kika.
Shell proved reserves were 4.3 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) at the end of 2025 for Na Kika and 7.2 million boe at the end of 2025 for Coulomb.
Shell’s Deep Water business is differentiated by its scale, efficiency, and infrastructure. Shell is the only international oil company with a leading portfolio position in both the Gulf of America and Brazil, two of the highest-margin and lowest-carbon production basins in the world.
The US is a key market and a leading destination for Shell investment, with operations and interests in all 50 states. Shell is the leading deep-water operator and largest producer of oil and gas in the Gulf of America and one of the largest buyers of US LNG. Through our Trading & Supply network, we move US energy reliably—from power and low-carbon fuels to LNG and refined products—to customers nationwide and globally. Shell operates the largest branded fuel network in the United States, with about 12,000 Shell branded gas stations serving more than seven million customers daily. With more than 100 years in the US and more than 11,000 employees (as of January 23, 2026), Shell is delivering secure energy supplies and meeting the evolving needs of our customers today and into the future.

Pfizer Press release
            Pfizer Showcases Clinical Advancements Across Infectious Diseases at IDWeek 2026
            Wednesday, October 14, 2026 - 06:45am
          |10 min readView pdfcopyCopy to clipboardOpen in tabData from 57 abstracts will highlight Pfizer’s scientific progress targeting infectious diseases, including pneumococcal disease and RSVNEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Pfizer Inc. (NYSE: PFE) will present data from more than 50 company-sponsored, investigator-sponsored and collaborative research abstracts across its infectious disease pipeline and portfolio at the upcoming IDWeek 2026 congress, held in Washington, D.C., from October 21-24, 2026. Data across 12 oral presentations will showcase the Company’s advancements in the prevention and treatment of infectious diseases.“At Pfizer, we address some of the most urgent challenges in infectious diseases, delivering vaccines and anti-infective therapies that protect and treat people today while pursuing innovations to expand their impact in the future. Our data at IDWeek 2026 reflects this commitment, with real-world and clinical data across our portfolio as well as important clinical milestones for our next-generation pediatric pneumococcal vaccine candidate and registrational Lyme vaccine candidate. Through these efforts, we are translating scientific advancements into meaningful benefits for communities around the world.”— Annaliesa Anderson, Ph.D., Senior Vice President and Chief Vaccines Officer, PfizerKey Highlights of Pfizer’s Presence at IDWeek 2026Advancing Next-Generation Vaccines Across Infectious DiseasesLate-breaking presentation of immunogenicity, safety, and tolerability data from a Phase 2 study comparing Pfizer’s 25-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine candidate (PF-07872412; 25vPnC) with PREVNAR 20 ®(Pneumococcal 20-valent Conjugate Vaccine) in healthy infants. Topline results from this study were announced in May 2026. These data support the potential of this next-generation vaccine candidate to broaden pneumococcal coverage while informing its ongoing pediatric Phase 3 program. (Presentation Title: Immunogenicity of a 25-valent pneumococcal coverage vaccine compared with PCV20 in healthy infants: Evaluating a candidate to improve pneumococcal coverage in a Phase 2 trial)Safety and immunogenicity data from a Phase 3 study evaluating a single 10-µg dose of Pfizer and BioNTech’s 2025-2026 formula of COMIRNATY ®(COVID-19 Vaccine, mRNA), targeting the LP.8.1 variant of SARS-CoV-2, in children 5-11 years of age at increased risk of severe COVID-19 due to underlying medical conditions. These results further support the safety and robust immunogenicity of the LP.8.1-adapted vaccine in at-risk children. (Presentation Title: Safety and immunogenicity of LP.8.1-adapted BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccine in children 5–11 years of age)Phase 3 results from the VALOR study of PF-07307405 (LB6V) evaluating the efficacy and safety of LB6V, Pfizer and Valneva’s 6-valent OspA-based Lyme disease vaccine candidate, in healthy participants 5 years of age and older living in Lyme disease-endemic regions of North America and Europe. These results build upon the topline readout announced in March 2026; additionally, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) has started the review of the Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) as announced in August 2026. These findings support the potential to provide clinically meaningful antibody-associated protection of LB6V against Lyme disease. (Presentation Title: Efficacy and safety of the LB6V Lyme disease vaccine candidate: Results from a Phase 3 study in participants ≥5 years of age)Expanding Evidence of Vaccine Impact in PracticeReal-world retrospective cohort study evaluating the effectiveness of ABRYSVO ® (Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine) vaccination against laboratory-confirmed RSV infection among Veteran Affairs nursing home residents across three RSV seasons. These results are the first available third-season data for this population and further support RSV vaccination in high-risk older adults while providing important insights into sustained vaccine effectiveness. (Presentation Title: First available vaccine effectiveness of bivalent RSVpreF against laboratory-confirmed RSV infection in nursing home residents through 3 seasons after vaccination — 2025-2026)Multicenter STREETON study evaluating the real-world effectiveness of maternal ABRYSVO vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age and younger, following the implementation of a national immunization program in Australia. These findings, which are also published in JAMA Pediatrics, support maternal ABRYSVO vaccination and demonstrate protection across infant age groups, disease severity, maternal vaccination characteristics, and RSV subtypes. (Presentation Title: Maternal RSVpreF vaccine effectiveness against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalized infants by age, vaccination characteristics, and RSV subtype: A multicenter test-negative design study in Australia, 2025-2026 (STREETON Study))Retrospective cohort analysis evaluating the effectiveness of PREVNAR 20 against all-invasive pneumococcal disease (all-IPD) due to any serotype and all-cause pneumonia (ACP) among U.S. adults 65 years of age and older, regardless of prior pneumococcal vaccination history. By demonstrating reductions in all-IPD and ACP, these real-world results underscore the substantial public health impact of PREVNAR 20 when implemented in routine vaccination practice for older adults. (Presentation Title: 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine: Impact and effectiveness against all-cause outcomes among the general population of US older adults by age group, regardless of prior pneumococcal vaccine history)Modeling study evaluating long-term immunogenicity following a two-dose series of PENBRAYA ®(Meningococcal Groups A, B, C, W, and Y Vaccine), administered to adolescents at extended intervals. These findings indicate that antibodies against meningococcal strain B (MenB) may persist for up to five years, and could offer prolonged protection for higher-risk adolescents alongside a streamlined vaccination schedule that can potentially improve uptake versus current three- or four-dose recommendations. (Presentation Title: Long-term seroprotection following two-dose MenABCWY: Modeling supports benefits of extended dosing intervals)IDWeek Presence Reinforces Pfizer’s Commitment to Addressing the Threat of Infectious DiseasesAs infectious diseases remain a persistent cause of illness and death worldwide, Pfizer is focused on generating the evidence needed to bring effective vaccines and anti-infective therapies to as many people as possible. Our data at IDWeek reflect that strategy, concentrating innovation in disease areas with the greatest opportunity to impact public health globally, whether through large at-risk populations, the potential for longer-lasting protection, or both. Highlights include emerging data from late-stage investigational programs advancing next-generation vaccines, new analyses supporting established vaccines as standards of care, real-world evidence that deepens understanding of vaccine effectiveness across diverse populations, and several studies surrounding our current and investigational COVID-19 anti-infective therapies.Detailed Presentation InformationInformation on oral presentations led by Pfizer and its collaborators can be found in the table below.
